title: Heart Failure Phenotyping and Prognosis by CMR-Derived Oxygen Delivery and Extraction.
abstract: Background Heart failure reflects impaired matching of systemic oxygen delivery to metabolic demand, yet resting oxygen transport is seldom measured. Objectives The purpose of this study was to noninvasively derive resting oxygen delivery and extraction using cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) and relate these to clinical characteristics and outcomes. Methods In this retrospective study, in patients with heart failure referred for clinical CMR, cardiac output was assessed by cine imaging; basal blood-pool T2 mapping provided imaging-derived venous oxygen saturation; and measured hemoglobin enabled calculation of arterial oxygen content. Arterial oxygen saturation was fixed at 96%. We derived indexed systemic oxygen delivery (DO 2 i), oxygen extraction fraction (OEF), and indexed systemic oxygen consumption (VO 2 i). The endpoint was all-cause death or heart failure hospitalization. Results A total of 429 patients were included (62 events). VO 2 i varied widely (tertile means 138.8, 207.9, and 293.8 mL/min/m 2 ), while left ventricular ejection fraction did not differ (38.8%, 40.6%, and 40.3%; P = 0.42). Imaging-derived venous oxygen saturation decreased across increasing VO 2 i tertiles (61.5%, 54.3%, and 50.7%; P < 0.0001). In Cox regression adjusted for age, sex, ejection fraction, and late gadolinium enhancement, VO 2 i was associated with the endpoint (HR: 1.15 per 50 mL/min/m 2 , 95% CI: 1.00-1.32; P = 0.046), but discrimination of VO 2 i alone was poor (Harrell's C = 0.53). Delivery-extraction phenotypes differed in event risk (log-rank P = 0.026): event proportions were 8.6% (high DO 2 i/low OEF), 14.0% (low DO 2 i/low OEF), 16.8% (high DO 2 i/high OEF), and 18.3% (low DO 2 i/high OEF). The delivery-extraction phenotype remained associated with outcome after adjustment for age, sex, left ventricular ejection fraction, and CMR-derived filling pressure. Conclusions In this hypothesis-generating study, CMR-based oxygen supply-demand assessment delineates resting delivery-extraction phenotypes associated with heart failure outcomes.

title: Management of Coronary Calcified Nodules: A Position Statement.
abstract: Coronary calcified nodules are an uncommon but important substrate for acute coronary syndromes, stent underexpansion, and recurrent target lesion revascularization. This consensus integrates pathologic, imaging, prognostic, and interventional evidence to guide practical decision-making. Intravascular imaging is essential for diagnosis, mechanism definition, and procedural optimization. Optical coherence tomography provides superior assessment of cap disruption and thrombus, whereas intravascular ultrasound remains valuable when contrast exposure or lesion crossing limits optical coherence tomography. Treatment should be tailored to lesion crossability, calcium distribution, and the need for mechanical scaffolding. No calcium-modification device or drug-eluting stent vs drug-coated balloon strategy has demonstrated consistent superiority. The proposed type IIa/IIb framework is hypothesis-generating and requires prospective validation. Calcified nodule-related target lesion failure should be managed by correcting the dominant mechanical mechanism before antiproliferative therapy. These recommendations emphasize individualized, imaging-guided percutaneous coronary intervention and identify priorities for prospective comparative research.

title: Transcatheter Solution to Atypical Anomalous Pulmonary Venous Drainage in a Single Ventricle Patient.
abstract: Background Partial anomalous pulmonary venous drainage (PAPVD) is typically incompatible with single ventricle physiology if left unrepaired before cavopulmonary connection. This report describes a rare anatomical variant and novel interventional solution. Case summary An 8-month-old female with hypoplastic left heart variant developed profound cyanosis following bidirectional Glenn because of unrepaired PAPVD of the right upper pulmonary vein to the superior vena cava (SVC). Retrospective 3-dimensional reconstruction of the patient's neonatal computed tomography angiogram revealed a small interlobar vessel between the anomalous pulmonary vein and the anatomically normal right lower pulmonary vein. This interlobar vessel's gross dilatation and anatomical features permitted percutaneous device occlusion of the PAPVD connection to the SVC, isolating SVC return to the cavopulmonary circulation while preserving unobstructed pulmonary venous return to the atrium. Discussion Surgical and interventional solutions are reviewed in the context of this unusual anatomical variant. Take-home messages In the uncommon circumstance of an unrecognized anomalous pulmonary vein with connections to both systemic and pulmonary venous circulations, consideration may be given to interventional occlusion of the PAPVD connection to the systemic vein. Retrospective application of contemporary 3-dimensional reconstruction tools can add great value in delineating complex or unusual anatomy.

title: Sarcomatoid Renal Cell Carcinoma With Cardiac Metastasis Causing Right Ventricular Outflow Tract Obstruction.
abstract: Background Renal cell carcinoma (RCC) rarely metastasizes to the heart, and an aggressive histologic transformation known as sarcomatoid dedifferentiation confers a poor prognosis. Case summary A patient presented with progressive exertional dyspnea. Initial laboratory studies revealed elevated troponin and elevated D-dimer. Computed tomography pulmonary angiography showed a right ventricle (RV) filling defect. Cardiac magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated a large lobulated mass extending from the RV free wall into the outflow tract, encroaching on the pulmonic valve with an ejection fraction of <20%. Abdominal magnetic resonance imaging revealed a right renal mass. The patient suffered a fatal arrest because of obstructive shock from severe RV outflow tract obstruction. Discussion Postmortem examination confirmed metastatic sarcomatoid RCC. Patients typically present with advanced disease, and survival is <1 year. Combination immunotherapy is approved for metastatic RCC. Initiating immunotherapy would not have addressed the patient's acute hemodynamic compromise. Take-home message Early recognition of metastatic RCC is crucial for potential therapeutic intervention, though prognosis remains poor in advanced cases.

title: True Left-Ventricular Aneurysm After Ventricular Tachycardia Ablation: The Role of Imaging in a Rare Complication.
abstract: Background Left ventricular (LV) pseudoaneurysm is an uncommon but recognized complication of ventricular tachycardia (VT) ablation. In contrast, true LV aneurysm has been reported only rarely. Case summary Transthoracic echocardiogram, supported by cardiovascular magnetic resonance imaging, initially suggested an LV pseudoaneurysm in a patient after VT ablation. During evaluation for percutaneous closure, left ventriculogram and 3-dimensional transesophageal echocardiogram revealed more complex anatomy, prompting referral for surgical repair. Intraoperative findings confirmed a true LV aneurysm. Discussion True LV aneurysm may represent a rare complication of deep radiofrequency energy delivery during catheter ablation resulting in myocardial injury. Because differentiating true aneurysms from pseudoaneurysms can be challenging, a multimodality imaging approach may improve anatomical characterization, guide management, and enhance understanding of the underlying mechanism. Take-home message Multimodality imaging can improve anatomical characterization and procedural planning in patients with the rare complication of true left aneurysm after catheter ablation.

title: Antegrade Dissection and Re-Entry for Recanalization of Traumatic Coronary Artery Dissection.
abstract: Background Traumatic coronary artery dissection (TCAD) is a rare catastrophic complication of blunt chest trauma, often masked by concomitant injuries, posing diagnostic and therapeutic challenges. Case summary A 20-year-old man with polytrauma after a motorcycle accident developed cardiogenic shock. Coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) suggested occlusive left anterior descending dissection, confirmed by delayed angiography under extracorporeal membrane oxygenation support. Stingray-based antegrade dissection and re-entry (ADR) with cutting balloon fenestration and drug-coated balloon angioplasty achieved TIMI flow grade 3. Three-month follow-up showed favorable left anterior descending healing and improved cardiac function. Discussion CCTA enables early TCAD diagnosis. ADR facilitates guidewire passage, and a stentless strategy is preferable in young polytrauma patients at high bleeding risk. Take-home messages Maintain suspicion for TCAD after blunt chest trauma, especially with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction features. CCTA aids early diagnosis; ADR-based percutaneous coronary intervention with drug-coated balloon is safe and effective.

title: "Whiplash Motion" in Cardiac Intimal Sarcoma With Functional Mitral Stenosis and Dynamic LVOT Obstruction.
abstract: Background Cardiac intimal sarcoma (CIS) usually presents as an isolated left atrial mass; pan-left-heart involvement producing simultaneous inflow and outflow obstruction is rare. Case summary A 43-year-old man presented in acute heart failure (B-type natriuretic peptide 948.8 pg/mL; right ventricular systolic pressure 59 mm Hg). Imaging showed a tumor in the left atrium and ventricle: an atrial mass infiltrated the mitral leaflet, causing functional mitral stenosis, whereas a mobile papillary-muscle component showed a "whiplash motion," prolapsing into the left ventricular outflow tract and protruding through the aortic valve in systole. Emergency debulking and mechanical mitral valve replacement followed; histopathology confirmed CIS (mouse double minute 2 homolog/cyclin-dependent kinase 4 positive, mouse double minute 2 homolog-amplified). Although adjuvant carbon-ion radiotherapy provided temporary control, the patient died 20 months later. Discussion We propose the "whiplash motion" sign and highlight the trade-off between mechanical-valve durability and bleeding risk during thoracic radiotherapy. Take-home message CIS can cause dual left-heart obstruction through multicomponent tumor dynamics; prosthetic valve choice should anticipate multimodality oncologic management.

title: Concomitant Wire-Loop Repositioning and Transapical Valve Replacement for a Migrated Sutureless Aortic Valve.
abstract: Background Sutureless aortic prosthesis migration is rare but potentially catastrophic. Case summary A 78-year-old woman on hemodialysis underwent minimally invasive double valve replacement using a sutureless aortic bioprosthesis. Failure to wean from cardiopulmonary bypass prompted intraoperative angiography, which raised suspicion of cranial migration of the aortic prosthesis, with bilateral coronary hypoperfusion; subsequent computed tomography confirmed the diagnosis. Because repositioning after surgical excision of the native leaflets would cause severe aortic regurgitation, a transapical transcatheter valve was prepositioned before transfemoral wire-loop repositioning. Coronary flow was restored, the failed valve was replaced, and 5-month follow-up showed preserved ventricular function and stable frame position. Discussion Prepositioning a transapical transcatheter valve before wire-loop repositioning enabled immediate valve replacement while minimizing the empty-annulus interval. Take-home message Failed passage of a Perceval sizer should preclude sutureless implantation; prepositioned transapical valve replacement with wire-loop repositioning is a viable bailout.

title: Miniaturizing Slipstream and Tip Detection to a 7-F Transradial System for Chronic Total Occlusion PCI.
abstract: Objective To demonstrate that the combination of the slipstream and tip detection can be miniaturized to a 7-F radial system using the SIDEPASS short-monorail dual-lumen catheter and AnteOwl intravascular ultrasound (IVUS) for a chronic total occlusion (CTO) lesion. Key steps Treat the in-stent restenosis in left circumflex artery #14 and insert the AnteOwl IVUS over the same wire (first-wire lumen only) to delineate the spatial relationship between the stent struts and the jailed ostium of left circumflex artery #15 CTO. Advance the SIDEPASS short-monorail dual-lumen catheter over the same wire within a 7-F guiding catheter, pass a second guidewire through an optimal stent-strut cell into the CTO, and complete lesion preparation. Potential pitfalls Narrow clearance within a 7-F guide, first-wire instability when removing the dual-lumen catheter, and inaccurate ostium identification can hinder the procedure. Take-home messages Miniaturizing slipstream and tip detection to a 7-F system provides a smaller radial access footprint for complex CTO percutaneous coronary intervention while preserving advanced IVUS-guided wiring.

title: Left Ventricular Hemangioma: Multimodal Imaging, TEE-Guided Resection, and Short-Term Follow-Up.
abstract: Background Cardiac hemangioma is a rare benign vascular tumor, with left ventricular involvement being particularly uncommon. Most patients are asymptomatic, making preoperative diagnosis challenging and optimal management controversial. Case summary We report a 72-year-old asymptomatic woman with a 2.3-cm left ventricular hemangioma, suspected on multimodal imaging (transthoracic echocardiography, contrast echocardiography, coronary computed tomography angiography, and cardiac magnetic resonance). The tumor was completely resected under intraoperative transesophageal echocardiography guidance and confirmed as a cavernous hemangioma on pathology. Short-term follow-up showed favorable recovery. Conclusions This case highlights the complementary role of multimodal imaging in differentiating hypervascular tumors from thrombus, and the value of intraoperative transesophageal echocardiography in guiding safe and complete resection. Take-home messages Left ventricular contrast echocardiography and cardiac magnetic resonance are complementary imaging modalities for differentiating hypervascular tumors from thrombus in patients with asymptomatic left ventricular masses. Complete surgical resection should be considered for surgically accessible left ventricular hemangiomas regardless of symptoms, given the potential risk of thromboembolism associated with hypervascular tumors in the left ventricle.

title: Long-Term Prognostic Value of Scar Characteristics in Cardiac Magnetic Resonance to Predict Appropriate Therapies in Primary Prevention.
abstract: Background Cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) with late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) provides unique insights into ventricular arrhythmogenic substrate, although few studies have analyzed its long-term value in patients with implantable cardioverter-defibrillators (ICDs) for primary prevention. Objectives The aim of this study was to evaluate the role of LGE characteristics in stratifying arrhythmogenic risk in patients with ICD implantation for primary prevention over long-term follow-up. Methods This was a prospective study, between 2011 and 2017, in which 226 patients who underwent LGE CMR before ICD implantation for primary prevention were consecutively enrolled. Dedicated software (ADAS 3D) was used to quantify LGE, border zone, core, and conducting channels (CCs). Results The median age was 62.9 years (Q1-Q3: 55.4-68.5 years), with 52% of participants (n = 104) with ischemic cardiomyopathy and a median MADIT (Multicenter Automatic Defibrillator Implantation Trial) score of 54 (Q1-Q3: 42-64). After a median follow-up period of 8.1 years (Q1-Q3: 6.2-10 years), 59 patients (29.5%) reached the primary endpoint (appropriate ICD therapy). LGE mass >10 g (HR: 3.58; 95% CI: 1.29-9.93; P = 0.014), CCs (HR: 3.42; 95% CI: 1.69-6.96; P = 0.009), and the presence of both LGE mass >10 g and CCs (34.92% vs 5.55%; HR: 4.65; 95% CI: 1.46-14.8; P = 0.009) were strongly associated with the primary endpoint. Patients without CCs and with LGE mass < 10 g had a very low rate of appropriate therapies (negative predictive value = 92%). LGE parameters remained independently associated with the primary endpoint after adjustment for MADIT score. Conclusions The characteristics of potential arrhythmia substrate assessed using LGE CMR are potent predictors of ventricular arrhythmias after ICD implantation for the primary prevention of sudden death.

title: Association of Left Ventricular Epicardial Adipose Tissue and Lipomatous Metaplasia With Ventricular Tachycardia Circuitry and Recurrence Following Ablation in Patients With Non-Ischemic Cardiomyopathy.
abstract: Background Patients with nonischemic cardiomyopathy (NICM) have complex intramural ventricular tachycardia (VT) circuitry and relatively high postablation recurrences. Objectives This study evaluated the association of left ventricular epicardial adipose tissue (LV EAT) and lipomatous metaplasia (LM) with critical VT circuitry and postablation VT recurrence in patients with NICM. Methods In this retrospective study, we quantified LV EAT and LM via cardiac contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CECT) in a cohort of consecutive patients with NICM before VT ablation. CECT image registration with VT critical sites in electroanatomic mapping was performed in a subset. Mixed-effects and subdistribution proportional hazard models were used to examine the association of image features with VT circuitry elements and outcomes, respectively. Results In 48 patients with coregistered CECT-electroanatomic mapping, segmental maximal EAT thickness was associated with critical VT sites (OR: 1.36 per mm increase; P < 0.001), and a threshold of >4.7 mm EAT achieved 72% sensitivity and 71% specificity (OR: 2.15; P = 0.006) for VT site identification. This association remained significant after adjusting for LM, with a significant EAT-LM interaction (P = 0.027). Among all 119 patients, 52 experienced VT recurrence during a median follow-up of 1.7 years (Q1-Q3: 0.7-4.0). Lower LV EAT attenuation was independently associated with time to VT recurrence (subdistribution HR: 1.04 per 1 HU decrease; P = 0.012) after multivariable adjustment including LM and a significant LM interaction (P = 0.020). Conclusions LV EAT density and thickness are associated with VT circuitry and postablation recurrence in patients with NICM, and demonstrate a significant statistical interaction with LM.

title: Natural History, Pathogenesis, and Early Detection of Asplenia in Autoimmune Polyendocrinopathy-Candidiasis-Ectodermal Dystrophy.
abstract: Background Autoimmune polyendocrinopathy-candidiasis-ectodermal dystrophy (APECED) is characterized by interferon-γ (IFN-γ)-mediated immune dysregulation. Although asplenia has been reported in APECED, its prevalence, pathogenesis, and optimal strategies for early detection remain incompletely characterized. Objective To define the natural history of asplenia in APECED, elucidate its immunopathogenesis, and identify clinical correlates that may enable earlier recognition. Methods We evaluated two large APECED cohorts (n=170) for prevalence, timing, and clinical features of asplenia. Longitudinal imaging, peripheral blood smears (PBS), and hematologic parameters were analyzed. Mechanistic studies were performed in AIRE-deficient mice. Functional splenic imaging with liver-spleen 99m Tc-sulfur colloid single-photon emission computed tomography (SC-SPECT/CT) was performed in selected patients. Results Asplenia was identified in 17-20% of patients across both cohorts with onset from childhood to adulthood, a cumulative risk approaching ∼40% by age 40, and enrichment among patients with severe multiorgan disease. Longitudinal imaging demonstrated progressive decline in splenic volume over years. PBS abnormalities appeared late, whereas SC-SPECT/CT imaging revealed markedly impaired splenic function earlier. In AIRE-deficient mice, splenic destruction developed in an age-dependent manner, was associated with increased IFN-γ activity, and was prevented by Ifng ablation. Persistent leukocytosis and/or thrombocytosis were present in 93.8% of patients with asplenia and frequently preceded diagnosis by months to years, whereas such abnormalities were uncommon and transient in patients without asplenia. Conclusions Asplenia is a common, acquired, IFN-γ-dependent manifestation of APECED characterized by a prolonged subclinical phase. PBS examination is insensitive for early detection. Persistent leukocytosis and/or thrombocytosis may serve as accessible clinical correlates for early recognition.

In AIRE-deficient mice, splenic destruction developed in an age-dependent manner, was associated with increased IFN-γ activity, and was prevented by Ifng ablation. Persistent leukocytosis and/or thrombocytosis were present in 93.8% of patients with asplenia and frequently preceded diagnosis by months to years, whereas such abnormalities were uncommon and transient in patients without asplenia.

Conclusions

Asplenia is a common, acquired, IFN-γ-dependent manifestation of APECED characterized by a prolonged subclinical phase. PBS examination is insensitive for early detection. Persistent leukocytosis and/or thrombocytosis may serve as accessible clinical correlates for early recognition.

title: Development of an Electronic Clinical Quality Measure for Excessive Radiation Dose or Inadequate Image Quality in Diagnostic CT in Adults.
abstract: The Excessive Radiation Dose or Inadequate Image Quality for Diagnostic CT in Adults (ExRad) measure is the first automated radiology outcome measure adopted by CMS. We describe its development, specification, calculation, and adoption. Beginning in 2018, the measure was developed under a CMS cooperative agreement following the Measures Management System Blueprint, with oversight from a multidisciplinary Technical Expert Panel. ExRad evaluates each adult diagnostic CT examination in three steps. First, the examination is assigned to 1 of 19 CT categories defined by anatomic region and clinical indication using International Classification of Diseases, 10th Revision, Clinical Modification and Current Procedural Terminology codes. Second, size-adjusted radiation dose and image noise are computed from the DICOM dose report and pixel data; because clinical and radiology data reside in separate systems, translation software inside the hospital firewall performs the linkage and calculations automatically. Third, dose and noise are compared with category-specific thresholds derived from a reader study in which 125 radiologists rated the image quality of 734 CT examinations. An examination is out of range if either value exceeds its threshold, and the measure score is the percentage of eligible examinations that are out of range. Testing across 32 facilities in eight health systems confirmed the availability, accuracy, validity, and reproducibility of all data elements, and the National Quality Forum endorsed the measure in 2021. CMS adopted ExRad in 2023 into hospital inpatient, hospital outpatient, and clinician quality reporting programs, with voluntary reporting beginning in 2025. It is the sole outcome measure in the Diagnostic Radiology MIPS (Merit-Based Incentive Payment System) Value Pathway.

title: Standalone commercial artificial intelligence software for pulmonary nodule detection on chest radiographs: a systematic review.
abstract: Background Pulmonary nodules may be missed on chest radiographs despite their clinical relevance for early lung cancer detection. Commercial artificial intelligence (AI) systems are increasingly available for chest radiograph interpretation, but evidence for their standalone performance remains fragmented across products, datasets, operating thresholds, and comparator designs. Purpose To systematically evaluate the standalone diagnostic performance of commercially available AI software for pulmonary nodule detection on chest radiographs compared with radiologists reading alone, and to identify methodological factors shaping interpretation of the evidence. Methods A systematic review was conducted according to PRISMA 2020 guidelines and registered with PROSPERO (CRD420261383905). PubMed, PubMed Central, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched. Eligible studies evaluated commercially available AI systems as standalone detectors for pulmonary nodules on chest radiographs and directly compared their performance with radiologists reading alone using an accepted clinical reference standard. Risk of bias was assessed using an adapted QUADAS-2 framework. Findings were synthesized narratively because of heterogeneity in study design, populations, reference standards, operating thresholds, and outcome measures. Results Six studies met the inclusion criteria, comprising 12 product-level evaluations across 10 commercial AI systems. Standalone AI performance varied: some evaluations showed AI exceeding radiologist-level performance, others showed no significant difference, and one showed AI below individual reader performance with approximately twice the false-positive rate. In the only standardized within-study comparison of multiple commercial products on the same dataset, four of seven systems significantly exceeded mean radiologist AUC. Standalone AI AUC ranged from 0.79 to 0.93 against a mean reader AUC of 0.81 (95% CI 0.77-0.85), indicating that performance varied among cleared products even when tested under identical conditions. Interpretation was limited by differences in operating thresholds, comparator design, reference standards, study populations, and outcome reporting. Risk-of-bias concerns were common, particularly in patient selection. Conclusions In the available peer-reviewed evidence, standalone commercial AI systems for chest radiograph pulmonary nodule detection show variable performance. Evidence remains insufficient to support class-wide standalone deployment because all studies were retrospective or reader-study based, thresholds were inconsistently reported, and real-world false-positive burden remains uncertain. Prospective real world evaluation with clearly reported operating thresholds, standardized comparator designs and complete diagnostic performance are needed.

title: Comparing 70 kV and 120 kV photon-counting CT protocols for pediatric cardiac imaging in children weighing 10-30 kg: Radiation dose and image quality.
abstract: Background Scanning at 70 kV on photon-counting CT (PCCT) reduces radiation dose by 50% compared to 120 kV in infants under 10 kg without loss of diagnostic quality. Whether scanning at a lower kV is of benefit in larger children, in whom greater attenuation increases image noise, has not been determined. Methods We retrospectively compared ultra-high-pitch cardiac PCCT examinations in children weighing 10-30 kg acquired at 70 kV (n = 79) or 120 kV (n = 80), both at a CARE keV IQ level of 25. We measured signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) and contrast-to-noise ratio (CNR) in the ascending aorta and main pulmonary artery and compared radiation dose. Two pediatric cardiac radiologists rated image quality in five vascular structures on a 5-point Likert scale. Results Groups were similar in age and size. Neither CNR nor SNR differed significantly. Median Likert scores were at least 4 for four of five structures in both groups. Median CTDI vol was 0.49 vs 0.63 mGy (P < 0.001), and effective dose 0.65 vs 0.75 mSv (P < 0.001) for 70 vs 120 kV. Conclusion In children weighing 10-30 kg, 70 kV ultra-high-pitch cardiac PCCT was associated with lower radiation dose than 120 kV, with no significant difference in CNR and median reader scores in the diagnostic range. A 120 kV protocol remains appropriate when metal-artifact reduction or advanced spectral reconstructions are needed.

title: CT-Based Deep Learning Assessment of Aortic Valve Fibrosis and Calcification: Development and Multicenter External Validation Against Experts, Histology, and Outcomes.
abstract: Background Computed tomography angiography (CTA) enables assessment of aortic valve tissue composition, providing insights into disease progression and helping predict outcomes in patients undergoing transcatheter aortic valve replacement for severe aortic stenosis (AS). The authors aimed to develop a deep learning system for CTA-based quantification of aortic fibrotic and calcific tissue, validate its agreement with expert manual analysis and histopathology, and evaluate its value for outcome prediction. Methods This international, multicenter study included 1,674 patients who underwent CTA at 9 sites. A deep learning model based on the nnU-Net architecture was trained in 468 patients and applied to an external test set of 1,206 patients, including 29 with valve histology and 12 with serial CTA. In 1,165 patients with clinical outcomes, prognostic value was assessed adjusting for clinical, echocardiographic, and procedural covariates. Results Deep learning-enabled tissue composition analysis was rapid (1.35 ± 0.4 min vs 7.2 ± 1.2 min for experts) with excellent agreement vs expert assessment (r = 0.915; intraclass correlation coefficient [ICC] = 0.913), histology (r = 0.909; ICC = 0.905), and scan-rescan reproducibility (r = 0.999; ICC = 0.999). In the external cohort, 469 patients (40%) died over 4.1 ± 1.1 years of follow-up. Fibrotic tissue volume (adjusted HR [aHR] 1.42 per IQR increase; P < 0.001), calcific tissue attenuation (aHR 1.02 per 25 HU increase; P = 0.005), left ventricular ejection fraction (aHR 1.10 per 5% decrease; P < 0.001), life-threatening bleeding (aHR: 1.96; P = 0.003), major vascular complication (aHR: 1.51; P = 0.042) and postprocedural peak pressure gradient (aHR 1.03 per 1 mm Hg increase; P < 0.001) independently predicted mortality. Patients in the highest tertile of fibrotic tissue volume (>0.940 cm 3 ) had a 2-fold higher risk of death (aHR: 2.0; P < 0.001), whereas patients with dense calcific tissue attenuation (>885 HU) had a 1.5-fold higher risk of death. Conclusions Deep learning enables rapid quantification of aortic valve fibrotic and calcific tissue from CTA, demonstrating excellent agreement with both expert CTA and histological assessments. Quantitative analysis of aortic tissue composition provides additional prognostic value for all-cause mortality after transcatheter aortic valve replacement in multicenter external evaluation.

title: Clinical and functional outcomes following transoral endoscopically-assisted treatment of mandibular subcondylar fractures: A single-center experience.
abstract: Purpose Evidence on the outcomes of transoral endoscopically-assisted treatment of mandibular subcondylar fractures remains limited. The primary aim of this study was to evaluate surgical outcomes, complication rates, revision rates, and long-term functional results following transoral endoscopically-assisted treatment of subcondylar fractures. The secondary aim was to identify predictors of postoperative complications, revision surgery, and craniomandibular dysfunction. Methods This monocentric observational study comprised a retrospective and a prospective study arm. The retrospective cohort included all patients with mandibular subcondylar fractures treated by transoral endoscopically-assisted open reduction and internal fixation without transbuccal trocars between December 2014 and August 2024. Fractures were classified using the AO CMF and Spiessl-Schroll Classification Systems based on preoperative CT imaging. Demographic, clinical, radiographic, surgical, and postoperative data were collected. The prospective cohort consisted of patients who underwent standardized clinical follow-up at least 12 months after surgery, including assessment of temporomandibular disorders, mandibular function, occlusion, pain, and maximum mouth opening using standardized DGFDT examination protocols. Primary outcomes were postoperative complications and revision surgery; long-term functional outcome was evaluated as a tertiary endpoint. Descriptive statistics, exploratory bivariate analyses, and multivariable logistic regression were performed to identify factors associated with postoperative complications. Results A total of 132 patients with 144 subcondylar fractures were included. Postoperative complications occurred in 43.8 % of fractures, whereas intraoperative revision following 3D C-arm imaging and postoperative revision surgery were required in 15.3 % and 2.8 % of cases, respectively. The most common complications were malocclusion (20.1 %), osteosynthesis material failure (15.3 %), and wound infection (14.6 %). Multivariable analysis identified longer intermaxillary fixation as the only independent predictor of postoperative complications (OR 1.052, 95 % CI 1.008-1.109; p = 0.036). Follow-up examinations demonstrated generally favorable long-term functional outcomes, although 22.7 % of patients showed signs of temporomandibular disorders and 31.8 % presented with objective occlusal disturbances. Conclusions Transoral Endoscopically-assisted open reduction and internal fixation provided reliable surgical management of subcondylar mandibular fractures, with a low revision rate and favorable long-term functional outcomes. Prolonged postoperative intermaxillary fixation was the only independent predictor of postoperative complications, while routine intraoperative 3D imaging supported accurate fracture reduction and implant positioning.

title: Evaluation of the accuracy of zygomaticomaxillary complex fracture reduction and fixation using a fully digital workflow versus conventional protocol: a randomized clinical trial.
abstract: The zygomatic bone has multiple points of articulation with the craniofacial skeleton, and accurate intraoperative reduction in various planes is very challenging and entirely dependent on the operator's subjective evaluation. This study aimed to investigate the efficiency of a novel fully digital protocol versus the conventional management strategy for zygomaticomaxillary complex fracture reduction and fixation. Twenty-eight patients with acute zygomatic fractures who met the inclusion criteria were recruited; each group of 14 patients was randomly assigned. The intervention group received a fully digital protocol, represented by customized predictive-hole surgical guides and patient-specific fixation plates, while the control group was managed conventionally. Accuracy of bone reduction was the primary outcome. The results showed that, when comparing the virtual reduction of both groups with the postoperative CT scans, the overall accuracy was markedly higher in the digital group (0.290 ± 0.132 mm) than in the conventional group (1.290 ± 0.525 mm), with a mean difference of -1.000 mm (95% CI -1.309 to -0.691; p < 0.001) and a very large effect size (d = -2.612). Clinically, the digital group showed higher patient satisfaction with aesthetics and a shorter operation duration, while no difference in infraorbital nerve numbness was observed between the two groups. Based on the statistical and clinical findings of this study, a fully digital workflow provided a valuable approach for the management of zygomaticomaxillary complex fractures, optimizing aesthetic and functional rehabilitation.

title: Engineering long-circulating deferoxamine targeting the innate immunity of neutrophil ferroptosis for systemic lupus erythematosus treatment.
abstract: Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) is characterized by dysregulation of both innate and adaptive immunity, in which ferroptosis-mediated neutrophil death has been implicated in disease progression. However, the clinical application of ferroptosis inhibitors remains limited by rapid systemic clearance and poor pharmacokinetic profiles. Here, we report a full positron emission tomography (PET)-guided strategy for pharmacokinetic engineering of ferroptosis inhibitors through albumin hitchhiking. By incorporating an albumin-binding motif into deferoxamine (DFO), we developed a series of albumin-hitchhiking conjugates and employed in vivo PET imaging-assisted evaluation to identify a long-circulating molecule, termed LAC NE . Blood pharmacokinetic analysis showed that LAC NE exhibited an estimated terminal blood half-life of 235.94 min, approximately 17-fold longer than that of DFO (13.74 min). Mechanistically, LAC NE was preferentially taken up by activated neutrophils via Fcγ receptor-mediated internalization under inflammatory conditions, resulting in effective suppression of neutrophil ferroptosis. Consequently, LAC NE reduced autoimmune responses, alleviated renal injury, and improved disease manifestations in lupus-prone mice. Collectively, these findings establish a PET-guided albumin-hitchhiking approach for pharmacokinetic optimization and targeted delivery of ferroptosis inhibitors, providing a promising strategy for precision treatment of SLE.

title: Stimuli-responsive CRISPR-based genome editing delivery system for cancer treatment: A review of fundamentals and applications.
abstract: Cancer remains a leading cause of mortality worldwide. Conventional modalities, namely surgery, radiotherapy, chemotherapy, and immunotherapy, continue to face substantial limitations. The advent of gene therapy, particularly CRISPR-based genome editing, offers new opportunities to overcome these barriers. Nuclease systems such as CRISPR/Cas9 enable precise excision of mutant alleles and targeted insertion of exogenous sequences by harnessing endogenous DNA-repair pathways, achieving durable and accurate genomic modification; derivative tools including CRISPRi, base editing, and prime editing enable diverse forms of gene regulation or precise genome modification through transcriptional repression, base conversion, or related editing mechanisms. To enhance the efficiency, specificity, and spatiotemporal control of CRISPR editing in vivo, sophisticated delivery platforms have been engineered to respond to endogenous tumor-microenvironment cues (e.g., pH, redox potential, hypoxia, ATP, enzymes and microRNAs) or exogenous triggers (e.g., light, ultrasound and magnetic fields). Distinct from material-centric classification schemes, this review organizes these stimuli-responsive systems according to their pathological relevance to the tumor microenvironment (TME), establishing a conceptual framework that links specific TME aberrations with corresponding delivery paradigms. These stimuli-responsive systems represent a major innovation and markedly expand the therapeutic potential of genome editing in oncology. In this review, we summarize the mechanistic basis of CRISPR-based editing, delineate design principles and engineering strategies for stimuli-responsive delivery, and highlight recent advances, outstanding challenges, and future directions toward clinical translation. We aim to provide a concise reference to guide the rational design of gene-editing cancer therapeutics.

title: Oral cancer data repositories: Challenges, ethical concerns, and strategic frameworks - A SWOT analysis.
abstract: Background Oral cancer represents a significant global health burden, with increasing incidence rates particularly in developing nations. The advent of Artificial intelligence and Machine learning in medical imaging has created unprecedented demand for high-quality, annotated oral cancer imaging datasets. Open-source repositories have emerged as critical resources for advancing diagnostic accuracy, treatment planning, and prognostic modeling. This review appraises the current landscape of open-source oral cancer imaging repositories, analyses the ethical frameworks governing dataset creation and distribution, and proposes future directions for responsible data sharing in oral oncology. Methodology A comprehensive literature search was conducted across PubMed, Google Scholar, and several medical imaging databases. We evaluated the available open-source datasets, their characteristics, ethical governance structures, technical specifications, strength, limitations and future scope. Results Various open-source repositories such as ORCHID (Oral Cancer Histology Image Database), AIKosh, Kaggle Oral Cancer Dataset, The Cancer Imaging Archive etc., exists for oral cancer imaging. However, significant gaps remain in dataset diversity, annotation quality, and ethical oversight. Key challenges include patient privacy protection, informed consent ambiguities, algorithmic bias from unrepresentative datasets, and inadequate data governance frameworks. Conclusions The development of ethical, comprehensive open-source oral cancer imaging repositories requires multi-stakeholder collaboration, robust regulatory frameworks, and commitment to principles of fairness, transparency, and patient autonomy. Future directions must prioritize diverse representation, federated learning approaches, and standardized ethical guidelines.

title: The SUBcutaneous Comprehensive UlTrasonographic (SUBCUT) protocol and Severity of Water and Edema Level Score (SWELS) for dynamic assessment of peripheral edema burden in critically ill patients: a prospective, longitudinal observational study.
abstract: Background Excessive fluid resuscitation may lead to pathologic fluid accumulation and increased mortality. Cumulative fluid balance (CFB) correlates poorly with outcomes. Ultrasonographic central congestion metrics (VExUS/Lung ultrasound) inherently overlook critical fluid shifts within the peripheral reservoir. To bridge this diagnostic gap, we developed the SUBcutaneous Comprehensive UlTrasonographic (SUBCUT) protocol for standardized, semi-quantitative assessment of peripheral edema burden. Methods Ultrasonographic assessment was performed bilaterally across six core anatomical regions using the SUBCUT protocol on days 1, 3, and 7. Individual sites were graded semi-quantitatively using the Ultrasonographic Subcutaneous Edema Grade (USEG, 0-4), yielding the Severity of Water and Edema Level Score (SWELS, 0-48) as the cumulative sum across 12 evaluation sites. The primary endpoint was ICU mortality, evaluating the prognostic performance of Day 3 SWELS. Results Among 111 patients analyzed (ICU mortality 23.4%; 26/111), baseline SWELS and CFB were similar between survivors and non-survivors. By Day 3, median SWELS surged in non-survivors (24 vs. 8; P < .001), yielding greater unadjusted, apparent discrimination than CFB (AUC 0.86 vs. 0.65). In competing-risk analysis, a 5-point increase in Day 3 SWELS was independently associated with ICU mortality (sHR, 1.51; 95% CI, 1.22-1.86; P < .001). Incorporating Day 3 SWELS into a contemporaneous clinical base model (Age, Admission Sepsis, Day 3 SOFA) enhanced model fit and discrimination (ΔAUC = 0.043; P = .008). Conclusions The SUBCUT protocol provides a novel framework for assessing peripheral edema burden. At Day 3, its derivative, SWELS, demonstrates incremental prognostic association beyond contemporaneous organ dysfunction, offering an extravascular perspective for multi-compartment fluid mapping.

The SUBCUT protocol provides a novel framework for assessing peripheral edema burden. At Day 3, its derivative, SWELS, demonstrates incremental prognostic association beyond contemporaneous organ dysfunction, offering an extravascular perspective for multi-compartment fluid mapping.

title: A Systematic Review of Bias, Validation, and Explainability in Artificial Intelligence Algorithms for Dental Diagnostics.
abstract: Objectives To critically evaluate the current role of artificial intelligence (AI) in dental diagnosis across multiple dental disciplines, assessing diagnostic performance, methodological quality, risk of bias, validation, explainability, and clinical applicability. Data and sources This systematic review was conducted in accordance with PRISMA guidelines and registered in PROSPERO (CRD42025639340). PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Embase, LILACS, Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, Web of Science, and ClinicalTrials.gov were searched up to December-2025. Two reviewers independently performed study selection, data extraction, and risk-of-bias assessment. Risk of bias in diagnostic accuracy studies was assessed using QUADAS-2-tool, evaluating the domains of patient selection, index test, reference standard, flow and timing whilst randomised studies were assessed using Cochrane RoB 2-tool. Reporting quality and transparency of AI-model development and validation were assessed using the selected items from TRIPOD-AI reporting guideline. Methodological quality and risk of bias in AI model development and evaluation were additionally assessed using PROBAST+AI. Study selection Ninety-six studies met the inclusion criteria, of which 90.6% were retrospective. Convolutional neural networks (CNN) were the most frequently used architecture (82.3%). Sixteen studies failed to specify the CNN architecture used. Reported diagnostic accuracy ranged from 81% to 99% across dental specialties, with high performance in implantology (92-99%), orthodontics (88-99%), endodontics (87-99%). Panoramic radiographs and cone-beam computed tomography were the most used imaging modalities. QUADAS-2 analysis indicated that high-risk of bias in 55.2% of studies and most lacked external validation, whilst Assessment using selected TRIPOD+AI items identified important gaps in reporting completeness and transparency, particularly in sample-size justification, missing-data handling, protocol availability, study registration, and data or code availability. Conclusions AI demonstrates substantial technical capability to enhance diagnostic accuracy and efficiency. However, the predominance of retrospective designs, limited external validation, and methodological weaknesses constrain the strength of current evidence. Clinical significance The use of AI is potentially considered as a decision-support tool rather than replacement for clinical judgement.

title: Accuracy of dynamic computer-assisted implant surgery in fully edentulous patients in a private practice: A retrospective cohort study.
abstract: Objectives To assess the accuracy of dynamic computer-assisted implant surgery (d-CAIS) in fully edentulous patients in a private practice setting and to identify factors associated with implant placement deviations. Methods A retrospective cohort study was conducted including patients treated with d-CAIS between June 2020 and September 2025. Pre- and postoperative cone beam computed tomography (CBCT) scans were superimposed to quantify deviations between planned and actual implant positions. To account for clustering of implants within patients, generalized estimating equation (GEE) models were used. A significance level of p < 0.05 was applied. Results A total of 107 patients (500 implants) were analyzed. Mean angular deviation was 1.87 ± 1.65°, while mean global deviations at the platform and apex levels were 1.06 ± 0.58 mm and 1.07 ± 0.60 mm, respectively. Mean directional and absolute apical depth deviation was -0.10 ± 0.84 mm and 0.60 ± 0.59 mm. Patient age, jaw (maxilla vs. mandible), implant region (anterior vs. posterior), placement site (healed vs. post-extraction), and pterygoid implants were significantly associated with implant placement deviations. Conclusions d-CAIS demonstrated a high level of accuracy for implant placement in fully edentulous patients, with low mean angular and linear deviations. Increased deviations were associated with older age and with implants placed in the maxilla, anterior region, post-extraction sites, and pterygoid areas. Clinical significance Dynamic navigation allows reliable implant placement in fully edentulous patients, despite the absence of stable anatomical references. Awareness of factors associated with increased deviations may help optimize treatment planning and improve surgical precision in complex cases.

title: Cognitive Evaluation of Multimodal Large Language Models in Dental Radiography.
abstract: Objectives We evaluated the cognitive capabilities and safety boundaries of general-purpose, zero-shot multimodal large language models (MLLMs) in dental radiography. Methods OralMLLM-Bench comprised 27 independently evaluated tasks across periapical, panoramic, and lateral cephalometric radiographs, grouped into four categories: perception, comprehension, prediction, and decision-making. Six MLLMs and two clinician comparators were evaluated across 3,820 assessment units using sensitivity, specificity, balanced accuracy (BA), partial-credit average score (PCAS), and conditional rationale accuracy (CRA). Results MLLMs showed relatively stronger performance for selected visually salient findings, with sensitivity up to 0.917 for root filling detection and 0.875 for restoration detection, but lower performance for low-contrast findings and spatial localization. Only 6 of 27 tasks showed significant between-model differences after false discovery rate correction, with no broad, consistent advantage for any model. Agreement with expert image-based reference assessments was generally limited in prediction and decision-making tasks. Errors included artifact-induced false positives, low-contrast-induced false negatives, spatial localization errors, conclusion-rationale inconsistency, and unflagged diagnostic uncertainty. Conclusions Under standardized, image-only benchmark conditions, MLLMs showed task-dependent performance and persistent limitations in dental radiography. Clinical significance OralMLLM-Bench provides a clinically grounded framework for evaluating model capability and safety boundaries across different categories of radiographic interpretation tasks, thereby supporting the development of safer and more clinically reliable AI systems.

title: Emerging optical coherence tomography markers and their association with the current classification of macular telangiectasia type 2.
abstract: To evaluate the frequency and clinical relevance of emerging optical coherence tomography (OCT) findings not included in the current Macular Telangiectasia (MacTel) type 2 classification system and to explore their associations with disease stage and visual acuity. This retrospective observational study included 60 patients (118 eyes) diagnosed with MacTel type 2. All patients underwent multimodal imaging, including color fundus photography, fluorescein angiography, fundus autofluorescence, and spectral-domain OCT. Eyes were classified according to the most recent MacTel Project criteria. OCT findings not incorporated into this classification, such as irregular foveal contour, hyperreflective middle retinal layer (MRL), inner and outer hyporeflective cavities (HC), and inner limiting membrane drape, were evaluated independently. Associations between these findings and disease stages were statistically analyzed. Additionally, the association of each OCT finding with best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA) was evaluated individually and through a multiple linear regression model to identify independent predictors of visual function. The mean patient age was 53.4±8.1 years. Stage 5 was the most common stage at diagnosis (P<0.001). The most prevalent non-classification OCT findings were hyperreflective MRL (65.3%), inner HC (62.7%), and irregular foveal contour (61.0%). Irregular foveal contour was significantly more frequent in advanced stages (P<0.001), while outer HC were present in 28.0% of eyes and were also associated with advanced disease (P=0.010). A significant stepwise deterioration in BCVA was observed across successive disease stages, with all pairwise stage comparisons reaching statistical significance (P<0.001). Among the OCT findings evaluated, irregular foveal contour was the only non-classification feature significantly associated with worse visual acuity. In the multivariate regression model, irregular foveal contour (P<0.001) also was an independent predictor of worse visual acuity. Several OCT features not yet incorporated into the current classification, particularly irregular foveal contour and outer retinal hyporeflective cavities, showed significant associations with advanced stage. The progressive decline in BCVA across disease stages supports the functional validity of the current classification system. Irregular foveal contour was independently associated with worse visual acuity, providing an additional rationale for its inclusion in future classification revisions. These findings suggest that integrating emerging OCT markers, such as irregular foveal contour and outer retinal hyporeflective cavities, into future revisions of the MacTel type 2 classification may improve disease staging accuracy and understanding of MacTel type 2 progression.

title: Skeletal Muscle Loss with Atezolizumab-Bevacizumab versus Lenvatinib in Unresectable HCC.
abstract: Background & aims Skeletal muscle loss is a recognized prognostic factor in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). However, whether skeletal muscle loss during systemic therapy reflects treatment-related effects rather than tumor progression remains unclear. This study evaluated treatment-specific muscle loss and its prognostic impact. Methods We retrospectively analyzed a prospective multicenter cohort of patients with unresectable HCC treated with lenvatinib (LEN) or atezolizumab plus bevacizumab (ATZ-BEV). Skeletal muscle index (SMI) was measured by computed tomography at baseline and 6 months, and a ≥5% decrease was defined as significant loss. Inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) adjusted baseline differences. The primary endpoint was change in SMI over 6 months between treatments among patients without progression within 6 months. Secondary endpoints assessed associations of muscle loss with overall survival (OS) and progression-free survival (PFS) using a 6-month landmark analysis. Results A total of 179 patients with disease control at 6 months were included. SMI decline was significantly greater in the LEN group than in the ATZ-BEV group both before and after IPTW adjustment (-6.4% vs -0.6%, P=0.017; -6.4% vs -1.0%, P=0.036). A ≥5% SMI reduction occurred in 52.8% of LEN-treated patients and 38.5% of ATZ-BEV-treated patients. In IPTW-adjusted analysis, ATZ-BEV was independently associated with a lower risk of significant muscle loss (odds ratio 0.45, 95% confidence interval 0.22-0.95; P=0.036). In the landmark analysis, treatment-related skeletal muscle loss was not associated with PFS but was significantly associated with worse OS both before (P=0.002) and after IPTW adjustment (P=0.008). Conclusion Treatment-specific skeletal muscle loss differs between regimens and is associated with worse overall survival in unresectable HCC. Impact and implications Skeletal muscle loss during systemic therapy is increasingly recognized as an important determinant of prognosis in patients with unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma. In this multicenter study, atezolizumab-bevacizumab was associated with a significantly lower risk of treatment-related skeletal muscle loss than lenvatinib after adjustment for baseline characteristics. These findings suggest that preservation of skeletal muscle should be considered when selecting systemic therapies and monitoring patients during treatment. Although confirmation in prospective studies is required, our results provide clinically relevant evidence supporting routine assessment of skeletal muscle and the development of interventions aimed at preventing treatment-related skeletal muscle loss.

title: Re-evaluating the 6-cm threshold for invasive intervention in lung abscess: a single-center retrospective cohort study.
abstract: Background Lung abscesses are associated with substantial morbidity and mortality, yet evidence-based treatment guidelines are lacking. Antibiotic therapy is primary, although cavities ≥6 cm are considered for percutaneous drainage or surgical resection. However, the prognostic significance of this threshold remains unclear. We evaluated whether an abscess cavity diameter ≥6 cm is associated with conservative antibiotic therapy failure. Methods A single-center retrospective cohort study of patients hospitalized with lung abscesses and initially treated with antibiotics between April 2004 and June 2024 was conducted. The primary endpoint was treatment failure, a composite of computed tomography-guided percutaneous drainage, surgical resection, and in-hospital death. Patients were classified into small-size (<6 cm) and large-size (≥6 cm) groups. Propensity score overlap weighting adjusted for baseline differences and restricted cubic spline logistic regression (four knots, adjusted for age and sex) assessed nonlinear associations. Results Among 109 patients (mean age, 71.2 years; 21 women [19.3%]), unadjusted treatment failure was higher in the large-size group than in the small-size group (38.5% vs. 12.5%, P = 0.044) but did not differ after weighting (39.8% vs. 28.8%, P = 0.483). No significant differences were observed in percutaneous drainage, surgery, or in-hospital mortality. Spline analysis showed a gradual increase in the estimated coefficient for treatment failure without a distinct threshold at 6 cm. Conclusions We found no clear evidence of an independent association between abscess cavities ≥6 cm and treatment failure or mortality after adjustment. Antibiotic therapy remains a valid initial approach, and intervention should be guided by clinical characteristics and response.

Background

Lung abscesses are associated with substantial morbidity and mortality, yet evidence-based treatment guidelines are lacking. Antibiotic therapy is primary, although cavities ≥6 cm are considered for percutaneous drainage or surgical resection. However, the prognostic significance of this threshold remains unclear. We evaluated whether an abscess cavity diameter ≥6 cm is associated with conservative antibiotic therapy failure.

Methods

A single-center retrospective cohort study of patients hospitalized with lung abscesses and initially treated with antibiotics between April 2004 and June 2024 was conducted. The primary endpoint was treatment failure, a composite of computed tomography-guided percutaneous drainage, surgical resection, and in-hospital death. Patients were classified into small-size (<6 cm) and large-size (≥6 cm) groups. Propensity score overlap weighting adjusted for baseline differences and restricted cubic spline logistic regression (four knots, adjusted for age and sex) assessed nonlinear associations.

Results

Among 109 patients (mean age, 71.2 years; 21 women [19.3%]), unadjusted treatment failure was higher in the large-size group than in the small-size group (38.5% vs. 12.5%, P = 0.044) but did not differ after weighting (39.8% vs. 28.8%, P = 0.483). No significant differences were observed in percutaneous drainage, surgery, or in-hospital mortality. Spline analysis showed a gradual increase in the estimated coefficient for treatment failure without a distinct threshold at 6 cm.

Conclusions

We found no clear evidence of an independent association between abscess cavities ≥6 cm and treatment failure or mortality after adjustment. Antibiotic therapy remains a valid initial approach, and intervention should be guided by clinical characteristics and response.

title: Effects of CBCT acquisition protocols and metal artifact reduction on gray-value measurements of dental restorative materials.
abstract: Background Cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) imaging is frequently affected by artifacts caused by dental restorative materials, which compromise gray-value accuracy and diagnostic reliability. This study evaluated mean ROI gray values in phantom teeth restored with glass ionomer or composite resin under different CBCT acquisition protocols, field-of-view settings, and metal artifact reduction (MAR) conditions. Methods Twenty standardized three-dimensional printed phantom teeth were restored with glass ionomer (n = 10) or composite resin (n = 10). Each specimen was evaluated under three CBCT acquisition protocols (2 mA-0.30 mm, 5 mA-0.30 mm, and 6.3 mA-0.15 mm), two field-of-view settings, and MAR-on and MAR-off reconstruction conditions. A total of 960 region-of-interest (ROI) gray-value measurements were obtained. Data were analyzed using a linear mixed-effects model with a specimen-level random intercept, including MAR × acquisition protocol and MAR × restorative material interactions. Tooth-level paired comparisons were performed with Holm adjustment for multiple testing. Results MAR-associated gray-value changes differed significantly across acquisition protocols (Wald χ 2 (2) = 1057.29, p < 0.001), and a significant MAR × restorative material interaction was identified (p < 0.001). In tooth-level paired analyses, significant MAR-associated reductions were observed only under the 6.3 mA-0.15 mm protocol (mean difference: -25.985; 95% CI: -32.188 to -19.781; Holm-adjusted p < 0.001). The reduction was greater for composite resin (-37.314) than for glass ionomer (-14.655). Mandibular field of view was associated with lower gray values (p = 0.014), whereas section orientation and ROI location showed no significant main effects (p > 0.05). Conclusions The observed ROI gray-value differences were specific to the evaluated phantom setup and acquisition and reconstruction conditions. These measurements do not establish changes in artifact severity or diagnostic accuracy. Clinical significance Protocol- and MAR-associated gray-value changes may have implications for image interpretation, but their diagnostic relevance requires validation in anatomically representative models or clinical studies.

title: Feasibility of Intraoperative Indocyanine Green Fluorescence Angiography for Perfusion Assessment in Pediatric Adnexal Mass-Associated Torsion.
abstract: Study objective To evaluate the feasibility of intraoperative indocyanine green (ICG) fluorescence angiography for perfusion assessment in children with adnexal mass-associated torsion and to explore its potential clinical value using a historical comparison cohort. Design Retrospective cohort study with a historical comparison cohort. Setting A single tertiary pediatric surgical center. Participants Thirty-eight children who underwent surgery with intraoperative ICG fluorescence angiography for adnexal mass-associated torsion between January 2022 and September 2024 were retrospectively compared with a historical cohort of 58 children treated without ICG between January 2020 and January 2022. Interventions Serial ICG fluorescence angiography was performed before detorsion and after lesion enucleation with adnexal reconstruction. Qualitative perfusion patterns, signal-to-background ratio (SBR), postoperative ultrasound findings, and propensity score-matched clinical outcomes were evaluated. Measurements and main results All 38 patients successfully underwent intraoperative ICG fluorescence angiography, with no ICG-related adverse events observed. Qualitative perfusion patterns changed from Type A/B/C in 3/16/19 patients before detorsion to 13/17/8 after adnexal reconstruction. The median signal-to-background ratio (SBR) increased from 0.841 (interquartile range [IQR], 0.569-0.979) before detorsion to 0.920 (IQR, 0.696-1.046) after reconstruction (P = .038). Among 16 patients with absent preoperative Doppler flow on the torsed side, 12 demonstrated Type A or B perfusion after reconstruction. Among the 36 patients with at least 3 months of postoperative ultrasound follow-up, 33 (91.7%) had a Good outcome, 2 (5.6%) had an Intermediate outcome, and 1 (2.8%) had a Poor outcome. Given the small numbers of Intermediate and Poor outcomes, associations between intraoperative ICG findings and postoperative ultrasound outcomes were evaluated descriptively. After 1:1 propensity score matching of patients with at least 3 months of postoperative ultrasound follow-up, 17 matched pairs were analyzed. Organ preservation was achieved in all patients in both groups (100% vs 100%; P = 1.000). Good postoperative ultrasound outcomes were observed in 17 of 17 patients (100%) in the ICG group and 16 of 17 patients (94.1%) in the non-ICG group, with no significant difference in outcome distribution (P = 1.000). Conclusion Intraoperative ICG fluorescence angiography is a feasible adjunct for real-time perfusion assessment during organ-preserving surgery in children with adnexal mass-associated torsion. It provides additional information on tissue perfusion that may support intraoperative organ-preserving decision-making. Further prospective multicenter studies are warranted to establish its role in clinical practice.

title: Evaluation of knowledge, attitudes, and perceptions of interventional radiology among the Jordanian population.
abstract: Background Interventional Radiology (IR) comprises multiple minimally invasive techniques that aid in the diagnosis and treatment of a plethora of conditions. However, some studies worldwide indicate low public awareness, with IR often conflated with Diagnostic Radiology (DR). No prior study has evaluated this knowledge gap in Jordan. This study aims to assess the knowledge, attitudes, and perceptions of IR among the Jordanian population. Methods A cross-sectional, questionnaire-based survey was distributed via social media and convenience sampling. The survey, available in both English and Arabic, assessed demographics, awareness, procedural knowledge, and attitudes toward IR. A total of 429 participants were analyzed using R software. Statistical analyses included descriptive statistics, reliability analysis, and multivariable logistic regression. Results Slightly over half (52.2%) of participants had heard of IR. Self-assessed knowledge was low (67.6% "Poor/Very poor"), and 73.9% were confused about the difference between IR and DR. While 72.0% preferred IR over surgery in a hypothetical choice, only 44.1% definitively agreed to undergo an IR procedure when advised. Awareness was significantly lower among females and those in non-medical occupations. High rates of misattribution were observed, with only 18.2% correctly identifying MRI as a DR procedure. Conclusion There is a significant public knowledge gap regarding IR in Jordan, creating an "awareness-preference paradox." Despite a theoretical preference for minimally invasive IR treatments, a lack of concrete knowledge hinders real-world acceptance. Targeted educational initiatives are needed to clarify the role of IR and improve the utilization of these therapeutic options. Plain language summary Interventional radiology uses minimally invasive procedures guided by medical imaging and can offer an alternative to some types of surgery. This study surveyed people in Jordan to understand their knowledge and views of interventional radiology and related imaging services. This study found that awareness and understanding of interventional radiology were generally low, many people confused it with diagnostic imaging, but most said they would prefer a minimally invasive treatment option. This matters because better public education could help people make informed healthcare decisions and improve access to available treatment options.

title: Quantitative DWI-ADC metrics in extrapulmonary tuberculosis: Differentiating endemic mimics with pathological validation.
abstract: Background Extrapulmonary tuberculosis (EPTB) causes disproportionate morbidity due to diagnostic delays. EPTB mimics endemic infections including cryptococcal meningitis, brucellosis, and echinococcosis, creating diagnostic uncertainty. Quantitative ADC measurement offers non-invasive differentiation but population-specific cutoff values for this setting remain absent. Methods This prospective diagnostic accuracy study enrolled 90 adults (45 confirmed EPTB, all anti-tuberculous therapy-naive at the time of imaging, and 45 endemic disease controls) at a tertiary care hospital. Primary outcome diagnostic accuracy of quantitative diffusion-weighted imaging-derived ADC for differentiating EPTB from endemic mimics. Secondary outcomes ADC associations with inflammatory markers; pathological correlates in surgically-confirmed cases. Standardized 1.5T/3.0T MRI protocols with quantitative ADC measurement. Receiver operating characteristic curve analysis. Results 90 completed (100%). TB cases: 53.3% CNS, 26.7% spinal, 20.0% abdominal; controls: 33.3% cryptococcal, 20.0% fungal, 26.7% brucellosis, 13.3% echinococcosis, 6.7% bacterial. Mean lesion ADC: TB 0.58 × 10⁻³ mm²/s versus cryptococcal 0.92, fungal 1.04, brucellosis 0.72, echinococcosis 1.18, bacterial 1.32 (p < 0.001). Optimal threshold ≤0.82: sensitivity 84.4%, specificity 88.9%, AUROC 0.919 (95% CI 0.868-0.959). ADC correlated with CSF lactate (r = -0.642) and procalcitonin (r = -0.584; both p < 0.001). Conclusions Quantitative ADC differentiated EPTB from endemic mimics with an AUROC of 0.919; a threshold of ≤0.82 × 10⁻³ mm²/s gave 84.4% sensitivity and 88.9% specificity, and implementation proved feasible (87.5% radiologist competency in 3.2 weeks). These estimates are provisional. The threshold was derived and evaluated in the same 90 participants without an independent test set; enrolment reached 45 cases against a calculated requirement of 64; and the cohort was drawn from a tertiary referral stream in which central nervous system and spinal disease predominated, with confirmed cases compared against confirmed alternative diagnoses rather than undifferentiated febrile presentations. The findings establish that a substantial and reproducible difference in lesion diffusivity exists, rather than accurately characterising its magnitude, and require prospective external validation before ADC-based algorithms are adopted clinically. Plain language summary Tuberculosis can occur outside the lungs and can be difficult to distinguish from other infections that cause similar symptoms. This study used MRI scans from adults with tuberculosis and other infections to assess whether a measurement called the apparent diffusion coefficient, which reflects how water moves within tissues, could help tell these conditions apart. This study found that people with extrapulmonary tuberculosis had lower apparent diffusion coefficient values than those with other infections, and the measurement showed good diagnostic accuracy. This matters because a non-invasive imaging marker may help support earlier and more accurate diagnosis, although further research is needed before routine clinical use.

title: Comparative performance analysis of lung sparse-view reconstruction algorithms for deep learning-based image quality improvement.
abstract: Sparse-view computed tomography is a promising technique to dramatically reduce the radiation dose delivered to patients; however, it also significantly degrades image quality. We investigated the trade-off between reconstruction algorithms, the number of X-ray projections, and image-quality improvement for 3 reconstruction algorithms. A total of 4586 lung CT images were collected, and the corresponding sparse-view images were simulated and reconstructed using three algorithms, namely the Filtered Back Projection, Simultaneous Iterative Reconstruction Technique, and Conjugate Gradient Least Squares, under six undersampling scenarios: 16, 32, 64, 128, 256, and 512 views. A Cycle-GAN model was developed to generate realistic CT images from low-dose sparse-view CT images. Then, generated images were compared to the ground truth images from a clinical dataset of 25 patients, using the Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE), Peak Signal-to-Noise Ratio (PSNR), Structural Similarity Index (SSIM), Universal Image Quality Index (UQI), and Fréchet and Kernel Inception Distances (FID) and (KID). Qualitative evaluation demonstrated good reconstruction of anatomical details across the three algorithms, with difference maps indicating lower reconstruction errors at higher projection counts. Quantitative assessment, however, revealed marked differences among the algorithms, especially in the 16- and 32-view CT sets, where the image improvement task was more challenging, and smaller errors were observed from 64 to 512 views. Furthermore, RMSE, PSNR, and SSIM values indicated higher reconstruction accuracy for FBP and SIRT at higher projection counts, whereas CGLS showed lower accuracy from 128- to 512-view CT. UQI, FID, and KID showed a continuous improvement pattern as the number of projections increased for all algorithms CONCLUSION: Sparse-view CT represents a promising dose-reduction strategy, particularly when combined with deep learning models to preserve higher image quality. CT scans can be performed with fewer X-ray measurements to reduce radiation exposure, but doing so can make images less clear. This study compared several image reconstruction methods and used artificial intelligence to improve low-dose CT images created from fewer X-ray measurements. This study found that image quality improved as the number of measurements increased, and that combining sparse-view CT with artificial intelligence helped preserve important anatomical details despite lower radiation exposure. This matters because these approaches may help reduce radiation dose while maintaining the image quality needed for diagnosis.

title: A reproducible pipeline for simulating individual and inter-brain neural dynamics from structural connectivity.
abstract: Background Computational models can link anatomical structure to neural dynamics. However, there is no validated, reproducible pipeline that simulates individual and inter-brain EEG-like dynamics from an individual's own structural connectome. New method To address this, we developed a comprehensive computational pipeline that combines probabilistic tractography from Diffusion Magnetic Resonance Imaging (dMRI) with dynamical systems modeling to simulate EEG-like neural dynamics from individual connectomes. It extracts anatomical connectivity, intra-individual functional connectivity, and inter-individual (two-brain) functional coupling features. It then evaluates their group-discriminative information with random-forest classification under repeated nested cross-validation. Simulated phase-locking values are calibrated against empirical resting-state EEG. Results In a test sample of individuals with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) and matched controls (16 each), simulated intra-individual synchrony added classification information beyond anatomy, raising accuracy from 71.2% (AUC 0.843) to 77.6% (AUC 0.871), in a sample where groups did not differ in mean structural connectivity. Comparison with existing methods Unlike current single-brain simulations, this pipeline generates and jointly simulates two individual brain models within a single system, and reports the contribution of each feature level explicitly. Conclusions The pipeline provides a reproducible, extensible framework for deriving informative individual-level dynamic features from anatomy. The two-brain extension generates and ranks candidate inter-brain features, providing a principled way to identify between-brain measures for hypothesis-driven testing.

title: Resomapper: An integrated workflow for quantitative multiparametric MRI in preclinical studies.
abstract: Background Quantitative magnetic resonance imaging (qMRI) provides insights into tissue microstructure and physiology, making it a tool in preclinical research. However, its processing often requires coding expertise. New method We present Resomapper, an open-source, cross-platform tool designed to simplify multiparametric MRI analysis. Resomapper integrates libraries into a user-friendly workflow that supports T 1 , T 2 , and T 2 * relaxometry mapping, magnetization transfer imaging, and diffusion tensor imaging. It incorporates preprocessing steps -including denoising, Gibbs artifact removal, and bias correction- and enables interactive and automated processing. Results Resomapper was applied to a multiparametric 7 T dataset of healthy mouse brain, generating T 1 , T 2 , T 2 *, magnetization transfer ratio and diffusion tensor maps. The values fell within the ranges reported in the literature and reproduced the differences between grey and white matter regions, illustrating its use in a preclinical study. Comparison with existing methods Resomapper distinguishes itself from qMRI tools not through novel algorithms, but through its integration of established, validated libraries into a single, streamlined pipeline for data conversion, preprocessing and parametric mapping. Maps showed excellent agreement with qMRLab for T 2 and were consistent with DSI Studio for mean and axial diffusivity, while systematic differences in radial diffusivity and fractional anisotropy were attributable to the tensor fitting methods. Its design prioritizes reproducibility and standardization, and its Python implementation makes the tool straightforward to install, inspect, and adapt, even for researchers without extensive coding backgrounds. Conclusions By improving accessibility, reproducibility, and standardization, Resomapper aims to facilitate broader adoption of qMRI in preclinical imaging despite current methodological challenges.

title: Osteoarthritis year in review 2026: Imaging.
abstract: Objective To narratively review the literature on osteoarthritis (OA) imaging published between March 2025 and March 2026 and to identify current trends and emerging directions in imaging-based OA research. Methods PubMed was searched for original English-language human in vivo studies published during the period. Trends by imaging modality and target-joint distributions were analyzed. For narrative synthesis, studies were selected subjectively by consensus among the authors based on methodological novelty, clinical or trial relevance, contribution to understanding OA pathophysiology or progression, and potential future impact. Results Of 1,910 publications identified, 1,035 specified a target joint. Approximately 70% investigated the knee, followed by the hip. Radiography and ultrasound yielded the most records, encompassing heterogeneous applications such as trial eligibility and image-guided procedures. Although publication counts for these modalities have gradually declined in recent years, those for MRI have remained stable. Semiquantitative MRI analysis linked worsening bone marrow lesions and Hoffa-synovitis to greater cartilage loss, and suggested differing associations between injection type and subsequent structural progression. Quantitative MRI studies linked cartilage T2 to BMI in a population-based cohort, while muscle radiomics predicted incident knee OA. Among emerging technique, magnetic resonance fingerprinting (MRF) provided rapid cartilage T2 mapping, and [18F]NaF PET-MRI linked increased metabolic activity at enthesis to worse knee-related outcomes. For clinical-trial eligibility, MRI detected exclusionary abnormalities in 10% of otherwise DMOAD-eligible knees. AI-related publications gradually increased, with applications including prediction of future total knee replacement (TKR) and automated tissue segmentation. Conclusion Studies highlight the use of imaging for longitudinal assessment of structural progression, clinical-trial eligibility, and quantitative tissue characterization. MRI remains central to understanding disease mechanisms and progression, while emerging techniques such as MRF and [18F]NaF PET-MRI broaden quantitative and metabolic assessment. AI may support prediction of future TKR and automated cartilage morphometry.
