title: Active negative loss: A robust framework for learning with noisy labels.
abstract: Deep supervised learning has achieved remarkable success across a wide range of tasks, yet it remains susceptible to overfitting when confronted with noisy labels. To address this issue, noise-robust loss functions offer an effective solution for enhancing learning in the presence of label noise. In this work, we systematically investigate the limitation of the recently proposed Active Passive Loss (APL), which employs Mean Absolute Error (MAE) as its passive loss function. Despite the robustness brought by MAE, one of its key drawbacks is that it pays equal attention to clean and noisy samples; this feature slows down convergence and potentially makes training difficult, particularly in large-scale datasets. To overcome these challenges, we introduce a novel loss function class, termed Normalized Negative Loss Functions (NNLFs), which serve as passive loss functions within the APL framework. NNLFs effectively address the limitations of MAE by concentrating more on memorized clean samples. By replacing MAE in APL with our proposed NNLFs, we enhance APL and present a new framework called Active Negative Loss (ANL). Moreover, in non-symmetric noise scenarios, we propose an entropy-based regularization technique to mitigate the vulnerability to the label imbalance. Our experiments demonstrate competitive performance against representative robust-loss methods across the evaluated symmetric, asymmetric, instance-dependent, and real-world label-noise settings. In addition, we evaluate the ANL framework on two medical image segmentation benchmarks, ISIC-2017 and GlaS, under noisy mask annotations. The source code of our method is available at: https://github.com/xichenye0930/Active-Negative-Loss.

title: BH-CDiff: Boundary-aware and heterogeneous feature synergy cold diffusion for medical image segmentation.
abstract: Recently, diffusion models have shown significant potential for medical image segmentation, providing improved interpretability through their iterative optimization process. To address the uncertainty introduced by Gaussian noise in traditional diffusion methods, the cold diffusion paradigm replaces stochastic noise with task-relevant perturbations, enabling more controllable mask generation. However, existing cold diffusion-based segmentation methods still face challenges in recovering boundary structures during iterative restoration and effectively exploiting dynamically evolving heterogeneous representations. This paper proposes a boundary-aware and heterogeneous feature synergy cold diffusion network (BH-CDiff). Specifically, we introduce a boundary-aware modeling mechanism through the boundary-aware feature modulation (BAFM) module, which uses boundary priors to guide channel-spatial attention and effectively enhance boundary information. The heterogeneous feature synergy mechanism is realized through the multi-domain representation synergy (MDRS) module and the dual-source feature fusion (DSFF) module. The former jointly models frequency-domain and spatial-domain features for synergistic multi-domain representation, while the latter fuses segmentation features with conditional priors to promote complementary enhancement of dual-source information. Extensive experiments on the ISIC 2018, CVC-ClinicDB, and REFUGE datasets demonstrate that the proposed method attains state-of-the-art results.

title: Long-term heading exposure in relation to structural MRI markers and neurocognitive function in retired professional soccer players.
abstract: Background and purpose Repetitive head impacts from purposeful heading in soccer have raised concerns about long-term neurological effects, but in vivo MRI markers remain underexplored. Most published imaging studies have involved amateur, youth or currently active players. Retired professionals with a full career of heading exposure and no reported concussion have rarely been investigated. Our objective was to evaluate structural brain differences and neuropsychological performance in retired or late-career professional soccer players without concussion history compared to high-level athletes from non-contact sports. Materials and methods In this cross-sectional study, male professional soccer players and male non-contact athletes underwent 3T brain MRI and standardized cognitive testing. Imaging included volumetric assessment of the cavum septi pellucidi (CSP) and cavum vergae, automated quantification of white matter hyperintensities (WMH), voxel-based morphometry analysis of regional brain volume, and cerebral microbleed detection. Neuropsychological testing assessed reaction time, memory, attention, and executive functioning. title: NA-DIP: A Noise-Aware Deep Image Prior for Generating Dedicated Brain PET-Quality Images from Whole-Body PET Acquisitions.
abstract: Purpose To generate dedicated brain PET-quality images from routine whole-body PET acquisitions by robustly enhancing the brain region using a noise-aware deep image prior (NA-DIP) approach. Methods NA-DIP integrates anatomy-guided priors derived from patient-specific μ-maps or MR images, a regularization strategy for enhanced denoising, and a variance-based early stopping criterion that adaptively monitors noise without requiring prior noise assumptions. Using noisy PET images as self-supervised targets, the method was first evaluated using simulation data spanning three noise levels to investigate the trade-off between noise suppression and bias. It was then applied to brain images extracted from 90-s-per-bed-position whole-body acquisitions from 15 pediatric FDG-PET studies spanning a broad range of patient demographics, physiological variability, and image noise levels. Using the corresponding 360-s-per-bed-position dedicated brain scans as the reference, NA-DIP-enhanced images were evaluated for noise reduction, standardized uptake value (SUV) accuracy, and image quality in a blinded reader study. Results NA-DIP demonstrated a superior noise-bias trade-off compared with Gaussian filtering and conventional DIP stopping strategies, particularly under high-noise conditions. The inclusion of MR or μ-map guidance further improved performance. Across pediatric patients, NA-DIP-enhanced 90-s images exhibited lower noise than the corresponding 360-s dedicated brain images while showing modest variability in SUV measurements. Blinded readers rated the NA-DIP-enhanced images as comparable to or better than dedicated brain images in most cases. Conclusion NA-DIP enhanced brain PET images from whole-body acquisitions demonstrated good quantitative agreement and image quality comparable to or exceeding the reference, supporting the feasibility of eliminating separate dedicated brain scans.

title: Accurate 3D brain cross-modality image translation by lesion-aware post-training of latent diffusion models with voxel-space objectives.
abstract: Cross-modality image synthesis offers significant potential for mitigating challenges in medical image acquisition, particularly in acute settings. While latent diffusion models (LDMs) currently represent the state-of-the-art in generative modeling by leveraging compressed latent spaces, this efficiency necessitates a trade-off that often compromises fine structural details. This limitation is particularly critical when reconstructing small but clinically significant structures, such as ischemic lesions, where high-fidelity delineation is essential for diagnostic utility. To address this challenge, we propose a novel post-training framework for LDMs in 3D medical image-to-image translation by incorporating lesion-aware medical voxel-space objectives (LDM-3D-LAPT). Specifically, we convert the pretrained 2D LDM into a 3D volumetric model and post-train the model using a multi-objective loss function incorporating global image reconstruction, focal lesion-specific reconstruction, and auxiliary lesion segmentation guidance. We evaluate this framework on the task of synthesizing diffusion MRI from CT perfusion scans in a cohort of 100 acute ischemic stroke patients. We further evaluate our framework in an independent external cohort of 85 patients. Ablation studies showed that voxel-space post-training improved lesion segmentation. Internal and external evaluations demonstrated gains in ADC lesion fidelity and lesion-detection sensitivity. Our adaptable post-training strategy provides a practical approach to improving lesion-focused medical image translation.

title: An approximation of MRI R 2 * as a rapid surrogate of nigral iron in Parkinson's disease.
abstract: Nigral iron accumulation is a robust imaging marker of Parkinson's disease and is commonly assessed using R 2 * mapping. However, its clinical implementation is limited by long acquisition times. An alternative metric, effective R 2 , derived from dual-contrast proton density- and T2-weighted MRI, has recently been proposed as a fast surrogate of tissue iron content. Using data from the Parkinson's Progression Markers Initiative (PPMI), we evaluated the diagnostic and longitudinal performance of effective R 2 in the substantia nigra (SN) across multiple scanner platforms. Cross-sectional analysis demonstrated significantly higher effective R 2 values in de novo Parkinson's disease patients (n = 187) compared with prodromal subjects (n = 26), with consistent effects across acquisition protocols. In Siemens data (177 patients and 25 prodromal subjects), effective R 2 achieved good discriminative performance for Parkinson's disease classification (AUC = 0.85). Longitudinal analysis for 14 patients over 36 months showed no significant change in effective R 2 values despite clinical progression measured by MDS-UPDRS Part III scores. These findings indicate that effective R 2 provides robust cross-sectional discrimination of early Parkinson's disease but with limited sensitivity to disease progression.

title: Choroid plexus remodeling in aging and cerebrovascular disease revealed by contrast-enhanced 7T MRI.
abstract: Background The choroid plexus is essential for brain homeostasis, yet its in vivo morphology remains incompletely characterized. Conventional MRI visualizes only part of the choroid plexus and may therefore misrepresent age- and disease-related structural changes. We aim to develop a 7T contrast-enhanced black-blood imaging (CeBBI) framework for whole-brain visualization and quantitative morphologic characterization of the choroid plexus, and to examine its associations with aging and cerebrovascular disease. Methods We retrospectively included 234 participants referred for evaluation of intracranial atherosclerotic disease who underwent CeBBI. A deep learning model was trained to segment the whole choroid plexus. Choroid plexus volume, centerline-based shape features and cystic components were quantified. Segmentations derived from CeBBI were compared with those obtained using a validated T1-weighted MRI-based method. Associations with age, ventricular size and vascular imaging markers were assessed. Results 7T CeBBI enabled visualization of the choroid plexus across all ventricular compartments. The segmentation model achieved high accuracy (Dice score=0.901±0.013), and recovered more than twice the choroid plexus volume detected by the T1-weighted method. Total choroid plexus volume was not associated with age. However, with advancing age, the lateral ventricular choroid plexus became shorter (left r=-0.250, right r=-0.303, both P<0.001) and showed greater cross-sectional area (left r=0.174, right r=0.176, both P=0.007). Choroid plexus cyst number (r=0.187, P=0.004) and cyst volume (r=0.159, P=0.015) also increased with age. Cerebral microbleeds were independently associated with greater lateral ventricular choroid plexus volume (standardized β=0.178, P=0.012). Conclusions Our method enables robust whole-brain visualization and quantitative morphologic assessment of the choroid plexus. Rather than undergoing simple age-related hypertrophy, the choroid plexus showed complex remodeling characterized by shortening, cross-sectional expansion and cystic change. The association between cerebral microbleeds and larger choroid plexus volume further supports a potential role of vascular dysfunction in choroid plexus remodeling.

title: Linking Theory of Mind and Cardiac Vagal Regulation: the Integrative Role of the Posterior Cerebellum.
abstract: Interpersonal interactions are fundamentally regulated by Social Cognition, a multifaceted construct encompassing the cognitive and neural processes used to navigate the social environment. Within this overarching architecture, Theory of Mind (ToM), or mentalizing, provides a foundational dual-level framework of implicit and explicit systems. Although these functions traditionally rely on a cortical mentalizing network, recent findings support a cerebellar contribution to ToM processes. Given that the cerebellar computational architecture is suited for the rapid, automated processing of visual social cues, investigating lower-level social decoding offers a unique window into the cerebellar contribution to ToM. Building on this framework, the present research explored the relation between cerebellar morphometry and lower-level ToM in healthy subjects. Participants underwent MRI to assess cerebellar Gray Matter volumes and completed the computerized version of the Reading the Mind in the Eyes Test (RMET). Since the lower-level mentalizing is closely tied to complex interactions between the Central and Autonomic Nervous Systems (ANS), the present study also examined the relationships between cerebellar volumes and Heart Rate Variability, namely the variations of Root Mean Square of Successive Differences (RMSSD) values across the RMET procedure. Findings revealed that volumes of cerebellar lobules VI, VIIb, Crus II, and vermis IX predicted the RMET accuracy. Furthermore, the volume of vermis IX selectively predicted RMSSD variation during the rest-recovery transition, with smaller vermis IX volumes associated with a sharper, more progressive RMSSD decline. Overall, these data highlight that posterior cerebellar morphometry is associated with RMET performance and cardiac vagal regulation, thus supporting lower-level mentalizing.

title: Multimodal MRI reveals brain structural and functional abnormalities associated with wearing-off phenomenon in Parkinson's disease.
abstract: Objectives The pathogenesis of the wearing-off (WO) phenomenon in Parkinson's disease (PD) remains unclear. This study aims to explore the abnormalities in brain structure and function among PD patients with WO. Methods A total of 39 PD patients with wearing-off (PD-WO) and 43 PD patients without wearing-off (PD-nWO) were prospectively enrolled. Voxel-based morphometry (VBM) was employed in this study to evaluate structural differences, and functional connectivity (FC) was used to assess functional differences between the two groups. Results Compared with PD-nWO patients, PD-WO patients showed significantly reduced gray matter volume (GMV) within the left middle occipital gyrus (MOG.L), bilateral middle temporal gyri (MTG.L/R), as well as the left triangular division of the inferior frontal gyrus (IFGtriang.L). Regarding functional connectivity, PD-WO patients exhibited widespread abnormalities, including weakened connectivity in the cerebellar-basal ganglia-sensorimotor cortex circuits, hippocampus-postcentral gyrus, and cerebellar-occipital (cuneal cortex) pathways, as well as enhanced connectivity between cerebellar subregions and between the cerebellum and occipital cortex (lingual gyrus) and parahippocampal gyrus. Conclusions This preliminary single-center cross-sectional study revealed significant differences in brain structure and function between PD-WO and PD-nWO patients. These findings provide a better understanding of the neural mechanisms behind the WO phenomenon in PD and suggest potential therapeutic targets.

title: A cross-modal hierarchical refinement network with uncertainty-guided multi-task learning for brain tumour segmentation, grading, and subtype classification.
abstract: Reliable brain-tumour assessment requires accurate volumetric delineation together with clinically meaningful grading. However, most existing pipelines treat segmentation, LGG/HGG classification, and low-grade glioma subtyping as separate tasks. We propose CMHRNet, a cross-modal hierarchical refinement network that jointly performs tumour segmentation from multimodal MRI, binary glioma grading, and astrocytoma versus oligodendroglioma classification using paired MRI and whole-slide histopathology images. The model combines a Hybrid Swin-Transformer segmentation encoder with deep supervision, Learnable Feature Pyramid Fusion and graph attention for LGG/HGG prediction, and a Cross-Modal Attention Transformer with supervised contrastive learning for subtype discrimination. The three stages are jointly optimized using an uncertainty-weighted multi-task objective, which facilitates cross-task feature reuse and reduces the need for manual loss-weight selection. Evaluation on BraTS-2020/2021, CPM-RadPath, and an institutional PGIMER cohort of 32 cases shows that CMHRNet achieves a whole-tumour Dice of 90.3%, LGG/HGG accuracy of 98.7%, and LGG-subtype F1 of 95.6 ± 0.4%. The segmentation performance is comparable to that of strong single-task baselines, while the integrated multi-task results, particularly for subtype classification, compare favourably with reported alternatives. Ablation studies, paired Wilcoxon tests, Grad-CAM visualizations, and failure-mode analysis support the contribution of feature fusion, graph attention, cross-modal attention, contrastive learning, and uncertainty weighting. CMHRNet therefore provides a unified radiology-pathology framework for hierarchical glioma assessment. Nevertheless, validation on larger multi-institutional cohorts is required before clinical deployment. Full multimodal operation depends on the availability of digitized histopathology; however, segmentation and grading remain available through the MRI-only fallback mode.

title: Cerebellar structural and electrophysiological alterations associated with neuropathic pain in mice.
abstract: The cerebellum is increasingly implicated in pain, yet direct electrophysiology in neuropathy is scarce. We tested whether sciatic nerve chronic constriction injury (CCI) alters cerebellar dynamics and structure. Adult male mice underwent CCI, von Frey testing, structural MRI, spontaneous LFP recordings in lobules IV-V, and spontaneous/evoked single-unit recordings under anesthesia. CCI produced rapid, persistent mechanical hypersensitivity. Deformation-based morphometry (DBM) revealed regional volumetric alterations including localized contractions in the IV-V cerebellar lobules. Spontaneous LFPs showed reduced absolute δ/θ power, with unchanged relative (normalized) power, while β/γ were unchanged. Multi-unit activity in CCI mice exhibited higher firing rates, shorter inter-spike intervals, and larger spike amplitudes. Peripheral stimulation evoked larger responses in CCI. Neuropathic pain is associated with structural remodeling, suppressed spontaneous slow-band cerebellar activity and enhanced unit/evoked responsiveness, which we interpret, as a working hypothesis, as a low-synchrony/high-gain operating regime. These structural and electrophysiological changes are candidate signatures that motivate future mechanistic and causal studies of cerebellar involvement in neuropathic pain.

title: Trajectory of influencing factors for post-thrombolysis early neurological deterioration and long-term functional recovery: insights from parallel explainable machine learning models.
abstract: Ischemic brain injury after intravenous thrombolysis (IVT) produces highly variable early deterioration and later disability, yet most prognostic models treat risk as a static, admission-only construct. This leaves the temporal reorganization of influencing factors poorly defined. In 609 consecutive patients treated with IVT alone within 4.5 h of last known well, we built three parallel explainable machine-learning models for 24-hour early neurological deterioration (END), poor function at 1 week, and poor function at 3 months. Stage-specific predictor sets followed the information actually available at each decision point, while an identical analytical pipeline (multi-method feature selection, Bayesian optimization, and synthetic minority oversampling) kept the comparisons methodologically aligned. Cross-validated areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve were 0.742, 0.831 and 0.914. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis showed a coherent trajectory after ischemic injury: metabolic load and early infarct burden (Alberta Stroke Program Early CT Score) dominated the hyperacute window; baseline National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale score and intracranial hemorrhage rose in the subacute window; discharge disposition, age and large-vessel occlusion dominated chronic outcome. A glucose × stroke-severity interaction further indicated that metabolic stress is not uniform across severity strata. These results provide a computational description of how clinically measurable factors re-weight over time after reperfusion, and they support phase-specific management of post-ischemic recovery.

title: Methylphenidate-associated brain structural changes and neuroimaging predictors of treatment response in youth with ADHD: a systematic review.
abstract: Background Methylphenidate (MPH) is a psychostimulant widely prescribed to children with attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD). Although its clinical efficacy is well established, its lasting effects on the developing brain remain unclear. Objective This systematic review aimed to examine associations between long-term MPH treatment and brain structure in children and adolescents with ADHD using structural magnetic resonance imaging (sMRI) and diffusion tensor imaging (DTI), distinguishing longitudinal treatment-effect studies from cross-sectional medication-history comparisons and baseline neuroimaging predictors of treatment response. Methods A systematic search was conducted in MEDLINE and Embase databases. Studies were included if they investigated structural brain changes (gray matter volume, white matter integrity and cortical thickness) after at least four weeks of MPH treatment in children with ADHD. Data extraction and quality assessment were performed using the NIH quality assessment tool. Results Eight studies met the inclusion criteria: three longitudinal studies using repeated MRI to assess within-subject treatment effects, two cross-sectional comparisons based on medication history, and three studies using baseline neuroimaging to predict subsequent treatment response. Greater putamen volume was associated with medication status ad volume with better treatment response in the cross-sectional and predictive analyses, while cortical effects were less consistent and mainly age-dependent in frontal areas. White matter findings were subtle and inconsistent across studies, and cortical thickness evidence-limited to one study-suggests short-term, possibly transient effects in children. Conclusion MPH treatment is associated l with age-dependent differences in brain structure in children and adolescents with ADHD; however, the limited number of included studies varied substantially in design, (cross-sectional and predictive studies alongside longitudinal treatment-effect studies), methodology, and reported outcomes, making firm causal conclusions difficult. Future research should prioritize larger, standardized, long-term longitudinal studies that account for developmental factors.

title: Multisystem assessment of white matter tracts in amyotrophic lateral sclerosis using NODDI and TractSeg.
abstract: Background Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) is a multisystem neurodegenerative disorder affecting motor, cognitive, and sensory networks. Conventional diffusion MRI lacks specificity for complex white matter pathology. This study combined neurite orientation dispersion and density imaging (NODDI) with automated fiber segmentation (TractSeg) to systematically evaluate microstructural alterations across multiple white matter pathways in a single ALS cohort. Methods We combined NODDI with automated TractSeg fiber segmentation in 83 sporadic ALS patients and 59 healthy controls. NODDI metrics (NDI, ODI, ISOVF) were extracted from 98 nodes along 19 tracts. Group comparisons used ANCOVA with FDR correction (q < 0.05). Results The left corticospinal tract (CST) showed ODI elevation and NDI reduction, and the right CST showed more extensive injury with ODI elevation, widespread NDI reduction, and ISOVF elevation. The corpus callosum exhibited focal changes in the rostral body, the anterior midbody and the posterior midbody involving ODI, NDI, and ISOVF. Among cerebellar motor, visuospatial processing, and limbic pathways, only the right superior longitudinal fasciculus II showed ISOVF elevation. Visual and language pathways predominantly showed ISOVF elevation, with additional NDI elevation in the right optic radiation and left arcuate fasciculus. Conclusions This study demonstrates asymmetric, pathway-selective white matter pathology in ALS. Focal damage in the mid-body of the corpus callosum supports its role as a hub for interhemispheric disease propagation. Evidence of both degeneration and possible compensatory neurite reorganization in visual and language pathways further establishes ALS as a multisystem network disorder. NODDI combined with TractSeg offers biologically specific imaging biomarkers for disease monitoring and clinical subtyping.

title: Distance-resolved diffusion-perfusion profiling of the Peri-enhancing tumor-brain Interface reveals entity-specific patterns in glioblastoma and contrast-enhancing Oligodendroglioma.
abstract: Purpose Contrast-enhancing diffuse gliomas may overlap visually with glioblastoma on standard MRI despite distinct molecular background, clinical course, and prognosis. This study investigated whether the peri-enhancing zone contains diffusion-perfusion differences between IDH-wildtype glioblastoma and contrast-enhancing IDH-mutant, 1p/19q-codeleted oligodendroglioma. Methods Treatment-naïve patients diagnosed between 2022 and 2024 underwent preoperative 3 T MRI including diffusion-weighted imaging and dynamic susceptibility contrast perfusion MRI. The contrast-enhancing tumor core and surrounding peri-enhancing zone (PEZ) were segmented using a distance-resolved three-dimensional framework. Peri-enhancing tissue was further stratified according to FLAIR signal status. Apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC) and cerebral blood volume (CBV) across PEZ layers were compared between tumor entities using three-dimensional volumetric compartment analysis, linear mixed-effects modeling of distance-resolved profiles, and receiver operating characteristic analysis. Results The final cohort included 72 patients (48 glioblastomas, 24 contrast-enhancing oligodendrogliomas). Tumor core volume and ADC did not differ between groups. In contrast, peri-enhancing diffusion-perfusion patterns showed entity-specific differences. The most pronounced differences were observed in the FLAIR-hyperintense peri-enhancing zone, where glioblastomas demonstrated progressively increasing ADC and decreasing CBV with increasing distance from the enhancing core, whereas oligodendrogliomas showed comparatively stable ADC and CBV profiles. Slope-based analysis of FLAIR-hyperintense peri-enhancing tissue provided the strongest discrimination between entities, with AUCs of 0.80 for ADC slope and 0.86 for CBV slope. Conclusions Quantitative profiling of the FLAIR-hyperintense peri-enhancing zone captures diffusion-perfusion differences beyond the enhancing core and may provide an imaging signature of the more aggressive peritumoral microenvironment of glioblastoma.
originalAbstract:
Purpose

Contrast-enhancing diffuse gliomas may overlap visually with glioblastoma on standard MRI despite distinct molecular background, clinical course, and prognosis. This study investigated whether the peri-enhancing zone contains diffusion-perfusion differences between IDH-wildtype glioblastoma and contrast-enhancing IDH-mutant, 1p/19q-codeleted oligodendroglioma.

Methods

Treatment-naïve patients diagnosed between 2022 and 2024 underwent preoperative 3 T MRI including diffusion-weighted imaging and dynamic susceptibility contrast perfusion MRI. The contrast-enhancing tumor core and surrounding peri-enhancing zone (PEZ) were segmented using a distance-resolved three-dimensional framework. Peri-enhancing tissue was further stratified according to FLAIR signal status. Apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC) and cerebral blood volume (CBV) across PEZ layers were compared between tumor entities using three-dimensional volumetric compartment analysis, linear mixed-effects modeling of distance-resolved profiles, and receiver operating characteristic analysis.

Results

The final cohort included 72 patients (48 glioblastomas, 24 contrast-enhancing oligodendrogliomas). Tumor core volume and ADC did not differ between groups. In contrast, peri-enhancing diffusion-perfusion patterns showed entity-specific differences. The most pronounced differences were observed in the FLAIR-hyperintense peri-enhancing zone, where glioblastomas demonstrated progressively increasing ADC and decreasing CBV with increasing distance from the enhancing core, whereas oligodendrogliomas showed comparatively stable ADC and CBV profiles. Slope-based analysis of FLAIR-hyperintense peri-enhancing tissue provided the strongest discrimination between entities, with AUCs of 0.80 for ADC slope and 0.86 for CBV slope.

Conclusions

Quantitative profiling of the FLAIR-hyperintense peri-enhancing zone captures diffusion-perfusion differences beyond the enhancing core and may provide an imaging signature of the more aggressive peritumoral microenvironment of glioblastoma.

title: In vivo probabilistic atlas mapping reveals brainstem nuclei volume increases in idiopathic REM sleep behavior disorder.
abstract: Objective Idiopathic rapid eye movement sleep behavior disorder (iRBD) serves as a key prodromal marker of synucleinopathies, and its core symptoms are closely associated with brainstem pathology. Nevertheless, in vivo imaging research on brainstem nuclei in iRBD patients is still limited due to methodological constraints. This study aimed to explore volume changes of brainstem nuclei in iRBD patients via a fine-grained probabilistic atlas, and analyze their clinical correlations and diagnostic value. Methods We enrolled 3D T1-weighted MRI data of 178 iRBD patients and 111 healthy controls from the PPMI database. After preprocessing, 54 brainstem nuclei were segmented using the Brainstem Navigator atlas, and their relative volumes were compared between groups with multiple comparison correction. Correlation analyses with clinical scales and ROC analyses were conducted for nuclei with significant inter-group differences. Results Compared to HCs, iRBD patients presented significantly enlarged relative volumes in the left cuneiform nucleus, left lateral parabrachial nucleus, and left superior medullary reticular formation. The volumes of the latter two nuclei were positively correlated with RBDSQ scores and related to autonomic, affective and cognitive indicators. The AUC of single nucleus for iRBD diagnosis ranged from 0.607 to 0.637, while the combined model reached 0.674. Conclusion These findings confirm volumetric enlargement in specific brainstem nuclei of iRBD patients, suggesting early pathological remodeling in these regions. They clarify the brainstem structural basis of iRBD symptoms and suggest that brainstem nuclei volumes, with moderate discriminative performance, may serve as supplementary imaging markers to complement clinical assessments in iRBD.

title: Relationship between integrated myocardial flow reserve and obstructive coronary artery disease and major adverse cardiac events: Findings from the multicenter REFINE PET Registry.
abstract: Introduction Although myocardial flow reserve (MFR) is a powerful marker of prognosis in patients undergoing positron emission tomography myocardial perfusion imaging (PET MPI), MFR cannot distinguish between epicardial and microvascular disease. Integrated MFR (iMFR) has been proposed to better detect epicardial coronary artery disease (CAD) by combining MFR with focal perfusion abnormalities. Methods We studied 34,761 patients as part of the REFINE PET registry of patients undergoing 82Rb or 13N-ammonia PET MPI. A subset of the above population without prior CAD (N=2,869) had a diagnostic angiogram within 180 days of PET MPI. Regions with an MFR <2 and a regional perfusion defect by total perfusion deficit (TPD) were defined as 'focally impaired' on a pixel by pixel basis. Regions with an MFR <2 without a regional perfusion defect were defined as 'diffusely impaired'. We also evaluated a separate angiographic cohort imaged with a third tracer, 18F-flurpiridaz, in the Flurpiridaz-301 trial (N=231). iMFR metrics were evaluated for the prediction of obstructive CAD and major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE). Results Of the 34,761 registry patients, 9,782 (28%) experienced MACE over a median follow-up of 3.8 years. In the angiographic cohort, 1,597 of 2,869 patients (56%) had obstructive CAD. For the diagnosis of obstructive CAD, the extent of focally impaired myocardium had an AUC of 0.77 (95% CI 0.75-0.79), outperforming conventional minimal-segment MFR (AUC 0.73, 95% CI 0.71-0.74, P<0.001), but did not differ significantly from ischemic TPD or physician visual scoring. For the prediction of MACE, the extent of diffusely impaired myocardium provided the most prognostic information in multivariable Cox models (adjusted HR per SD 1.35, 95% CI 1.32-1.38; C-statistic 0.723), compared with global MFR (C-statistic 0.722) and focally impaired myocardium (C-statistic 0.711). Conclusion The extent of focally impaired myocardium by iMFR outperformed conventional MFR for the diagnosis of obstructive CAD but performed similarly to ischemic TPD and physician visual scoring. For the prediction of MACE, the extent of diffusely impaired myocardium provided more prognostic information than focally impaired myocardium or global MFR.

title: Influence of preoperative and intraoperative variables on refractive error in patients undergoing phacovitrectomy.
abstract: Introduction and objectives Phacovitrectomy has been associated with a postoperative myopic shift, potentially resulting from inaccuracies in intraocular lens (IOL) power calculation due to anatomical changes following vitrectomy. This study evaluated postoperative refractive error (RE) and identified pre- and intraoperative factors influencing refractive outcomes after phacovitrectomy. Materials and methods A retrospective review of 311 patients who underwent uncomplicated phacovitrectomy between October 2022 and December 2023 was performed. Preoperative variables included demographic characteristics, diagnosis, axial length, keratometry, anterior chamber depth, biometry method, and IOL calculation formula. Tamponade type was recorded intraoperatively. The primary outcome was RE, defined as the postoperative achieved spherical equivalent (SE) minus the predicted SE based on the implanted IOL power, measured at 1 and 3 months. Results The mean postoperative SE was -0.828 ± 1.045 D at 1 month and -0.840 ± 0.981 D at 3 months. Mean RE was -0.544 D and -0.556 D, respectively, with no significant difference between visits (p = 0.756). Nearly half of patients (48.5%) had a myopic shift greater than -0.50 D. Rhegmatogenous retinal detachment (RRD) showed the greatest myopic shift (-1.026 D). The combination of optical biometry and Barrett Universal II was associated with lower RE than ultrasound biometry and SRK/T (p < 0.05). Tamponade type showed no significant association with RE. Conclusions Phacovitrectomy was associated with a consistent postoperative myopic shift. The combination of optical biometry and Barrett Universal II provided greater refractive accuracy. Patients with RRD showed a greater tendency toward myopic shift. These findings support a more individualized approach to optimize refractive outcomes following phacovitrectomy.

title: A Teleglaucoma Screening System for Individuals at Risk of Open-Angle Glaucoma: Long-Term Clinical Outcomes and Comparative Cost Analysis.
abstract: Purpose To evaluate the clinical effectiveness and economic impact of a teleglaucoma screening program for individuals at increased risk of developing open-angle glaucoma (OAG). Design Prospective cohort study with retrospective evaluation of long-term clinical outcomes and comparative cost analysis. Participants Consecutive individuals with risk factors for OAG enrolled in a teleglaucoma screening program between 2020 and 2022. Methods A targeted teleglaucoma screening program was implemented within the Donostialdea Integrated Healthcare Organization (Gipuzkoa, Spain). Consecutive individuals with risk factors for OAG were included. The teleglaucoma assessment included best-corrected visual acuity, non-contact tonometry, pachymetry, and peripapillary retinal nerve fiber layer optical coherence tomography (pRNFL-OCT), performed by an optometrist and reviewed asynchronously by glaucoma specialists. Findings consistent with glaucoma or suspicious for glaucoma were considered positive screening results, whereas ocular hypertension (OHT) or the absence of abnormalities were considered negative screening results. Clinical effectiveness was evaluated through analysis of glaucoma-related diagnoses recorded using ICD-10 codes during a five-year follow-up period. A comparative cost analysis was conducted from a societal perspective. Patient satisfaction was assessed using the Client Satisfaction Questionnaire (CSQ-8). Main outcomes measures Agreement between teleglaucoma classifications and glaucoma-related ICD-10 diagnoses recorded during follow-up, diagnostic performance indicators, patient satisfaction, and costs. Results A total of 1,112 patients were included (mean age 60.2 years), of whom 63.1% were women. Positive screening results were identified in 8.2% of participants. Overall agreement between the teleglaucoma assessment and follow-up ICD-10 diagnoses was 92.6%, with a mean follow-up of 3.7 ± 0.8 years. Sensitivity was 64.5%, specificity 93.4%, and negative predictive value 98.9%. Patient satisfaction was high, with a mean score of 8.5/10. The economic analysis demonstrated a 50% reduction in total costs compared with conventional care, with a cost per patient of €40.7 versus €81.2. Conclusions The teleglaucoma system demonstrated a high ability to rule out disease among individuals at risk of glaucoma, reduced costs and achieved high patient satisfaction. However, moderate sensitivity and the use of coded clinical records as the reference standard should be considered.

title: External validation of a deep-learning algorithm for perimetric glaucoma detection on color fundus photographs in the Rotterdam Study.
abstract: Purpose To externally validate a deep-learning (DL) algorithm detecting perimetric glaucoma on color fundus photographs (CFPs) in a population-based cohort. Design External validation in a prospective population-based cohort. Participants Participants aged 50-80 years from three Rotterdam Study cohorts. Methods We applied the winning Artificial Intelligence for Robust Glaucoma Screening (AIROGS) challenge algorithm, trained on 101,442 macula-centered CFPs to detect referable presumed perimetric glaucoma. Performance was assessed at eye and participant level, with participant-level cluster bootstrap confidence intervals. Misclassified cases underwent qualitative review. Longitudinal detection was evaluated by Kaplan-Meier analysis. Additionally, paired analyses compared macula- with disc-centered CFPs. A post-hoc analysis examined the effect of image quality on positive predictive value (PPV). Main outcome measures Sensitivity at 95% specificity, area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (ROC-AUC), partial AUC (pAUC) for 90-100% specificity, PPV, and precision-recall AUC (PR-AUC). Results Among 19,088 eyes (9,837 participants), 201 eyes (1.1%) had perimetric glaucoma. At eye level, sensitivity at 95% specificity was 70.6% (95% CI: 63.8-76.8), with an ROC-AUC of 0.911 (95% CI: 0.887-0.934) and a PR-AUC of 0.343 (95% CI: 0.274-0.427). At participant level, sensitivity was 68.8% (95% CI: 61.8-75.9) and ROC-AUC 0.909 (95% CI: 0.882-0.934). Overall, this resulted in 5.1 referrals per detected glaucoma case. True positives showed more advanced visual field damage than false negatives (median mean deviation -10.8 vs -5.8 dB; P < 0.001). Among true positives with prior imaging, 33 of 61 (54%) were flagged before conversion, typically 4-7 years before diagnosis. Discrimination in the 90-100% specificity range was higher for disc- than macula-centered CFPs (pAUC 0.860 vs 0.802; P = 0.003). PPV improved substantially after excluding CFPs with incomplete optic nerve head (ONH) visibility. Conclusions The DL-algorithm achieved meaningful discrimination for perimetric glaucoma in an external population-based dataset. Correctly identified cases were frequently flagged at an earlier examination, years before the perimetric diagnosis. Despite having been trained exclusively on macula-centered CFPs, the DL-algorithm showed no loss of discriminative performance on disc-centered CFPs. Incomplete ONH visibility was an important source of false positives. These findings support CFP-based deep learning as a scalable triage tool for glaucoma screening and highlight image acquisition standards for implementation.

Methods

We applied the winning Artificial Intelligence for Robust Glaucoma Screening (AIROGS) challenge algorithm, trained on 101,442 macula-centered CFPs to detect referable presumed perimetric glaucoma. Performance was assessed at eye and participant level, with participant-level cluster bootstrap confidence intervals. Misclassified cases underwent qualitative review. Longitudinal detection was evaluated by Kaplan-Meier analysis. Additionally, paired analyses compared macula- with disc-centered CFPs. A post-hoc analysis examined the effect of image quality on positive predictive value (PPV).

Main outcome measures

Sensitivity at 95% specificity, area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (ROC-AUC), partial AUC (pAUC) for 90-100% specificity, PPV, and precision-recall AUC (PR-AUC).

Results

Among 19,088 eyes (9,837 participants), 201 eyes (1.1%) had perimetric glaucoma. At eye level, sensitivity at 95% specificity was 70.6% (95% CI: 63.8-76.8), with an ROC-AUC of 0.911 (95% CI: 0.887-0.934) and a PR-AUC of 0.343 (95% CI: 0.274-0.427). At participant level, sensitivity was 68.8% (95% CI: 61.8-75.9) and ROC-AUC 0.909 (95% CI: 0.882-0.934). Overall, this resulted in 5.1 referrals per detected glaucoma case. True positives showed more advanced visual field damage than false negatives (median mean deviation -10.8 vs -5.8 dB; P < 0.001). Among true positives with prior imaging, 33 of 61 (54%) were flagged before conversion, typically 4-7 years before diagnosis. Discrimination in the 90-100% specificity range was higher for disc- than macula-centered CFPs (pAUC 0.860 vs 0.802; P = 0.003). PPV improved substantially after excluding CFPs with incomplete optic nerve head (ONH) visibility.

Conclusions

The DL-algorithm achieved meaningful discrimination for perimetric glaucoma in an external population-based dataset. Correctly identified cases were frequently flagged at an earlier examination, years before the perimetric diagnosis. Despite having been trained exclusively on macula-centered CFPs, the DL-algorithm showed no loss of discriminative performance on disc-centered CFPs. Incomplete ONH visibility was an important source of false positives. These findings support CFP-based deep learning as a scalable triage tool for glaucoma screening and highlight image acquisition standards for implementation.

title: Diagnostic orthodontic traction with a miniscrew for stacked horizontal impaction of the mandibular second and third molars followed by fixed orthodontic appliance involving premolar extractions in a young adult presenting with Class II incisal biprotrusion: A case report.
abstract: Stacked horizontal impaction of the mandibular second and third molars presents complex clinical challenges because of uncertainty regarding tooth preservation, uprighting mechanics, and the possibility of ankylosis. A 23-year-old male presented with a skeletal Class II malocclusion, excessive overjet, and moderate crowding. Radiographic examination revealed stacked horizontal impactions of the left mandibular second and third molars. To evaluate the orthodontic responsiveness of the impacted mandibular left second molar before irreversible extraction decisions were made, diagnostic orthodontic traction using a miniscrew was performed. Following extraction of the mandibular left third molar, a miniscrew was placed distal to the impacted second molar to initiate orthodontic traction. This diagnostic approach confirmed responsiveness of the impacted second molar to orthodontic force and guided definitive treatment planning. Once orthodontic tooth movement had been confirmed, the mandibular left second premolar were extracted, allowing mesial movement of the mandibular left first molar and successful uprighting of the impacted second molar. A stable Class I molar relationship and functional occlusion were achieved. Clinical and radiographic evaluation after a 2-year retention period demonstrated excellent occlusal stability and healthy periodontal conditions. This case demonstrates that diagnostic orthodontic traction using a miniscrew can provide a useful staged decision-making strategy for managing severely impacted mandibular second molar with uncertain prognosis.

title: Predictive Factors of Facial Paralysis in Vestibular Schwannoma Surgery: A 2-Year Prospective Cohort Study.
abstract: Introduction Preservation of facial nerve (FN) function remains a major challenge in vestibular schwannoma (VS) surgery. Identifying reliable prognostic factors, particularly those available intraoperatively, may improve surgical decision-making and long-term functional outcomes. Materials and methods A prospective cohort study including 42 patients undergoing VS surgery between June 2022 and June 2024 was conducted. Clinical, radiological, surgical, and intraoperative neurophysiological variables were analyzed, including the compound muscle action potential (CMAP) amplitude and stimulation threshold recorded at the fundus and cerebellopontine angle (CPA) before and after tumor resection. FN function was assessed using the House-Brackmann (HB) and Sunnybrook scales up to 12 months postoperatively. Univariate analysis, ROC curves, and multivariate logistic regression were performed to identify predictors of one-year facial outcome." Results At 12 months, acceptable FN function (HB I-III) was observed in 85.7% of patients. Univariate analysis showed significant associations for extent of resection (p = 0.024), intraoperative FN condition (p = 0.018), immediate (p = 0.006) and delayed oculoplastic surgery (p < 0.001), extracanalicular tumor size (p = 0.016), and age (p = 0.030). Neurophysiological predictors included presurgical fundus CMAP amplitude (p = 0.021), presurgical CPA CMAP amplitude (p = 0.008), presurgical CPA stimulation threshold (p = 0.018), and postsurgical CPA CMAP amplitude (p = 0.002). In multivariate analysis, only postsurgical CPA CMAP amplitude remained independently associated with one-year outcome (OR = 0.993; 95% CI 0.987-1.000; p = 0.041). Discussion Facial nerve outcomes appear to depend on the interaction between tumor characteristics, surgical manipulation, and intraoperative nerve integrity. Neurophysiological monitoring provides objective real-time information that may help surgeons balance tumor resection with functional preservation and anticipate postoperative recovery. Conclusions Postsurgical CPA CMAP amplitude was an independent predictor of one-year FN outcome, supporting the role of intraoperative electrophysiological monitoring in guiding FN-preserving surgical strategies.

title: Quantitative 3D mapping of the integrated sweat duct-microvasculature unit via fingerprint-guided photoacoustic/ultrasound microscopy.
abstract: Cutaneous thermoregulation relies on coordinated interactions between sweat ducts and the dermal microvasculature. However, single-modality imaging cannot simultaneously visualize and characterize this functional coupling. Here, we present a fingerprint-guided dual-modal photoacoustic/ultrasound (PA/US) microscopy framework for three-dimensional mapping of the integrated sweat duct-microvasculature unit (SDMU). This strategy combines high-frequency ultrasound with deep learning (U-Net) to extract sweat duct and fingerprint features; simultaneously, the distribution of microvasculature in PA imaging is accurately localized via structural similarity index metrix (SSIM) analysis of depth-dependent melanin. Crucially, fingerprint-guided non-rigid registration eliminates motion artifacts, enabling dynamic tracking of the identical SDMUs during physiological processes. Quantitative analysis indicated that the functional coupling of microvasculature is highly concentrated within a 75-micrometer radius around sweat ducts, and that the expansion of US-visible sweat ductal structures exhibits a strong positive correlation with microvascular recruitment. Furthermore, a physiology-informed operational dual-response criterion further revealed significant spatial heterogeneity in functional activation, thereby facilitating robust discrimination between activated and unactivated SDMUs. This study not only established the SDMU as a quantifiable functional unit for studying cutaneous thermoregulation, but also highlighted its potential as a candidate biomarker for assessing diabetes-associated neurovascular dysfunction.

title: Serum neurofilament light chain and striatal specific binding ratio predict motor and cognitive outcomes in tremor dominant versus postural instability/gait difficulty subtypes of Parkinson's disease.
abstract: Background Parkinson's disease (PD) exhibits clinical heterogeneity between tremor-dominant (TD) and postural instability/gait difficulty (PIGD) subtypes. Whether striatal dopaminergic denervation mediates associations between serum neurofilament light chain (NfL), a marker of neuroaxonal injury, and disease progression remains unclear. Methods We analyzed 264 patients with de novo PD (TD, n = 177; PIGD, n = 80) and 132 healthy controls (HCs) from the Parkinson's Progression Markers Initiative (PPMI). Baseline NfL and dopamine transporter (DAT) single-photon emission computed tomography-derived striatal specific binding ratios (SBRs) were assessed. Spearman correlations, linear mixed-effects models, and mediation analyses examined cross-sectional relationships, five-year clinical outcomes, and mediation. Results Serum NfL was higher in PD than in controls (P = 0.002), without significant subtype differences (P = 0.661). Higher NfL correlated with worse motor and cognitive function and lower caudate SBR (r = -0.270, P < 0.001). Baseline NfL predicted five-year motor deterioration (MDS-UPDRS III: β = 0.239, P = 0.043) and cognitive decline (MoCA: β = -0.063, P = 0.037). Subtype analyses associated NfL with cognitive decline in TD (β = -0.076, P = 0.031) and motor deterioration in PIGD (β = 0.564, P = 0.004). Caudate, anterior caudate, and posterior caudate SBRs significantly mediated associations with both outcomes (indirect effects, P < 0.05). Conclusions Baseline serum NfL predicts five-year deterioration with subtype-specific patterns. Caudate SBRs partially mediate these associations, while residual cognitive associations suggest possible extrastriatal involvement. Integrating NfL, DAT imaging, and clinical subtypes may help identify patients at risk of rapid progression.

title: Hyperspectral Histopathology with Spectral-Spatial Multiple-Instance Learning for Acute Leukemia Classification.
abstract: Background Acute myeloid leukemia (AML) and acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL) may show overlapping morphology on bone-marrow trephine sections, while definitive ancillary testing is not always immediately available. We evaluated whether microscopic hyperspectral imaging (HSI) combined with patient-level spectral-spatial deep learning could support differentiation of AML, ALL, and normal marrow. Methods This retrospective single-center study included 78 patients (26 AML, 26 ALL, and 26 normal marrow). H&E-stained bone-marrow trephine sections were imaged across 400-1000 nm. Patient-level nested stratified five-fold cross-validation was defined before region-of-interest (ROI) sampling to prevent information leakage. We developed HemaSpec-MIL, a new hierarchical spectral-spatial multiple-instance learning algorithm and a major methodological output of this study. The framework combines multi-scale spectral encoding, morphology encoding, bidirectional cross-attention, and gated multiple-instance aggregation to generate patient-level probabilities. The primary endpoint was pooled out-of-fold macro-AUC. Results HemaSpec-MIL achieved a pooled out-of-fold accuracy of 0.897, macro-F1 of 0.897, and macro-AUC of 0.957. One-vs-rest AUCs were 0.964 for AML, 0.945 for ALL, and 0.962 for normal marrow. Performance exceeded spectral-only, morphology-only, 3D-CNN, Vision Transformer, and spectral Transformer baselines. Ablation analysis supported complementary contributions from the spectral branch, morphology branch, cross-attention fusion, gated patient-level aggregation, and spectral augmentation. Conclusions Microscopic HSI combined with the newly developed HemaSpec-MIL framework enabled accurate internal differentiation of AML, ALL, and normal marrow while preserving wavelength- and tissue-level interpretability. Independent multicenter validation and acquisition harmonization are required before clinical translation.

title: Association of Scanning Laser Ophthalmoscopy-Derived Fundus Metrics with Corneal Remodeling after Transepithelial Photorefractive Keratectomy: A Retrospective Study.
abstract: Purpose To investigate the associations between preoperative fundus metrics and postoperative corneal remodeling following transepithelial photorefractive keratectomy (TransPRK). Methods This retrospective observational study included 103 patients (200 eyes) who underwent TransPRK. Corneal parameters were measured preoperatively and at 1, 3, and 6 months postoperatively. A screening strategy using two standardized metrics, A = SD(Δ)/SD(T₀) and B = median(|Δ|)/SD(T₀), was implemented to identify high-variability corneal parameters, where Δ denotes the change from preoperative baseline, SD(Δ) the standard deviation of the change, and SD(T₀) the preoperative standard deviation of the same parameter. Patient-clustered generalized estimating equation (GEE) models adjusted for age, sex, preoperative spherical equivalent (SE), and preoperative corneal epithelial thickness (CET) were used to examine the associations between retained corneal parameters and preoperative fundus metrics, including fundus tessellation density (FTD), parapapillary atrophy (PPA) area, vertical cup-to-disc ratio (VCDR), and rim-to-disc area ratio (RDAR). The Benjamini-Hochberg (BH) procedure was applied to control the false discovery rate. Results Twenty-seven corneal parameters were identified as high-variability parameters, most showing their greatest change at 1 month postoperatively. VCDR was positively associated with changes in TNP K1 and TCRP K1 (standardized β = 0.065 to 0.076), and these associations remained significant after BH correction at both 1 and 3 months (all q < 0.05). RDAR was negatively associated with the same parameters in these generalized estimating equation (GEE) models (standardized β = -0.071 to -0.060) and remained significant at 3 months postoperatively (q < 0.05); PPA area and FTD were not significantly associated with any corneal parameter. Conclusions Preoperative VCDR was significantly associated with corneal changes after TransPRK, independent of surgical parameters, whereas the association for RDAR was partly attenuated after adjustment. These findings suggest that posterior segment structure may influence anterior corneal remodeling through biomechanical pathways, though further prospective validation is warranted.

Methods

This retrospective observational study included 103 patients (200 eyes) who underwent TransPRK. Corneal parameters were measured preoperatively and at 1, 3, and 6 months postoperatively. A screening strategy using two standardized metrics, A = SD(Δ)/SD(T₀) and B = median(|Δ|)/SD(T₀), was implemented to identify high-variability corneal parameters, where Δ denotes the change from preoperative baseline, SD(Δ) the standard deviation of the change, and SD(T₀) the preoperative standard deviation of the same parameter. Patient-clustered generalized estimating equation (GEE) models adjusted for age, sex, preoperative spherical equivalent (SE), and preoperative corneal epithelial thickness (CET) were used to examine the associations between retained corneal parameters and preoperative fundus metrics, including fundus tessellation density (FTD), parapapillary atrophy (PPA) area, vertical cup-to-disc ratio (VCDR), and rim-to-disc area ratio (RDAR). The Benjamini-Hochberg (BH) procedure was applied to control the false discovery rate.

Results

Twenty-seven corneal parameters were identified as high-variability parameters, most showing their greatest change at 1 month postoperatively. VCDR was positively associated with changes in TNP K1 and TCRP K1 (standardized β = 0.065 to 0.076), and these associations remained significant after BH correction at both 1 and 3 months (all q < 0.05). RDAR was negatively associated with the same parameters in these generalized estimating equation (GEE) models (standardized β = -0.071 to -0.060) and remained significant at 3 months postoperatively (q < 0.05); PPA area and FTD were not significantly associated with any corneal parameter.

Conclusions

Preoperative VCDR was significantly associated with corneal changes after TransPRK, independent of surgical parameters, whereas the association for RDAR was partly attenuated after adjustment. These findings suggest that posterior segment structure may influence anterior corneal remodeling through biomechanical pathways, though further prospective validation is warranted.

title: Changes in Retinal and Choroidal Thickness and OCTA-Derived Vessel Density after Anti-VEGF Therapy for Diabetic Macular Edema.
abstract: Purpose To evaluate the effects of anti-vascular endothelial growth factor (anti-VEGF) therapy on retinal and choroidal thickness and optical coherence tomography angiography (OCTA)-derived retinal vessel density in patients with diabetic macular edema (DME), with prespecified primary outcomes and exploratory OCTA outcomes controlled for multiplicity. Methods This retrospective clinical study included 45 patients (45 eyes) with DME treated at the Affiliated Eye Hospital of Chengdu University of Traditional Chinese Medicine between January 2023 and January 2026. All patients received three consecutive monthly intravitreal injections of conbercept (0.5 mg/0.05 mL). OCTA examinations were performed at baseline, 1 month, and 3 months after the first injection to measure central macular thickness (CMT), subfoveal choroidal thickness (SFCT), vessel density of the superficial capillary plexus (SCP) and deep capillary plexus (DCP), foveal avascular zone (FAZ) area, and parafoveal vessel density at 300 μm (FD-300). Best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA) was also recorded. BCVA, CMT, and SFCT were prespecified as primary outcomes. All OCTA-derived parameters were exploratory and were corrected using the Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate (FDR) procedure across 12 comparisons. Results The study included 45 patients (45 eyes), comprising 21 male patients (21 eyes) and 24 female patients (24 eyes), with a mean age of 54.44 ± 12.09 years. The mean duration of diabetes was 13.33 ± 4.36 years, and the baseline HbA1c level was 7.36% ± 1.73%. At 3 months, BCVA significantly improved from 0.65 ± 0.45 to 0.33 ± 0.27 logMAR (P < 0.001). CMT significantly decreased from 392.02 ± 139.90 μm at baseline to 322.26 ± 85.60 μm at 3 months (P = 0.002 vs baseline; overall P = 0.006). SFCT significantly decreased from 260.51 ± 106.16 μm at baseline to 243.80 ± 91.15 μm at 3 months (P = 0.020 vs baseline; overall P = 0.037). In exploratory OCTA analyses, foveal SCP and DCP vessel density showed numerical increases at 3 months (SCP: 26.88 ± 6.71% to 29.94 ± 7.32%; DCP: 30.02 ± 6.46% to 33.54 ± 6.74%), with uncorrected main-effect P values of 0.041 and 0.043, respectively. However, neither remained statistically significant after FDR correction (adjusted P = 0.224 and 0.256, respectively). No significant changes were observed in parafoveal SCP or DCP vessel density, FAZ area, or FD-300 (all FDR-adjusted P > 0.05). No serious adverse events occurred. Conclusion Anti-VEGF therapy significantly improved BCVA and reduced CMT and SFCT over 3 months. Foveal SCP and DCP vessel density increased numerically, but these exploratory OCTA changes did not survive FDR correction and may reflect edema-resolution-related segmentation effects; they are hypothesis-generating only. Longer prospective studies with standardized OCTA metrics are needed.

title: Culturally tailored breast cancer screening resources: South Asian women's and healthcare providers' perspectives in Victoria Australia.
abstract: Organisational and information gaps in culturally appropriate breast health information can contribute to inequities in breast cancer screening participation. The aim of the study was to explore the perspectives of South Asian women, General Practitioners (GPs), and non-primary healthcare providers (HCPs) to inform the development of targeted breast health information resources in Victoria. Semi-structured interviews were conducted with 25 South Asian women (Pakistani and Indian; aged 35-65 years) and 15 HCPs including nine GPs and six non-primary HCPs. Inductive and deductive thematic analysis was undertaken. Three major themes emerged: tailored breast health information, preferred formats, and community-based dissemination. Participants recommended concise, visually engaging one-page or digital resources in English, Urdu and Hindi explaining mammography and addressing pain, modesty, female staff availability and free screening. HCPs valued clinic-ready resources to support proactive discussions, while participants recommended dissemination through trusted community organisations, faith-based venues, ethnic media and community leaders. Digital or print materials were preferred by younger and older women respectively. Culturally and linguistically tailored resources may support breast screening discussions among South Asian women and healthcare providers. These findings provide a basis for co-designing and evaluating targeted resources, although their impact on breast screening participation remains to be established. Participants' preferences can inform multilingual print and digital resources for primary care and community settings. Their acceptability, feasibility and effects on screening participation require evaluation before wider implementation.

title: Functional lung avoidance planning with combined ventilation-perfusion imaging versus individual functional imaging in lung cancer radiotherapy.
abstract: Background and purpose Functional lung avoidance radiotherapy using four-dimensional computed tomography (4DCT) ventilation or single-photon emission computed tomography (SPECT) perfusion has been studied independently, however few studies have evaluated their combined use. The aim of this study was to examine whether integrating both modalities improved sparing of high functional lung (HFL) in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Materials and methods Forty-seven patients with NSCLC underwent 4DCT ventilation and SPECT perfusion imaging. One patient was excluded, leaving 46 for analysis. Functional lung maps were segmented into high, middle, and low functional lung. Four volumetric-modulated arc therapy (VMAT) plans using 6 MV photons per patient were generated: anatomical (A), ventilation-guided (V), perfusion-guided (Q), and combined ventilation-perfusion-guided (VQ). Dose-volume and dose-function metrics were compared among plans. Correlations between tumor proximity to HFL and dose reduction were assessed. Results All function-guided plans significantly reduced HFL dose compared with A plans ( p < 0.001). Among the function-guided plans, VQ plans yielded the lowest mean lung doses (MLDs) in high ventilated lung (VQ plans, 11.5 Gy; A plans, 12.4 Gy) and high perfused lung (VQ plans, 10.0 Gy; A plans, 11.1 Gy). Function-weighted metrics, including functional MLD, were also lowest with VQ plans, indicating improved functional lung sparing. Dose reduction correlated with tumor proximity to HFL, with the strongest associations observed at planning target volume expansions between 25 and 45 mm. Conclusions Integrating 4DCT ventilation and SPECT perfusion into radiotherapy planning improved functional lung sparing compared with anatomical or single-modality planning. Tumor proximity to functional lung influenced the magnitude of dose-volume benefits.

title: Bayesian deep learning framework to address multi-rater annotation uncertainty in prostate cancer magnetic resonance imaging segmentation.
abstract: Background and purpose Accurate prostate segmentation in magnetic resonance imaging is critical for prostate cancer radiotherapy, but manual annotation is time-consuming and exhibits high inter-rater variability. This study proposes a Bayesian deep learning framework that improves prostate segmentation under annotation noise and inter-rater variability while providing uncertainty estimation. Materials and methods Using the prostate cancer imaging dataset (140 subjects), simulated prostate annotations modeled boundary ambiguity, annotator subjectivity, and annotation tool-related artifacts across three scenarios: single rater with distinct simulated annotations (S1), majority-vote consensus from three raters (S2), and multi-annotation of all rater masks with majority voting (S3). The framework used Flipout convolutional layers for uncertainty estimation, trained with a combined Kullback-Leibler divergence and Focal Tversky loss. Bayesian learning was implemented first in a standard U-Net and then in nnU-Net to evaluate generalization across backbones. Comparisons included deterministic counterparts, Swin UNETR, and variants with Monte Carlo Dropout, Label Smoothing, and Test-Time Augmentation. Results Bayesian U-Net achieved Dice Similarity Coefficients of 0.730, 0.782, and 0.780 in S1, S2, and S3, respectively, and the lowest Expected Calibration Error in S1 (0.065). Bayesian nnU-Net achieved the highest Dice Similarity Coefficients among nnU-Net-based methods in all scenarios (0.879, 0.903, and 0.900) and the lowest Expected Calibration Error in all scenarios. Predictive uncertainty was consistently higher in incorrectly than in correctly segmented voxels. Conclusions Bayesian learning improved segmentation robustness under multi-rater noisy labels, across both U-Net and nnU-Net while providing voxel-wise uncertainty estimates and may support clinical decision-making and enhance treatment accuracy.

title: Treatment-position magnetic resonance imaging reduces bony-landmark co-registration error in head and neck radiotherapy.
abstract: Background and purpose Routine diagnostic magnetic resonance imaging is acquired without immobilisation, creating co-registration uncertainty with planning computed tomography. We quantified whether treatment-position imaging reduced bony-landmark co-registration error, and whether the benefit persisted after resampling and deformable refinement. Materials and methods Fifty patients with paired treatment-position and diagnostic magnetic resonance imaging were retrospectively analysed. Each magnetic resonance imaging dataset was separately registered to planning computed tomography. Mean Euclidean distance between corresponding bony landmarks on the computed tomography and magnetic resonance images was compared after rigid registration and after deformable refinement, using Holm-adjusted landmark-wise comparisons. Through-plane resampling was assessed in all 50 patients, and interobserver reproducibility in a 15-patient subset. Results Treatment-position imaging reduced mean Euclidean distance from 7.5 to 4.1 mm after rigid registration (difference 3.4 mm; 95% confidence interval 2.7-4.1; p = 2.0 × 10 -13 ). The benefit persisted after resampling (4.3 mm) and deformable refinement (3.4 versus 6.0 mm; difference 2.6 mm; 95% confidence interval 2.1-3.1; p = 7.1 × 10 -14 ), although refinement reduced the advantage by 0.8 mm (interaction p = 0.023). Each magnetic resonance imaging dataset was separately registered to planning computed tomography. title: Quantitative static contrast-enhanced phantom study to establish performance of advanced cone beam computed tomography for functional imaging applications.
abstract: Background and purpose Dynamic contrast-enhanced computed tomography (DCE-CT) is a quantitative imaging technique that measures vascular perfusion. Extending this to cone beam CT (CBCT) would enable functional measurements on radiotherapy machines. An advanced CBCT imaging solution, with enhanced image quality and rapid acquisitions, offers potential. However, the static quantitative and spatial performance of advanced CBCT relevant to DCE imaging has not been characterized. Materials and methods To address this, the image quality of advanced CBCT was compared with standard CBCT and CT using contrast-enhanced phantoms with DCE-specific characteristics not previously applied to CBCT. A contrast enhancement CT (CECT) phantom (acrylic cylinder with capsule inserts) and a humanoid phantom (human torso with a liver containing tumour-mimicking spheres) were imaged across different acquisition settings. Results Using the CECT phantom, advanced CBCT demonstrated improved CT number accuracy compared to standard CBCT (<23.9 vs. <78.9 HU) and greater CT number constancy (<8.4 vs. <12.9 HU). Iterative reconstruction on advanced CBCT offered improvements over filtered back-projection. Using the humanoid phantom, findings were confirmed with CT number accuracy (<7.1 vs. <42.8 HU), CT number variation (<11.3 vs. <49.8 HU) and volume accuracy (<128.8 vs. <1067.3 mm 3 ). Advanced CBCT achieved spatial resolutions of 2.3-5.0 lp/cm across different acquisitions and measurements, meeting the 5 lp/cm clinical benchmark under certain conditions. It also displayed stable CT number-density calibration. Conclusions Advanced CBCT compared to standard CBCT improved image quality, approaching CT-level performance. Findings demonstrated robust volume and contrast-specific quantification under DCE conditions, supporting further evaluation of functional CBCT.

title: Quantitative gamma-based evaluation of a novel four-dimensional computed tomography reconstruction algorithm for stack artifact reduction.
abstract: Background and purpose Four-dimensional computed tomography (4DCT) is essential for motion-resolved imaging in radiotherapy, but stack alignment artifacts caused by irregular breathing may compromise anatomical accuracy. This study established a quantitative framework to evaluate reconstruction differences between clinical reference reconstruction (CRR) and stack artifact-reduced reconstruction (SARR) and identify clinically relevant changes. Materials and methods Retrospective 4DCT datasets from 80 lung cancer patients were analyzed, comprising a rated cohort ( n = 30) and an independent control cohort ( n = 50). Geometric, intensity-based, and combined metrics, including gamma analysis, were calculated across ten respiratory phases for segmented organs-at-risk. Correlations with reader ratings identified metrics that best reflected clinically relevant reconstruction differences. Results Most similarity and intensity-based measures showed limited association with image quality differences (Pearson correlation coefficient r < 0.5). Gamma-based metrics demonstrated the strongest correlation, with relative gamma area > 0.3 reaching r ≈ 0.59 for phase-based data (95% confidence interval 0.30-0.79). Reconstruction differences were predominantly observed in the liver and lower lung lobes, consistent with respiratory motion, while the spinal cord showed minimal variation. Robust z-score thresholding enabled automated categorization of moderate and substantial deviations. In the control cohort, 12% showed substantial and 14% moderate changes for phase-based reconstructions. In the patient with the largest changes, the liver appeared as a double contour in the CRR and as a single contour in the SARR. Conclusions Gamma-based evaluation provided an objective method to detect and localize reconstruction differences in 4DCT, supporting transparent clinical implementation of advanced reconstruction algorithms in radiotherapy.

title: Artificial intelligence for computational placental analysis in global health: A rapid scoping review of opportunities, challenges, and clinical translation in low-resource settings.
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) could support placental examination where diagnostic resources are limited, but evidence for clinical deployment remains uncertain. We conducted a rapid scoping review, reported in accordance with PRISMA-ScR, of PubMed, IEEE Xplore, and the ACM Digital Library for studies published between 1 January 2015 and 31 December 2025. Of 1,441 unique records screened, 124 met the eligibility criteria, and 36 additionally demonstrated applicability to low-resource settings and were charted at full text. Most charted studies analysed ultrasound (27 of 36) and addressed segmentation and classification tasks using convolutional architectures, principally U-Net and its variants. Digital photography, a relatively accessible post-delivery modality, was analysed in six studies; 13 studies used data from low- or middle-income countries. While recent work has begun to explore multimodal learning, self-supervised approaches, and model efficiency, key challenges persist, including limited labelled data, variability in imaging conditions, and a lack of standardised evaluation datasets and frameworks. We also identify critical gaps in real-world deployment: computational constraints were addressed in eight charted studies and on-device evaluation reported in one, evidence of clinical workflow integration was limited, and external or cross-site validation was reported in five. This review highlights the need for data-efficient, robust, and clinically grounded AI systems and outlines future directions towards scalable and equitable computational placental analysis in global health contexts.

title: MRI-based radiomics and deep learning for the prenatal diagnosis of Placenta Accreta Spectrum: a systematic review and exploratory meta-analysis.
abstract: Objective accuracy of Placenta Accreta Spectrum (PAS) diagnosis using conventional magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is still limited by subjective interpretation. Increasing evidence showed that radiomics and Deep Learning (DL) may improve diagnostic objectivity by extracting quantitative features from MRI data. This study aimed to synthesize the evidence on the diagnostic performance and clinical utility of these models. Methods a systematic review and meta-analysis was conducted following PRISMA-DTA guidelines and PRISMA 2020 recommendations: PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science databases from inception to December 2025. We searched for primary studies evaluating MRI-based radiomics or DL models for the binary diagnosis of PAS. Data were extracted to create 2 × 2 contingency tables and used a bivariate random-effects model to calculate pooled sensitivity, specificity, and to generate a summary ROC (SROC) curve. We assessed robustness via leave-one-out sensitivity analysis, and clinical utility using Fagan's nomogram and likelihood ratios. A secondary meta-analysis was performed for the prediction of postpartum hemorrhage (PPH) ≥1000 mL. Results twelve studies met the inclusion criteria (N = 1135 patients). The pooled sensitivity for PAS diagnosis was 0.83 (95% CI: 0.75-0.89) and pooled specificity was 0.82 (95% CI: 0.74-0.88). The summary AUC was 0.896, confirming high diagnostic accuracy. The positive likelihood ratio (LR+) was 4.61 and the negative likelihood ratio (LR-) was 0.21. Subgroup analyses based on AI model type (p > 0.05) and study design (p > 0.05) did not find significant differences between groups but revealed that single-center studies tended to report higher accuracy compared to multicenter studies. The secondary meta-analysis on massive PPH prediction (n = 4 studies, N = 353 patients: 165 PPH+ and 188 PPH-) yielded a pooled sensitivity of 0.88 (95% CI: 0.63-0.97), a pooled specificity of 0.78 (95% CI: 0.50-0.93), and an AUC of 0.901. Conclusions MRI-based AI models demonstrate high exploratory pooled accuracy for the prenatal diagnosis of PAS in high-risk cohorts. These results suggest that these tools show promising exploratory accuracy and may provide decision support as an adjunct ("human-in-the-loop") in equivocal cases. However, their real-world clinical generalizability remains constrained by retrospective designs and index test threshold optimization.
