title: From mid to late pregnancy changes in gestational diabetes mellitus patients: preliminary study by placental viscoelasticity.
abstract: Objective To investigate longitudinal changes in placental viscoelastic parameters from second trimester to third trimester between gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) and non-GDM pregnancies, and to evaluate the clinical utility of viscoelastic imaging. Methods This study included 122 singleton pregnancies (107 non-GDM, 15 GDM). All participants underwent placental viscoelastic ultrasound examination at least once during mid-trimester (14-27 +6 weeks) and again during third trimester (≥28 weeks). Elastic parameters (Emean, Emax, Emin, ESD) and viscosity parameters (Vmean, Vmax, Vmin, VSD) were measured in central (C), central-to-edge (C-E), and edge (E) placental regions. Changes (δ = late-pregnancy value - mid-trimester value) were calculated. Group comparisons used t-tests or Mann-Whitney U tests. Results At third trimester, GDM placentas showed significantly lower Emean (4.71 vs. 5.18 kPa, P = 0.035) and Emin (3.05 vs. 3.18 kPa, P = 0.039) in the E region compared to non-GDM. Longitudinal trend analysis revealed that most viscoelastic parameters in the C-E and E regions decreased over time in GDM, whereas they increased or remained stable in non-GDM, with the change in Vmax in the C-E region reaching statistical significance (P = 0.047). Maternal baseline characteristics and pregnancy outcomes were comparable between groups. Conclusion GDM pregnancies exhibit a distinct longitudinal evolution of placental viscoelasticity, characterized by a progressive decline in peripheral regional parameters, in contrast to the upward or stable trend seen in normal pregnancies. This unique pattern may serve as a novel imaging biomarker for early detection of subclinical placental changes and facilitate risk stratification and individualized management in GDM.

title: Advances in retinal cellular imaging: Towards single-cell resolution and functional biomarkers.
abstract: Retinal imaging has traditionally described tissue and layer level pathology, whereas direct assessment of individual cells in the living human retina has been limited by ocular aberrations, optical contrast and image analysis constraints. Adaptive optics (AO) has substantially changed this landscape by improving lateral resolution and enabling in vivo visualization of photoreceptors, retinal pigment epithelium (RPE), ganglion-cell-layer structures, immune cells and microvasculature. This review discusses human retinal cellular imaging across three major AO-enhanced platforms: flood-illumination adaptive optics (FIAO), adaptive optics optical coherence tomography (AO-OCT) and adaptive optics scanning laser ophthalmoscopy (AOSLO). These modalities provide complementary capabilities, including rapid en face imaging, depth-resolved volumetric assessment and flexible confocal, non-confocal and fluorescence-based contrast. Recent progress is also being shaped by faster wavefront correction, wider-field acquisition, compressed multichannel imaging, sensorless AO and artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted reconstruction, segmentation and quantification. Beyond optical resolution, molecular labeling strategies are beginning to add biological specificity to retinal cellular imaging. Indocyanine green (ICG) supports AO-assisted assessment of RPE mosaic contrast, annexin V-based Detection of Apoptosing Retinal Cells (DARC) provides a molecular readout of retinal cell stress and apoptosis, and curcumin-based imaging has been explored as an experimental retinal amyloid marker in Alzheimer's disease. Together, these advances indicate a shift from high-resolution visualization alone towards cellular and molecular biomarkers of disease activity, progression and treatment response. Further translation will require standardized acquisition, robust automated analysis, multimodal validation and larger prospective studies across devices, disease populations and clinical sites.

title: Dual-phase deep learning recommendation system for radiographic crown lengthening assessment and post selection for the restoration of endodontically treated teeth.
abstract: Statement of problem Restoring endodontically treated teeth requires careful evaluation of the supracrestal tissue attachment, ferrule integrity, and post-space dimensions to ensure long-term success. Manual radiographic analysis for crown lengthening indication and post selection is often time-consuming, subjective, and inconsistent, particularly in resource-limited settings where specialist access may be constrained. Purpose The purpose of this study was to design and validate an artificial intelligence (AI)-driven system that automated 2 essential restorative planning tasks, evaluating the clinical need for crown lengthening and recommending appropriate post dimensions in endodontically treated teeth, using dental radiographs as the input. Material and methods Two deep learning pipelines were developed and trained on annotated panoramic and periapical datasets with annotations created under the supervision of dentistry professionals. The crown measurement pipeline employed a U-shaped network (U-Net) model for initial tooth segmentation (assigning unique instance masks to each tooth), then cropping individual teeth and feeding them into a Mask Region-based Convolutional Neural Network (Mask R-CNN) for precise detection and crown length calculation, facilitating the assessment of parameters such as supracrestal tissue attachment and ferrule height, for identification of potential violations or restoration limitations. The post measurement pipeline utilized Mask R-CNN directly on the original images to detect endodontic posts and measure their length and width, enabling comparison against established prosthodontic criteria. Both models were trained in a graphics processing unit (GPU)-enabled environment (Kaggle; Google LLC) and evaluated using standard metrics including Intersection over Union (IoU), Dice coefficient, and measurement accuracy, with validation involving visual overlays and quantitative comparisons to expert annotations. Results The segmentation model achieved a mean IoU of 0.52 and a Dice coefficient of 0.66, with diagnostic accuracy exceeding 99% in identifying post locations and assessing ferrule presence. The system accurately detected supracrestal tissue attachment violations and provided clinically relevant post dimension recommendations, closely aligning with expert-guided decisions. GPU acceleration reduced model training time by over 70% compared to local central processing unit (CPU)-only workflows. Conclusions The AI-powered system demonstrated promising performance in automating radiographic evaluations critical to restoring endodontically treated teeth. By identifying crown lengthening requirements and suggesting post dimensions, the integrated pipelines supported objective and reproducible treatment planning. This approach may enhance prosthodontic workflows, especially in settings with limited specialist availability, and holds potential for integration into commercial dental imaging platforms.

title: Predicting early EGFR-TKI treatment response in EGFR-mutant lung adenocarcinoma from H&E histopathology with weakly supervised multiple-instance learning.
abstract: Background This study sought to construct a deep-learning pipeline using an attention mechanism and multiple-instance learning (MIL) to predict early treatment response to epidermal growth factor receptor-tyrosine kinase inhibitors (EGFR-TKIs) directly from routinely available hematoxylin-eosin (H&E) whole-slide images (WSIs) of pretreatment tissue in patients with EGFR-mutant lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD). Methods We retrospectively obtained clinicopathological data from 100 patients with EGFR-mutant lung adenocarcinoma. The model employed ResNet-50 for feature representation and integrated a gated-attention pooling mechanism for feature aggregation at the patient level. This weakly supervised approach did not require pixel-level manual annotations and enabled direct slide-level prediction of early treatment response. Results The proposed gated-attention model attained an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.891 in 5-fold cross-validation, which was numerically higher than those of mean pooling (0.837), max pooling (0.821), ABMIL (0.869), CLAM (0.874), and TransMIL (0.863); however, the difference relative to CLAM did not reach statistical significance (unadjusted P = 0.062). In ablation analyses, replacing gated attention with mean pooling resulted in the largest reduction in AUC (0.054). Patient-level nuclear morphometric profiling revealed that the early adverse response group exhibited larger nuclear areas (78.3 ± 22.1 μm² vs. 62.7 ± 18.4 μm² in the favorable response group), along with elevated nuclear-to-cytoplasmic ratios, nuclear eccentricity, and chromatin texture entropy. Chromatin texture entropy was positively correlated with the model-predicted probability of adverse response (r = 0.58, P < 0.001). Furthermore, the adverse response group displayed a higher frequency of TP53-associated alterations (62.5% vs. 38.3%), which encompassed next-generation sequencing findings and p53 immunohistochemical surrogates. In exploratory analyses, a four-variable clinical model yielded an AUC of 0.792, whereas an integrated model incorporating the multiple instance learning (MIL) risk score demonstrated an apparent AUC of 0.918 in this cohort, warranting further out-of-sample validation. Conclusion This study demonstrates that a lightweight and weakly supervised computational-pathology model can support the early estimation of EGFR-TKI treatment response. This pipeline uses routinely acquired H&E slides without requiring additional tissue sampling, provides biologically interpretable outputs, and may support clinical decision-making in precision oncology.

title: Effectiveness of Upfront Radiotherapy in Central Nervous System Germ Cell Tumors.
abstract: Background and purpose Radiotherapy (RT) is essential for curing central nervous system germ cell tumors (CNS-GCTs) except for pure mature teratoma (MT), but the optimal target volume, dose, and timing remain controversial. This study evaluated the benefit of upfront RT in CNS-GCTs. Materials and methods We reviewed CNS-GCT patients under 30-year-old treated from 2015 to 2023. Patients with pure germinomas (PG) received whole-ventricular irradiation (WVI) with tumor bed (TB) boost. Patients with malignant non-germinomatous germ cell tumor (MNGGCT) received WVI or whole-brain irradiation (WBI) with TB boost, with or without craniospinal irradiation (CSI), before or after platinum-etoposide-based chemotherapy (CTX). Serum alpha-fetoprotein and human chorionic gonadotropin levels guided diagnosis when histopathology was unavailable. Patients with MT were treated surgically. The primary endpoint was 5-year event-free survival (EFS); secondary endpoints included overall survival (OS), neurocognitive outcomes, and endocrinopathy rates. Results Twenty-nine patients were analyzed: 13 PGs, 7 MNGGCTs with upfront RT, 7 MNGGCTs with upfront CTX, and 2 MTs. The median follow-up of these tumors was 6.0, 6.6, 3.7, and 10.3 years, respectively. PGs receiving upfront RT achieved 5-year EFS and OS of 100% and 100%, respectively. For MNGGCTs receiving upfront RT, 5-year EFS and OS was 85.7% and 85.7%, respectively; 1 patient died from post-treatment disease progression. MNGGCTs treated with upfront CTX had 5-year EFS and OS of 41.7% and 60.0%, respectively; 2 patients relapsed (1 died), and 1 died from treatment-related complications. Both MTs remained event-free over 6 years following surgery alone or with Gamma Knife radiosurgery. Conclusions Upfront RT provided excellent outcomes in PGs and may eliminate the need for CTX in those achieving complete response.

title: Global Interobserver Variation among Head and Neck Cancer Experts in Target Delineation and Plan Quality Given a Standardized Gross Tumor Volume.
abstract: Purpose To characterize divergence among international experts in clinical and planning target volume (CTV/PTV) delineation and resulting treatment plans when all begin from the same standardized gross tumor volume (GTV) and organs-at-risk (OAR) set, in two representative scenarios: HPV-associated oropharyngeal and EBV-associated nasopharyngeal carcinoma treated with definitive chemoradiotherapy. Methods A global panel recruited through ASTRO, ESTRO, IAEA, FARO, and regional radiation oncology societies received identical DICOM data for two anonymized cases, comprising an expert-defined GTV (primary GTVp, involved-node GTVn) and a shared OAR set; target delineation and planning were left to participants. Each expert drew CTV1/CTV2 (±CTV3) and PTV1/PTV2/PTV3 and produced a deliverable IMRT/VMAT plan. Contours pooled in ProKnow DS yielded a consensus atlas whose 50% iso-agreement envelope served as the consensus reference. Agreement was scored by matching, missing, and extra volume, Dice similarity coefficient (DSC), and mean center-of-mass (COM) displacement in X/Y/Z. Submitted plans were benchmarked against a consensus plan and published dose thresholds. Results Thirty-two experts contributed target delineations (per-structure N 26-32); 25 submitted complete, deliverable plans. CTV1 concordance was moderate-to-high but heterogeneous (oropharynx DSC 0.72 ± 0.19; nasopharynx 0.73 ± 0.19), approximating a GTV + ∼5 mm expansion, and fell for CTV2 (0.66 ± 0.17 and 0.67 ± 0.17). It was lowest for the elective low-dose nasopharyngeal PTV3 (0.45 ± 0.21; extra volume mean 245.5 cc, SD 310.5; COM shift up to ∼17-26 mm). Target coverage was adequate (oropharynx PTV1 D95 mean 69.4 Gy, SD 1.4; nasopharynx 68.7 Gy, SD 2.0). OAR doses, though generally within accepted limits, were heterogeneous: in nasopharynx, dispersion and the gap between the average expert and consensus plan were greatest for the optic apparatus, eyes/lens, cochleae, and brainstem, which the consensus plan spared substantially more than the population average; in oropharynx, dispersion was greatest for the supraglottic larynx, cochlea, brainstem, and spinal canal. Conclusions Even from a standardized GTV, experts did not achieve high agreement in target volumes or plans; disagreement widened in elective nodal coverage and OAR trade-offs. Consensus-based peer review, potentially with AI-assisted contouring and planning guidance, warrants prospective study to reduce interobserver variation and standardize plan optimization and acceptance.

title: Safely Navigating the MR-Linac: A New Risk Framework for Prostate SBRT Patients with Cardiac Devices.
abstract: Purpose Prostate stereotactic body radiation therapy (SBRT) on a 1.5-T magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) linear accelerator (MR-linac) combines high-contrast intrafraction imaging with online adaptive replanning and enables focal dose intensification. Patients with cardiac implantable electronic devices (CIEDs) nonetheless face barriers to MR-guided radiotherapy (MRgRT), because existing guidance addresses diagnostic MRI and radiotherapy exposures separately and does not specify fraction-level requirements for their combination. We developed and implemented a framework integrating both domains in one operational pathway. Methods A multidisciplinary group synthesized diagnostic MRI, radiotherapy, and MR-linac safety evidence into a dual-axis risk model. The MRI/CIED axis is keyed to device exposure (generator-lead configuration, manufacturer conditions, and sequence-level radiofrequency and gradient compliance) rather than anatomic field of view. The radiotherapy (RT)/CIED axis stratifies neutron production, cumulative generator dose, generator-to-field geometry, and pacing dependence. A failure mode and effects analysis translated high-priority scenarios into hold points and role assignments; the pathway is implemented prospectively for CIED patients on a 1.5-T MR-linac. Results The two axes intersect in a matrix assigning every patient to one of six classes: LOW, LOW/INTERMEDIATE, INTERMEDIATE, INTERMEDIATE/HIGH, HIGH, or HOLD. Each class specifies monitoring, consent, interrogation, programming, personnel, and platform requirements. These are implemented through a day-of-treatment workflow with named role ownership and sequential hold points aligned with the 2026 American College of Radiology Manual on MR Safety. Two determinations override the matrix: MR-hold defers MRgRT irrespective of radiotherapy category, and RT-high defaults to computed tomography-guided radiotherapy. Conclusions By unifying MRI- and radiotherapy-specific device risks, the dual-axis framework converts categorical CIED exclusion into a graded, prospectively assigned disposition and makes every decision auditable. It is in prospective clinical use and offers appropriately selected patients a conservative route to MRgRT and the documentation from which multi-institutional validation can be built.

title: Single- Versus Two-Fraction HDR Brachytherapy Boost for Prostate Cancer: Long-Term Oncologic and Toxicity Outcomes.
abstract: Background and purpose High-dose-rate (HDR) brachytherapy boost with external beam radiotherapy (EBRT) is an established dose-escalation strategy for high-risk prostate cancer, but the optimal number of HDR fractions is unclear. We compared oncological outcomes and toxicity between single- and two-fraction HDR boost. Materials and methods Retrospective cohort of 378 patients with localized prostate cancer treated as high risk by institutional criteria (D'Amico-based; regrouped by NCCN) in 2004-2016 with EBRT (46 Gy) and a CT-guided HDR boost. Before November 2009, patients received EBRT followed by two HDR fractions of 9-10 Gy 8 hours apart (n=205); from November 2009, a single 15 Gy fraction preceded EBRT (n=173). Biochemical recurrence-free (BRFS), metastasis-free, cancer-specific (CSFS), and grade ≥3 genitourinary (GUTFS) and gastrointestinal toxicity-free survival were estimated with Kaplan-Meier and compared with the log-rank test; Cox models were fitted. Results Median follow-up was 130.1 months (IQR 94-158). Single-fraction patients more often had cT3 disease (72.3% vs. 43.4%) and NCCN high or very high risk (84.4% vs. 67.8%). At 10 years, BRFS, MFS, and CSFS were 81.4%, 91.5%, and 95.4%, without significant differences between one and two fractions (BRFS 79.6% vs. 82.6%, p=0.784; CSFS 95.3% vs. 95.4%, p=0.992). Crude grade ≥3 GU toxicity was higher with two fractions (22.9% vs. 10.4%, p=0.002); 10-year GUTFS was 82.2% vs. 89.7% (p=0.076). PSA and Gleason score >7 independently predicted CSFS and BRFS. Conclusion In this non-randomized comparison of consecutive protocols, one and two HDR boost fractions showed no significant difference in long-term oncological control. The confidence intervals were wide, and equivalence was not tested. Two fractions had more grade ≥3 GU toxicity, which cannot be separated from treatment era, EBRT sequence, and follow-up. A single 15 Gy fraction appears adequate as a boost combined with EBRT. It does not apply to HDR monotherapy. Prospective confirmation is needed.

title: Feasibility of DLAS-Driven Reoptimization to Accelerate MR-guided Online Adaptive Radiotherapy for Abdominal Malignancies.
abstract: Purpose MR-guided online adaptive radiation therapy (MRgOART) adjusts for daily anatomical changes. One challenge is prolonged treatment time due to organs-at-risk (OARs) contour editing. Recently, deep learning auto-segmentation (DLAS) models have demonstrated accuracy on MRI images, reducing contour editing demands. In this retrospective study, we investigate the dosimetric impact of DLAS-driven MRgOART, in which daily adaptive plans are created directly using unedited DLAS contours, and the feasibility of a one-step contour and adaptive plan review and approval process. Methods Six patients treated for abdominal malignancies on a 1.5T MR-Linac were studied. Daily OAR anatomy was segmented by a MR-based DLAS model, with targets rigidly transferred from reference images. The DLAS-driven plan was generated by re-optimizing using unedited DLAS contours. Dose was recalculated using clinical contours for dosimetric comparison with the clinical plan. Dice Similarity Coefficient (DSC), mean distance-to-agreement (MDA), surface Dice Similarity Coefficient (sDSC), and relative added path length (rAPL) were used to compare geometric accuracy of DLAS to clinical contours. Target coverage, D0.03cc to the gastrointestinal OARs, and V1200cGy to kidneys and liver were used to assess plan quality. Wilcoxon matched-pairs signed-rank tests evaluated dosimetric differences between DLAS-driven and clinically delivered plans. Time savings for contour editing to plan approval were estimated. Results DLAS and clinical contours demonstrated good agreement, with most average DSC scores exceeding 0.8 and average MDA under 3mm for OARs. No significant differences were found in target coverage, D0.03cc, or V1200cGy between the clinically delivered and DLAS-driven plans. Estimated treatment time savings ranged from 8 to 24 minutes. Conclusions Accurate MR-based DLAS models may enable DLAS-driven adaptive planning, eliminating contour edits prior to reoptimization. DLAS-driven plans were comparable to clinically delivered plans for the six patients studied. DLAS-driven adaptive planning is a promising approach to reduce physician burden and treatment times in MRgOART.

title: Associations between ENIGMA-identified OCD-associated brain morphology and treatment response: an exploratory study.
abstract: Selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs) and cognitive behavioural therapy (CBT) are first-line treatments for obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD). However, treatment outcomes vary substantially between individuals. This prognostic study aimed to examine whether OCD-associated brain morphometric measures identified by the ENIGMA Consortium were associated with responses to SSRI treatment and CBT in patients with OCD. This study included 80 patients with OCD who underwent structural brain MRI before treatment. Of these, 40 received SSRI treatment and 40 received CBT, each over a 12-week period. Significant reductions in OCD symptom severity were observed in both treatment groups following treatment. Total pallidum volume was associated with treatment response in the SSRI group, but not in the CBT group, with greater deviations from healthy controls associated with poorer treatment outcomes. Exploratory analyses of left and right pallidum volumes suggested potentially distinct patterns of association: left pallidum volume was associated only with SSRI treatment response, whereas right pallidum volume was associated with treatment response in the pooled sample. Pallidum volume may represent a candidate neuroimaging marker of SSRI treatment response in patients with OCD.

title: Alterations of resting arterial spin labeling perfusion in veterans and first responders with post-traumatic stress disorder following an open-label eTMS treatment protocol.
abstract: Military veterans and first responders experience higher rates of post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) than the general population. Despite being recognized since the DSM-III, existing treatments fail to address the underlying mechanisms of PTSD. Understanding these complexities could dramatically improve prognosis and treatment outcomes. We performed 20 treatments of electroencephalogram transcranial magnetic stimulation (eTMS) in a sample of veterans and first responders with PTSD. In a subsample (n = 16), we collected MRI before and after the open-label eTMS protocol. MRI consisted of pseudo-continuous arterial spin labeling to evaluate resting cerebral perfusion. Self-reported PTSD symptoms, measured using the PTSD Checklist for DSM-V, revealed a significant decrease of nearly 30-points on average, 3 times larger than the 10-point threshold commonly used to indicate treatment response. Following 20 eTMS treatments, resting perfusion was found to significantly increase in several regions of the brain including the amygdala and hippocampus. Compared to a cohort of healthy individuals (n = 28), perfusion was significantly lower in these regions prior to treatment. Moreover, symptom improvement was significantly correlated with perfusion increases within the left amygdala and hippocampus. The relationship between increased perfusion and decreased symptomology suggests that restoration of amygdala perfusion may reflect a normalization of emotional salience processing and threat detection mechanisms disrupted in PTSD. As resting perfusion reflects underlying metabolic demand, these findings point to widespread metabolic disruptions that improved after 20 eTMS treatments. Identifying such neurophysiological markers holds the promise for developing objective diagnostic tools for PTSD and provides insight into the response mechanisms of novel interventions.

title: Multimodal imaging evaluation of a giant aneurysm originating from a branch of the left circumflex coronary artery: A case report.
abstract: Giant coronary artery aneurysm (CAA) is a rare cardiovascular disease characterized by abnormal coronary dilatation and a high mortality rate. It lacks specific clinical manifestations and is often detected incidentally during imaging examinations, so early identification and timely intervention are crucial for improving patient prognosis. Existing studies have rarely documented the multimodal imaging characteristics of giant CAA, and clinical diagnostic and therapeutic experience remains to be further enriched. Here, we report a case of a giant aneurysm originating from a branch of the left circumflex coronary artery (LCX), incidentally detected by transthoracic echocardiography (TTE) performed for palpitations. TTE and transesophageal echocardiography (TEE), contrast-enhanced echocardiography, and CT angiography (CTA) were combined to accurately evaluate the location, size, and adjacent anatomical relationship of the aneurysm, and a surgical plan was formulated accordingly. The patient recovered well after surgery. This case summarizes the multimodal imaging characteristics of giant CAA, offering a clinical reference for similar rare cases.

title: Diagnostic value of coronal CT imaging in a patient with cecal volvulus accompanied by intestinal ischemia: A case report.
abstract: A 43-year-old woman presented with abdominal pain and vomiting. Contrast-enhanced abdominal computed tomography (CT) with coronal reconstruction revealed marked dilatation of the ileocecal region, a whirl sign, a bird beak sign, and decreased enhancement of the ascending colon wall. The patient was diagnosed with cecal volvulus accompanied by intestinal ischemia. Consequently, emergency surgery was performed. Intraoperative findings revealed 360° torsion of the ileum and ascending colon, with partial necrosis of the ascending colon wall. After resection of the twisted segment, functional end-to-end anastomosis was performed. The postoperative course was uneventful and the patient was discharged on postoperative day 11. Coronal CT imaging enabled the early diagnosis of cecal volvulus accompanied by intestinal ischemia and allowed prompt surgical intervention that resulted in a favorable outcome.

title: Interventional radiology management of juvenile nasopharyngeal angiofibroma.
abstract: Juvenile nasopharyngeal angiofibroma is a rare, highly vascular tumor that occurs almost exclusively in adolescent and young adult males and is associated with substantial intraoperative bleeding risk during surgical resection. Preoperative intra-arterial embolization is commonly performed to reduce tumor vascularity and improve perioperative safety. We present a case of a 21-year-old male with a history of asthma presenting with persistent unilateral nasal congestion who was found to have a left-sided nasopharyngeal mass. Surgical pathology later confirmed sinonasal angiofibroma. Diagnostic cerebral angiography demonstrated tumor blush supplied by branches of the left sphenopalatine artery arising from the internal maxillary artery of the external carotid circulation without significant contribution from the internal carotid artery or ophthalmic artery anastomoses. Using a microcatheter system, selective catheterization of the left sphenopalatine artery was performed, and embolization was achieved with 200-micrometer polyethylene glycol microspheres until near stasis was observed. Postembolization angiography demonstrated marked reduction of tumor blush, consistent with successful devascularization. The patient subsequently underwent successful surgical resection with remarkably low intraoperative blood loss (estimated 50 mL). This case highlights the role of interventional radiology in targeted preoperative embolization for the management of juvenile nasopharyngeal angiofibroma. Selective embolization of the sphenopalatine arterial supply can significantly reduce tumor vascularity and facilitate safer surgical resection with minimal blood loss. The relatively insidious clinical presentation and use of polyethylene glycol microspheres, which, to our knowledge, have not been previously described in juvenile nasopharyngeal angiofibroma, represent distinctive clinical and technical features of this case.

title: Isolated abdominal wall metastasis of endometrial carcinosarcoma: A case report.
abstract: Uterine carcinosarcoma, formerly called malignant mixed Müllerian tumor, is a rare and aggressive biphasic neoplasm made up of malignant epithelial and mesenchymal elements. Recurrence is frequent even after multimodal treatment, and distant relapses usually involve the lung, liver, or peritoneum. Isolated recurrence in the abdominal wall or subcutaneous tissue is rare and can easily be mistaken for a benign or unrelated soft-tissue lesion. A 71-year-old woman with hypertension and gout was diagnosed with grade 2 endometrioid endometrial adenocarcinoma, staged IA on preoperative MRI. Surgical staging (total hysterectomy, bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy, and bilateral pelvic lymphadenectomy) revealed a carcinosarcoma with a predominantly endometrioid carcinomatous component, deep (>50%) myometrial invasion, endocervical stromal involvement, and lymphovascular invasion (pT2 N0). She received adjuvant pelvic radiotherapy with vaginal brachytherapy, followed by 6 cycles of paclitaxel-carboplatin, and remained disease-free for more than 3 years. Routine surveillance imaging then showed a new calcified mass in the anterior abdominal wall with an adjacent para-umbilical nodule. Percutaneous biopsy confirmed a poorly differentiated carcinoma whose immunohistochemical profile was consistent with the known gynecologic primary. With no disease elsewhere, she underwent wide local excision with mesh reconstruction, achieving clear margins, followed by radiotherapy to the surgical bed. Uterine carcinosarcoma can recur in unusual extra-pelvic soft-tissue sites years after seemingly successful treatment. Any new abdominal wall or subcutaneous lesion in these patients should be biopsied promptly and discussed in a multidisciplinary setting, as isolated recurrences may still be treated with curative intent.

title: Patient perceptions of artificial intelligence in MRI reconstruction: A mixed methods study from a single NHS trust.
abstract: Introduction As part of a strategy to increase magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) capacity, the UK government funded the purchase of manufacturer artificial intelligence (AI) MRI image reconstruction software on MRI scanners. It aimed to reduce scan duration without compromising image quality and has been widely installed on clinical MRI scanners across the UK. Methods This is a mixed methods study, using an initial questionnaire to quantify opinions followed by focus groups of responders to further explore their views on technical issues. Patient views on the use of AI in MRI image reconstruction for reducing acquisition times, and more generally in their MRI pathway, were assessed. Results Study participants prefer improved image quality over faster acquisition times. If reducing acquisition times with AI, they feel it should only be used if extremely accurate images can be ascertained. They are uncomfortable with the use of manufacturer AI software for image reconstruction where accuracy is not stated and would like to be told about the use of AI in MRI. Conclusions Many participants felt that manufacturer AI software for MRI image reconstruction may be used only if a high accuracy is demonstrated, and if the training data is representative of the patient population, to not exacerbate health inequalities. This information is not currently given by manufacturers, which made the patient representatives concerned. Implication for practice

Introduction

It aimed to reduce scan duration without compromising image quality and has been widely installed on clinical MRI scanners across the UK.

Methods

This is a mixed methods study, using an initial questionnaire to quantify opinions followed by focus groups of responders to further explore their views on technical issues. Patient views on the use of AI in MRI image reconstruction for reducing acquisition times, and more generally in their MRI pathway, were assessed.

Results

Study participants prefer improved image quality over faster acquisition times. If reducing acquisition times with AI, they feel it should only be used if extremely accurate images can be ascertained. Conclusions

Many participants felt that manufacturer AI software for MRI image reconstruction may be used only if a high accuracy is demonstrated, and if the training data is representative of the patient population, to not exacerbate health inequalities. title: Evaluation of image-matching and prostate movement angle using anatomical characteristics obtained from planning computed tomography.
abstract: Introduction Setup errors and prostate movement may be associated with individual patient anatomy and internal physiological conditions. We evaluated image-matching and angle of prostate movement during prostate radiotherapy using anatomical characteristics. Methods We included 103 patients who underwent prostate volumetric-modulated arc therapy. Body mass index (BMI) and the volumes of the lesser pelvic cavity, bladder, rectum, and prostate were measured using planning computed tomography. Patients were divided into small- and large-value groups according to the median value of each anatomical characteristic. The medians and standard deviations of bone setup errors and inter- and intra-fraction prostate movements were calculated in the anterior-posterior (AP), left-right (LR), and superior-inferior (SI) directions using pelvic bone and fiducial markers with the ExacTrac X-ray system. Prostate movement angles were calculated from the approximation equation of correlation between the AP and SI direction for both groups (rectum volume, bladder capacity). Results The average setup errors in the LR direction exhibited a moderate positively correlation (r = 0.43) with lesser pelvic cavity volume in the small-value group, and a moderate negative correlation (r = -0.45) in the large-value group, as determined by BMI and lesser pelvic cavity volume. Intra-fraction prostate movement angles were tilted 6.7° in the AP direction in the large rectal volume group and 3.1° in the SI direction in the large bladder volume group. Conclusions Image-matching and prostate movement angles differed between groups stratified according to patient anatomical characteristics, suggesting the potential utility of anisotropic margins and careful patient setup. Implications for practice Evaluating patient-specific anatomical characteristics before radiotherapy planning may help estimate susceptibility to setup errors and facilitate the definition of anisotropic margins based on individual prostate movement angle information.

title: Evaluation of the experience of imposter phenomenon in advanced practice and consultant therapeutic radiographers.
abstract: Introduction Research suggests a high prevalence of imposter phenomenon among healthcare professionals, which is associated with negative impacts on professional identity, performance, well-being, careers, and service development. This local NHS service evaluation explored the imposter phenomenon among advanced and consultant therapeutic radiographers in a single radiotherapy department. This research aimed to understand determinants and the impact of imposter phenomenon, and to investigate management strategies, generating recommendations for future practice. Methods This qualitative research adopted an interpretivist approach, utilising purposive homogeneous sampling in recruitment. Data collection was via semi-structured focus groups; data analysis was inductive reflexive thematic analysis. Researcher reflexivity and independent observer review enhanced the credibility and trustworthiness of findings. Results Four key themes were identified from the data. Imposter phenomenon was context-dependent, influenced by a complex blend of individual, interpersonal, and systemic factors. Most participants identified with feelings of imposter phenomenon and experienced surges throughout their careers. Organisational factors such as strong hierarchy, isolation, and lack of role clarity compounded imposter phenomenon. Peer comparison and perceived judgment were strong individual determinants. Management strategies included role planning, mentorship, peer support, clear development pathways, and reflective practice. Conclusion Clear role definition and career pathways, alongside interprofessional education, could reduce feelings of imposter phenomenon among advanced practice and consultant therapeutic radiographers. Individualised transition plans, mentorship, peer support, shared workspaces, and structured feedback can enhance confidence, collaboration, and performance. Implications for practice Organisational and professional guidance on career development, funding, workforce strategies, and strategic planning would support role efficacy, staff wellbeing, and retention, ultimately improving service delivery and patient care.

title: Abbreviated and full-protocol breast magnetic resonance imaging in the detection of breast cancer: A comparative diagnostic test accuracy meta-analysis.
abstract: Introduction Abbreviated breast magnetic resonance imaging (abMRI) has emerged as a faster and potentially more accessible alternative to conventional full-protocol MRI (fpMRI). However, its diagnostic performance has been inconsistently reported across studies. This meta-analysis aimed to determine and compare the performance of abMRI and fpMRI for breast cancer detection. Methods CINAHL, EMBASE and PubMed were searched and finalised on 26 August 2026 for studies involving treatment-naïve women undergoing abMRI and/or fpMRI. Histopathology and/or clinico-radiological follow-up of ≥6 months served as the reference standard. Sensitivity and specificity were pooled using a bivariate random-effects model. Included studies were critically appraised with Quality Assessment of Diagnostic Accuracy Studies-2 (QUADAS-2) and -Comparative (QUADAS-C) tools. Results Seventeen studies comprising 5614 women were included. abMRI demonstrated a pooled per-patient sensitivity of 90.5% (95% confidence interval [CI]: 83.8-94.6%) and specificity of 75.4% (95% CI: 69.0-81.0%), with a pooled per-lesion sensitivity of 93.9% (95% CI: 86.7-97.3%) and specificity of 80.0% (95% CI: 71.0-86.4%). In comparison, fpMRI yielded a pooled per-patient sensitivity of 95.4% (95% CI: 92.1-97.4%) and specificity of 79.6% (95% CI: 70.2-86.6%), with a pooled per-lesion sensitivity of 96.3% (95% CI: 93.0-98.0%) and specificity of 80.0% (95% CI: 68.4-88.1%). Likelihood-ratio tests revealed significantly higher sensitivity for fpMRI than abMRI at per-patient level (p < 0.01). No significant differences in sensitivity was observed at per-lesion level and, specificity remained comparable between both protocols at per-patient and per-lesion levels (all p > 0.05). Conclusion abMRI demonstrates comparable specificity to fpMRI, with slightly lower sensitivity (approximately 2.61-4.78% difference) for breast cancer detection. Implications for practice abMRI may serve as a practical alternative to fpMRI in selected clinical settings where rapid imaging, improved accessibility and reduced resource utilisation are priorities, particularly when protocols incorporate T2 and/or diffusion-weighted imaging.

title: Experiences of adverse prenatal ultrasound findings and their communication: A systematic review of expectant parent and ultrasound Practitioner perspectives.
abstract: Introduction Current evidence suggests that the identification and communication of adverse prenatal findings are associated with negative psychological outcomes for both patients and ultrasound practitioners. There remains a need to synthesise and better understand this evidence to assess the extent and nature of the problem. This study therefore aimed to explore the experiences, views and preferences of ultrasound practitioners and expectant parents regarding the identification and communication of adverse prenatal ultrasound findings. Methods Systematic review and narrative synthesis of studies reporting qualitative and quantitative data. The databases MEDLINE, CINAHL and Web-of-Science were searched between January-2010 and May-2026. Results Twelve studies were included. Findings highlight a lack of formal communication training and limited emotional support for practitioners when identifying and communicating adverse prenatal findings, contributing to anxiety, burnout, and role-related uncertainty. For patients, inadequate explanations, inconsistent communication, and insufficient time to process information were associated with immediate shock and longer-term psychological burden. Additionally, environmental and organisational factors, such as time pressures, workload, and suboptimal clinical settings, further influenced communication quality and exacerbated distress for both patients and practitioners. Conclusion Identification and communication of adverse prenatal findings have significant psychological impacts on patients and practitioners, influenced by communication quality. Ongoing gaps in training, emotional support, and role clarity contribute to inconsistent practice and increased distress, highlighting the need for structured frameworks and strengthened organisational support. Future research should evaluate communication interventions and include more diverse populations to improve psychological outcomes and consistency of care. Implications for practice Structured, empathetic communication of adverse findings should be supported by targeted training, clear role delineation, and organisational support to reduce psychological burden and improve consistency of care.

originalAbstract:
Introduction

Current evidence suggests that the identification and communication of adverse prenatal findings are associated with negative psychological outcomes for both patients and ultrasound practitioners. There remains a need to synthesise and better understand this evidence to assess the extent and nature of the problem. This study therefore aimed to explore the experiences, views and preferences of ultrasound practitioners and expectant parents regarding the identification and communication of adverse prenatal ultrasound findings.

Methods

Systematic review and narrative synthesis of studies reporting qualitative and quantitative data. The databases MEDLINE, CINAHL and Web-of-Science were searched between January-2010 and May-2026.

Results

Twelve studies were included. Findings highlight a lack of formal communication training and limited emotional support for practitioners when identifying and communicating adverse prenatal findings, contributing to anxiety, burnout, and role-related uncertainty. For patients, inadequate explanations, inconsistent communication, and insufficient time to process information were associated with immediate shock and longer-term psychological burden. Additionally, environmental and organisational factors, such as time pressures, workload, and suboptimal clinical settings, further influenced communication quality and exacerbated distress for both patients and practitioners.

Conclusion

Identification and communication of adverse prenatal findings have significant psychological impacts on patients and practitioners, influenced by communication quality. Ongoing gaps in training, emotional support, and role clarity contribute to inconsistent practice and increased distress, highlighting the need for structured frameworks and strengthened organisational support. Future research should evaluate communication interventions and include more diverse populations to improve psychological outcomes and consistency of care.

Implications for practice

Structured, empathetic communication of adverse findings should be supported by targeted training, clear role delineation, and organisational support to reduce psychological burden and improve consistency of care.

title: Clinical workflow optimisation through advanced practice radiation therapist-led cone-beam computed tomography image matching in thoracic stereotactic body radiotherapy.
abstract: Introduction Thoracic stereotactic body radiotherapy (SBRT) requires accurate image verification because of high dose per fraction, steep dose gradients and tight treatment margins. In many departments, cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) image matching remains dependent on radiation oncologist (RO) availability, which may contribute to workflow delays and inefficient use of specialist clinical time. This clinical workflow evaluation examined whether credentialed advanced practice radiation therapist (APRT)-led CBCT image matching could maintain workflow efficiency while reducing immediate RO attendance requirements. Methods Routine operational workflow data were extracted for thoracic SBRT fractions delivered between October 2025 and May 2026. All Day 1 fractions were excluded from the primary comparison, irrespective of matching personnel. Non-Day 1 RO-led and APRT-led fractions were compared for patient in-room duration, personnel attendance duration, workflow variability, documented protocol deviations, image-matching failures, workflow disruptions and estimated direct manpower cost. Results A total of 362 fractions from 89 treatment courses were analysed, including 89 Day 1 fractions, 170 RO-led non-Day 1 fractions and 103 APRT-led non-Day 1 fractions. In the primary non-Day 1 analysis, median patient in-room duration was 19 min for RO-led fractions and 20 min for APRT-led fractions. Median image-matching duration was 11 min and 13 min, respectively. No APRT-related protocol deviations, image-matching failures or workflow disruptions were documented in the reviewed treatment records. Annualised projections indicated approximately 31.3 physician-hours released and SGD 1864 in direct manpower cost savings per year. Conclusion Credentialed APRT-led CBCT image matching was feasible within thoracic SBRT and did not materially prolong workflow duration. Implications for practice Structured credentialing, Day 1 collaborative review, defined escalation criteria and ongoing audit may support safe APRT-led image verification in high-precision radiotherapy workflows.

title: Image interpretation performance among pre-registration diagnostic radiography students in Ghana: A cross-institutional study.
abstract: Introduction Preliminary image evaluation (PIE) supports timely clinical decision-making, yet little is known about the preparedness of pre-registration diagnostic radiography students for this role. This study assessed image interpretation performance of final-year diagnostic radiography students in Ghana. Methods A cross-sectional study involving 80 final-year diagnostic radiography students across three tertiary training institutions in Ghana was conducted. Participants completed a supervised 60-image interpretation test comprising chest (n = 22), axial skeleton (n = 16) and appendicular skeleton (n = 22) radiographs at their respective institutions' computer laboratories. Responses were assessed against an established reference standard. Descriptive statistics, Kruskal-Wallis H and post-hoc tests, were used to compare performance across institutions. Results Mean overall image interpretation test scores were 81.8% (SE: 0.84), 70.0% (SE: 1.67) and 84.6% (SE: 0.92) for Institutions X, Y and Z, respectively. Corresponding mean diagnostic classification accuracy was 88.6% (SE: 0.71), 79.4% (SE: 1.41) and 88.8% (SE: 0.78). Overall, 82.5% (66/80) achieved ≥80% diagnostic classification accuracy. Mean sensitivity was 88.4% (SE: 1.04), 83.0% (SE: 2.2) and 93.4% (SE: 1.1), while mean specificity was 88.7% (SE: 1.1), 77.0% (SE: 2.5) and 85.3% (SE: 1.5), respectively. Performance differed significantly across institutions (p < 0.05), with Institutions X and Z generally demonstrating stronger performance than Institution Y. Self-perceived image interpretation ability correlated moderately with overall test performance (r = 0.46, p < 0.001). Conclusion Final-year diagnostic radiography students in Ghana demonstrated encouraging image interpretation performance, although substantial inter-institutional variation was evident. Implications for practice Greater consistency in pre-registration image interpretation education may strengthen graduates' foundational skills for potential future involvement in PIE.

title: Comparison of ocular radiation doses between ultra-low-dose photon-counting computed tomography and digital radiography for orbital foreign body screening: A phantom study.
abstract: Introduction Metallic orbital foreign bodies may pose a safety risk during magnetic resonance imaging due to potential displacement or heating of ferromagnetic material within the magnetic field, potentially resulting in severe ocular injury. When their presence cannot be reliably excluded based on patient history, imaging is performed as a precautionary screening step prior to magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). Digital radiography (DR) is commonly used for this purpose due to its low radiation dose but provides limited anatomical and spatial information. Photon-counting CT (PCCT) offers high spatial resolution and improved dose efficiency and may serve as an alternative ultra-low-dose screening technique. This phantom study compared radiation exposure between DR and ultra-low-dose PCCT for orbital imaging. Methods Orbital imaging was performed in an Alderson RANDO phantom using DR and PCCT. Absorbed radiation doses to the eye lens and globe were measured using optically stimulated luminescence dosimeters (OSLDs) and effective doses were estimated from standard dose descriptors and compared for both modalities. Results Mean absorbed doses of PCCT imaging were 0.092 mGy for the lens and 0.087 mGy for the globe, compared with 6.215 mGy and 4.855 mGy for DR, corresponding to dose reductions of 98.5% and 98.2%. Effective doses were 0.002 mSv for PCCT and 0.023 mSv for DR, corresponding to a 91.3% reduction. Conclusion Ultra-low-dose PCCT substantially reduced ocular radiation exposure compared with DR while allowing visualization of the tested metallic foreign body. Further studies are warranted to evaluate its diagnostic performance as a dose-saving alternative for orbital foreign body screening prior to MRI. Implication for practice Ultra-low-dose PCCT may represent a dose-saving alternative for orbital foreign body imaging prior to MRI, with the additional benefit of cross-sectional visualization. Further validation of diagnostic performance is required before routine clinical implementation.

title: Exploring the workforce culture of advanced practice in therapeutic radiography.
abstract: Introduction Advanced practice (AP) is an established career pathway in therapeutic radiography and integral to sustaining radiotherapy services; however, high attrition among mid-to late-career radiographers threatens workforce capacity. This study explored the workforce culture of advanced-level practice in therapeutic radiography in the United Kingdom, seeking to establish the barriers to retention. Methods A qualitative design was adopted. Using purposive sampling, ten therapeutic radiographers (TRs) who were either currently employed in an AP role or had left such a role within the preceding five years were recruited. Semi-structured interviews were conducted with thematic analysis of the transcripts. Results AP was valued for its clinical breadth, autonomy and influence over the patient pathway. Retention was undermined by poorly defined roles and a fragile professional identity, exacerbated by absent or unrealistic job plans that did not recognise the holistic nature of the four pillars. Support, supervision and peer networks were key protective factors. Limited progression and unclear routes to consultant practice further contributed to dissatisfaction. Conclusion Retention of AP TRs depends less upon the appeal of the role than upon the organisational culture in which it is enacted, including clear job planning, enduring supervision and support, recognition of their value by others and a defined pathway encouraging individuals towards consultant practice. Implications for practice Realistic job plans with protected time for the four pillars are required to enable TRs to enact the full AP role. Clinical supervision, mentorship and peer support should be sustained across the AP career pathway to protect practitioner wellbeing and retention. Consistent national frameworks, job titles and banding, together with a defined route to consultant practice, are needed to support the recruitment and retention of advanced practitioners.

title: Ultra-portable chest X-ray in community tuberculosis screening: Operational lessons for radiologic technologists.
abstract: Introduction Ultra-portable chest X-ray can extend tuberculosis (TB) screening beyond hospital-based imaging services, but field implementation introduces operational constraints that are less visible in technical performance studies. This study examined practical lessons from a community-based TB screening programme, with emphasis on radiography practice. Methods A mixed-methods operational evaluation was conducted within a hospital-led active TB case-finding programme in high-risk urban communities in Bangkok, Thailand. Routine service records from all 22 ultra-portable X-ray-supported sessions were reviewed retrospectively. Research-specific data collected after ethics approval comprised service-recipient questionnaires (n = 140), staff questionnaires, and semi-structured interviews with 24 multidisciplinary staff. The Input-Process-Output framework was prespecified as the organising framework. Qualitative interview data were analysed descriptively using cumulative structured notes derived from review of the audio-recorded interviews. Results Across the 22 ultra-portable X-ray-supported sessions, 1161 chest X-ray examinations were performed, with a mean throughput of approximately 53 examinations per session. Abnormalities requiring referral were recorded in 162 examinations (14.0%), including 71 (6.1%) with findings suspicious for pulmonary TB and 91 (7.8%) with other abnormalities requiring clinical evaluation. Recurrent operational categories included site and environmental readiness, detector-workstation connectivity, equipment and image-acquisition constraints, radiation and infection safety, integrated review and referral workflow, multidisciplinary coordination, and workload and training requirements. Conclusion Ultra-portable chest X-ray can support same-visit community TB screening and referral, but reliable implementation depends on the surrounding service system as well as the imaging device. The findings support practice considerations including early radiologic technologist input to site assessment, connectivity contingency planning, infection-prevention preparation, realistic workflow capacity, and workload support. Implications for practice Community programmes using ultra-portable X-ray should consider radiologic technologists as contributors to pre-deployment planning, imaging safety, technical readiness, and workflow design, while prospectively monitoring image quality, repeat imaging, dose indicators, connectivity failures, and workload.

Recurrent operational categories included site and environmental readiness, detector-workstation connectivity, equipment and image-acquisition constraints, radiation and infection safety, integrated review and referral workflow, multidisciplinary coordination, and workload and training requirements.

Conclusion

Ultra-portable chest X-ray can support same-visit community TB screening and referral, but reliable implementation depends on the surrounding service system as well as the imaging device. The findings support practice considerations including early radiologic technologist input to site assessment, connectivity contingency planning, infection-prevention preparation, realistic workflow capacity, and workload support.

Implications for practice

Community programmes using ultra-portable X-ray should consider radiologic technologists as contributors to pre-deployment planning, imaging safety, technical readiness, and workflow design, while prospectively monitoring image quality, repeat imaging, dose indicators, connectivity failures, and workload.

title: MRI-guided HDR brachytherapy or integrated VMAT boost for tumour-targeted dose escalation in localised prostate cancer: long-term results of the TARGET study.
abstract: Purpose To evaluate local control of the gross tumour volume in localised prostate cancer following focal dose escalation delivered by integrated boost volumetric modulated arc therapy (IB-VMAT) or high-dose-rate (HDR) brachytherapy. Materials and methods Patients with localised prostate cancer and an intraprostatic lesion identified on multiparametric magnetic resonance imaging (mpMRI) were included in a prospective, non-randomised phase II study. Eighty patients received VMAT to the prostate 76 Gy/38 fractions. Boost strategy involved an IB of 95 Gy/38 fractions (IB-VMAT) or a single fraction of 10 Gy (HDR-VMAT). Three patients received 6 months androgen deprivation therapy. The primary endpoint was 3-year local control (LC) assessed by MRI or MRI-guided biopsy. Secondary outcomes included biochemical failure-free survival (bFFS), toxicity and health-related quality of life (HRQoL), assessed using CTCAE v.4.0, the American Urological Association Symptom Score and EPIC. Results Median follow-up was 4.8 years (IQR, 4.0-8.0). Sixty-six patients underwent a 3-year MRI or MRI-guided biopsy; one patient demonstrated recurrence within the boost volume. Four patients demonstrated intraprostatic failure outside the boost volume and three patients developed regional/distant metastases. Eight patients experienced biochemical failure (4 IB-VMAT; 4 HDR-VMAT). Overall, 5-year bFFS was 86.9% (95% CI, 79.1-95.5). No substantial differences in late toxicities and HRQoL were observed between cohorts. Conclusion Intraprostatic tumour-targeted dose escalation using IB-VMAT or HDR-VMAT provided high rates of LC and bFFS with limited adverse impact in late toxicity and HRQoL. Randomised studies are needed to further define the merits and differences between the two techniques.

title: A prospective randomized evaluation of AI assisted GTV contouring in head-and-neck radiotherapy.
abstract: Background AI-assisted contouring has demonstrated efficiency and consistency benefits for organs-at-risk in radiotherapy. However, its impact on gross tumor volume (GTV) delineation remains unexplored. The aim of this study was to evaluate AI-assisted GTV contouring in head and neck cancer radiotherapy in an exploratory randomized controlled clinical trial. Methods In this prospective, single-centre, randomized controlled evaluation, patients referred for curative-intent radiotherapy of head-neck cancer were randomized to manual contouring (control) or AI-assisted contouring (intervention) of gross tumor volumes using an in-house developed segmentation model. The primary endpoint was the extent of editing during a blinded multidisciplinary target conference, using normalized Added Path Length (APL). Secondary endpoints included conference duration, self-reported contouring time, and perceived complexity of the cases. Results Between Sept 11, 2023, and Jan 20, 2025, 85 patients were enrolled; 83 were included in the analysis (41 control, 42 AI-assisted). The median difference in APL (AI-assisted minus control, negative favoring the intervention) was -0.02 [-0.32; 0.07] for GTV-T and 0.06 [-0.01; 0.14] for GTV-N. Conference duration, contouring time, and perceived complexity were similar between groups. No adverse events were reported. Conclusion The median difference in APL between groups was consistent with no relevant effect for GTV-T. For GTV-N, however, AI-assisted contouring tended towards more editing during peer review for APL, but not for supplementary contour metrics. No efficiency benefits were demonstrated. Overall, these findings do not indicate a concern, but warrants further research before widespread adoption.

title: Predictors of radiation-induced lymphopenia in NSCLC: blood and bone marrow dose during chemoradiotherapy.
abstract: Purpose Radiation-induced lymphopenia (RIL) is a significant complication for patients with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) undergoing radiotherapy, particularly as immunotherapy becomes increasingly integral to treatment. Understanding the predictors and mechanisms underlying RIL will support and help direct efforts to preserve anti-tumor immunity and optimize therapeutic outcomes. Methods This study assessed the relationship between radiation dose to the blood and bone marrow and the development and recovery of lymphopenia in two (training and validation) cohorts, 134 patients in total, with NSCLC treated with either proton (PSPT) or photon-based chemoradiotherapy (CRT) between June 2009 and March 2014. Compartmental blood flow models and automatic organ segmentation were used to quantify radiation doses to circulating blood, large vessels and proliferating bone marrow. Multivariable logistic regression was performed to identify significant predictors of severe lymphopenia within 2 months from CRT start and its recovery. Results We found that both the generalized equivalent uniform dose (gEUD) to blood and baseline absolute lymphocyte count (ALC) were significant predictors of grade 4 lymphopenia. The discriminative ability (measured by AUC) for blood dose gEUD peaked around negative a values, suggesting that low-dose contributions to the blood pool are most relevant for predicting lymphopenia risk. Despite proton therapy delivering mean blood doses lower by 12.1% (p = 0.006) compared to photon therapy, there were no significant differences in nadir lymphocyte counts between the modalities. Bone marrow dose was only weakly correlated with lymphocyte nadir and showed no association with lymphocyte recovery after treatment. Conclusion Our findings demonstrate that radiation dose to circulating blood is a significant predictor of radiation-induced lymphopenia in NSCLC patients. Despite the observed correlations, these findings suggest that optimizing radiation dose to the blood alone may not be the most effective strategy for reducing lymphopenia.

title: Phase I dose-escalation study of stereotactic body radiotherapy with elective nodal irradiation for borderline resectable and unresectable locally advanced pancreatic cancer.
abstract: Background Locoregional recurrence remains a major clinical challenge in borderline resectable (BR) and unresectable locally advanced (UR-LA) pancreatic cancer, even after stereotactic body radiotherapy (SBRT). This phase I trial evaluated the safety, maximum tolerated dose (MTD), and preliminary efficacy of adding prophylactic elective nodal irradiation (ENI) to 5-fraction SBRT. Methods Patients with BR/UR-LAPC were enrolled in a 3 + 3 dose-escalation design. SBRT was delivered in 5 fractions using either adaptive magnetic resonance image-guided radiation therapy or respiratory breath-hold radiotherapy with a fiducial marker. The ENI dose was fixed at 30 Gy in five fractions, while the primary tumor dose increased from Level 1 (35 Gy) to Level 3 (40 Gy). The primary endpoint was acute dose-limiting toxicity (DLT) (any Grade ≥ 3 non-hematological adverse events within 14 days after the completion of SBRT). Results Twelve patients (BR: 4, LA: 8) were enrolled, 11 of whom had previously received systemic chemotherapy. One patient at Level 1 experienced acute Grade 3 anorexia/nausea requiring hospitalization. No DLTs were observed at Levels 2 and 3, and the MTD was not reached. Three patients with preexisting biliary stents developed subacute Grade 3 cholangitis. No Grade ≥ 3 late adverse events occurred. The median overall survival after SBRT was 17.3 months, and the 1-year locoregional control rate was 75%. Conclusion Five-fraction SBRT with simultaneous 30 Gy ENI was feasible, and the MTD was not reached within the tested dose levels up to 40 Gy. Further prospective studies are needed to evaluate its long-term safety and treatment outcomes.

title: Independent validation of a predictive risk model for contrast-enhancing brain lesions supports enhanced periventricular radiosensitivity and variable proton RBE.
abstract: Background and purpose Contrast-enhancing brain lesions (CEBLs) were reported as MR-imaging (MRI) endpoint to assess dose effects in healthy brain tissue following proton radiotherapy (PRT) of low-grade-glioma (LGG) patients. A voxel-level risk model was proposed with absorbed dose (D), dose-averaged linear energy transfer (LET D ), and proximity to the ventricular system as risk factors. We validated this model in an independent LGG patient cohort. Material and methods LGG patients treated at the same institution but more recently (2015-2019) were considered. For each patient, follow-up MRI data were screened for CEBLs, complication-risk maps were calculated and patient-level NTCP CEBL values were determined according to the original model. Eventually, risk model coefficients were updated by regressing the original logistic model to the validation cohort (validC) data. Results The validC comprised 112 subjects. Observed CEBL incidence of 21% was the same as in the modelling cohort (modelC); observed number of CEBLs and median lesion volume were considerably smaller in the validC, (N validC = 26, N modelC = 67 and V med,validC = 110 mm 3 , V med,modelC = 235 mm 3 ). Good calibration of the original patient-level NTCP CEBL model was obtained in the validC. Update of the model coefficients yielded a more pronounced LET D -effect and a 2.4 times higher odds ratio for the complication risk in the periventricular space (PVS). Conclusions The presented validation confirms an enhanced radiosensitivity of the PVS, a variable proton RBE, and supports serial complication characteristics of the brain. This underlines the need for a PRT strategy that actively spares the PVS under consideration of an LET D -dependent proton RBE. Clinical trial information The study was approved by the ethics committee of the Heidelberg University Hospital (ethics vote: S-516/2022).

title: Femoral artery Doppler, an innovative predictor of successful caudal block: A prospective observational study.
abstract: Background Caudal block is a common regional anaesthesia technique in paediatric surgery. Although various parameters have been proposed to evaluate the success of this block, the optimal, gold standard assessment method remains elusive. This study aims to examine the potential of femoral artery Doppler indices as a non-invasive, objective tool for predicting the efficacy of caudal block. Methods In this prospective observational study, 44 paediatric patients undergoing surgery under general anaesthesia with caudal block were assessed. Standard anaesthesia protocols were followed, and femoral artery Doppler ultrasound was performed at 3 time points: before the block, and 15 and 30 minutes after. title: 18 F-FDG PET-based radiomics for the prediction of aggressive/high-grade tumor in patients with cartilaginous tumors: A preliminary study.
abstract: Objective To assess the role of texture analysis of pre-treatment 18 F-FDG PET in the prediction of aggressive/high-grade tumor subtypes of cartilaginous tumors. Materials and methods Patients with cartilaginous tumors (benign cartilaginous tumors or CSs) who underwent pre-treatment 18 F-FDG PET for primary staging or restaging of recurrent disease were included in this retrospective study. Demographic and clinicopathologic data were collected. Textural and conventional PET parameters (maximum standardized uptake value (SUVmax), SUVmean, metabolic tumor volume (MTV), and total lesion glycolysis (TLG)) were obtained from PET/CT images using LIFEx program. The least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression analysis was performed for feature selection. Univariate and multivariate logistic regression analyses were performed to determine predictors of aggressive/high-grade tumor subtypes in cartilaginous tumors. Results A total of 29 18 F-FDG PET scans from 26 patients were included in the present study. Among 29 included 18 F-FDG PET scans, 18 (62.1%) scans were performed in patients with a benign/low-grade tumor(benign cartilaginous tumors and G1-2 CSs), while 11 (37.9%) scans were performed in patients with an aggressive/high-grade tumor(G3, dedifferentiated, mesenchymal, and other aggressive CSs). In the LASSO logistic regression analysis, seven potential predictors were selected for predicting aggressive/high-grade cartilaginous tumors. Whereas SUVmax (p = 0.025), SUVmean (p = 0.028), GLRLM_Run Entropy (p = 0.007), GLSZM_ZSE (p = 0.011), and GLSZM_SZLGLE (p = 0.007) were significantly associated with aggressive/high-grade pathology in univariate analysis, GLRLM_Run Entropy was found as the only independent predictor in multivariate analysis. Conclusion Tumor heterogeneity assessed by texture analysis of pre-treatment 18 F-FDG PET may be a significant predictor of aggressive/high-grade tumor subtypes in cartilaginous tumors.

title: Pancreatic Neuroendocrine Neoplasms: Integrating WHO Classification with CT, MRI, and Molecular Imaging.
abstract: Pancreatic neuroendocrine neoplasms (pNENs) are a heterogeneous group of tumors within gastroenteropancreatic neuroendocrine neoplasms (GEP-NENs), with variable clinical behavior and prognosis. The World Health Organization (WHO) classification distinguishes well-differentiated neuroendocrine tumors (NETs) from poorly differentiated neuroendocrine carcinomas (NECs), including the recognition of grade 3 NETs (NET G3) as a separate entity with important clinical implications. Multiphasic computed tomography (CT) and multiparametric magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) are central to detection, staging, and follow-up, with MRI offering superior sensitivity for liver metastases, particularly with diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) and hepatobiliary phase (HBP). Molecular imaging with somatostatin receptor-targeted PET and 18 F-FDG PET provides complementary biologic information by assessing receptor expression, metabolic aggressiveness, and tumor heterogeneity. SSTR-targeted PET supports confirmation of neuroendocrine phenotype, whole-body staging, and selection of candidates for peptide receptor radionuclide therapy, whereas 18 F-FDG PET identifies aggressive or dedifferentiated tumor components that may influence prognosis and favor chemotherapy-oriented strategies. Despite advances, noninvasive grading remains limited, requiring integration of imaging with histopathology. An integrated multimodality approach combining CT, MRI, molecular imaging, and pathology is therefore essential for accurate staging, biopsy targeting, treatment stratification, and personalized management.

title: AI-driven radiopharmaceutical dosimetry optimization for theranostics: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract: Introduction Personalised radioligand therapy (RLT) depends on accurate absorbed-dose estimation. Standard dosimetry requires multiple post-therapy single-photon emission computed tomography/computed tomography (SPECT/CT) acquisitions, imposing logistical burdens. Machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) have been proposed to streamline organ segmentation, generate synthetic imaging timepoints, and predict patient-specific doses. We evaluated the performance, methodological quality, and translational readiness of artificial intelligence (AI)-driven dosimetry in the clinical theranostics literature. Methods In this systematic review and meta-analysis, we searched PubMed, Web of Science, Scopus, and regional databases (Jan 1, 2014, to March 1, 2025). Studies applying AI to dosimetry in human RLT recipients were eligible. Two reviewers screened and extracted data. Risk of bias was assessed with the Prediction model Risk Of Bias ASsessment Tool (PROBAST) and the Quality Assessment of Diagnostic Accuracy Studies-2 (QUADAS-2). Meta-analyses of organ segmentation (Dice similarity coefficient [DSC]) and dose prediction (concordance correlation coefficient [CCC]) used restricted maximum-likelihood (REML) random-effects models restricted to studies with independent validation sets. Prospero CRD420261349805 (https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/prospero/display_record.php?RecordID=1349805). Results 58 studies met inclusion criteria covering 1847 patients (1523 [82%] male, 324 [18%] female). 23 studies with independent validation were eligible for meta-analysis. Pooled DSC was 0.87 (95% CI 0.83-0.90; 16 studies). Pooled voxel dosimetry relative absolute error (RAE) was 6.1% (4.6%-8.1%; 12 studies). Pretherapy kidney dose prediction yielded pooled CCC 0.79 (0.72-0.85; 8 studies). PROBAST identified high risk of bias in 71% of prediction studies. Reducing timepoints from ≥3 to 1-2 scans increased RAE by 8.2 percentage points (5.1-11.4). AI reduced median processing time from 180 to 25 min. Conclusions On independent validation data, AI-driven dosimetry shows promising accuracy for organ-level dose estimation and substantially reduces processing time. However, the evidence base remains immature: 71% of prediction studies carry high risk of bias, only four studies report external validation, and most pooled outcomes were graded as low or very low certainty. External multicentre validation and prospective randomised trials comparing AI-guided against fixed-activity RLT are needed before clinical adoption. Current evidence primarily demonstrates technical feasibility rather than proven clinical utility.

title: Clinical significance of the COPD assessment test in evaluating treatment response in Mycobacterium avium complex pulmonary disease.
abstract: Background In Mycobacterium avium complex pulmonary disease (MAC-PD), sputum culture conversion is a key endpoint but does not fully reflect symptom burden. We evaluated the COPD Assessment Test (CAT) as a patient-reported measure of disease severity and treatment response. Methods We retrospectively analyzed 179 treatment episodes in 174 patients with MAC-PD who continued therapy for at least 12 months. CAT scores were assessed at baseline and at 6 and 12 months. We examined associations of baseline CAT scores with chest computed tomography (CT) scores and sputum culture status, and of CAT changes (Δ6 and Δ12) with the 12-month culture-positive versus culture-negative/sputum-unobtainable classification and a study-defined composite incorporating 12-month radiographic response and the microbiologic course through 24 months. Results Baseline CAT scores correlated weakly with CT scores and were higher in baseline culture-positive and poorly controlled episodes. Neither Δ6 nor Δ12 differed by 12-month culture classification. Δ12 was more favorable in well-controlled than in poorly controlled episodes (p = 0.010), but discrimination was limited (area under the curve, 0.646 in all classifiable episodes and 0.682 in those with baseline CAT > 2). In the latter subgroup, an exploratory decrease of at least 3 points showed a sensitivity of 52.0% and a specificity of 71.9%. Conclusions CAT may complement microbiologic and radiographic assessments by capturing patient-reported symptom changes. The limited discriminatory performance does not support the use of CAT alone to classify treatment control.

title: French protocol for the diagnosis and management of chronic nonbacterial osteomyelitis.
abstract: Chronic Nonbacterial Osteomyelitis (CNO) is a primary, non-infectious inflammatory bone disorder predominantly affecting children (median age 10 years), with a female predominance. It presents as bone pain with an inflammatory pattern, sometimes accompanied by localised swelling, and follows a relapsing-remitting course. Typical lesions involve the metaphysis of the lower limbs, while clavicular, mandibular, and vertebral involvement may also occur, the latter often being asymptomatic. Cutaneous manifestations (such as palmoplantar pustulosis), articular features, or gut inflammation may coexist, placing the disease within the broader spectrum of Synovitis, Acne, Pustulosis, Hyperostosis, and Osteitis (SAPHO) syndrome. Diagnosis is based on imaging, with whole-body MRI being the gold standard in children. It reveals multiple, symmetric inflammatory bone lesions often exceeding the clinically apparent sites. Bone biopsy is reserved for atypical or unifocal presentations or when a diagnostic uncertainty persists. Non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) are the first-line treatment. In refractory cases or in patients with vertebral involvement, second-line therapies - including intravenous bisphosphonates or TNF inhibitors - may be considered off-label. Management primarily aims to control pain and preserve quality of life. Overall prognosis is favourable, with spontaneous remission in most patients after a median disease duration of four years. However, up to 50% of patients still experience flares after five years, and orthopaedic sequelae or spinal deformities may persist. General practitioners play a key role in early recognition, appropriate referral to specialist care, avoidance of unnecessary bone biopsies, and initial therapeutic management.
