title: Synchrotron X-ray Data of non-diseased and diabetic Human Pancreas Tissue and Islet Segmentation Model.
abstract: Three-dimensional virtual histology using synchrotron radiation micro-computed tomography enables non-destructive visualization of biological tissue microarchitecture with isotropic resolution. To support quantitative studies of human pancreatic morphology, we provide high-resolution 3D X-ray imaging datasets of 55 pancreatic tissue cores from 32 individuals. The collection comprises histologically non-diseased pancreatic tissue from organ donors and non-neoplastic regions of surgical resection specimens from patients with pancreatic cancer, including subgroups with insulin-dependent diabetes or following neoadjuvant chemotherapy. Formalin-fixed, paraffin-embedded tissue cores with a diameter of 1 mm were imaged at 650 nm isotropic voxel size, yielding a mean effective spatial resolution of 1.66 µm. The cohort includes reconstructed volumes, corresponding immunohistochemistry, clinical metadata, expert-validated annotations, and dataset-specific example 2.5D U-Net models for automated segmentation of islets of Langerhans. A representative co-registered section yielded a Dice similarity coefficient of 0.81 and intersection-over-union of 0.67. This openly accessible, FAIR-compliant resource supports quantitative analysis of endocrine, exocrine, ductal, and stromal architecture and provides a reproducible reference framework for three-dimensional virtual histology of human pancreatic tissue and computational benchmarking.

title: Effects of risedronate on volumetric bone mineral density and CT-derived muscle-bone associations after sleeve gastrectomy: a pilot randomized controlled trial.
abstract: Sleeve gastrectomy (SG) is an effective surgical treatment for severe obesity but is associated with bone mineral density (BMD) loss. This analysis investigates postoperative bisphosphonate effects on computed tomography (CT)-derived compartmental volumetric BMD (vBMD) and associations with CT-derived muscle outcomes. The 6-month pilot study randomized 24 SG patients to once-monthly 150 mg risedronate (n = 11) or placebo (n = 13). CT scans were collected at baseline, and 6- and 12-months postoperatively to assess hip and spine vBMD. Treatment effects were estimated using a mixed linear model adjusted for sex and baseline measures, and Pearson correlations with CT-derived muscle outcomes were assessed. There were no significant vBMD differences between risedronate vs. placebo groups after SG, but 6-month trends suggest vBMD losses [mg/cm 3 ] with risedronate were potentially attenuated in the trabecular compartment of the total hip [- 8.8 vs. - 9.6], femoral neck [- 3.6 vs. - 7.3], and L1-L4 vertebrae [- 8.4 vs. - 11.1]. Muscle-bone correlations were not significant but trends suggest larger and less fat infiltrated trunk muscles may protect against spine vBMD loss. This pilot study did not find a significant treatment effect of risedronate on vBMD in SG patients, but exploratory findings in relation with muscle measures warrant additional investigation in a larger study.

title: Contextualizing biological heterogeneity in brain structural normativity assessments across the aging continuum with the nearest neighbor normativity framework.
abstract: Background Despite established consensus about the individuality of brain physiology and structural changes, current neuroimaging biomarker paradigms heavily rely on population averages. Here, we define normativity not as a single reference point but as a landscape of permissible configurations arising from diverse physiological manifestations. Methods We introduce the Nearest Neighbor Normativity (N 3 ) framework, designed to parse the natural heterogeneity in brain structural measurements into a diversity-aware biomarker of brain structural decline. Through repeated comparisons within different demographic subgroups, N 3 contextualizes an individual's measurements from several viewpoints along the aging continuum. Relying on local density estimation, it accommodates multiple, shared normative configurations within and across age groups. We use T1-weighted MRI data from 29,883 individuals for training and 7,013 individuals for validation, and benchmark our framework against Brain Age models and Normative Modeling. We evaluate each biomarker's ability to detect neurodegenerative diseases, using them as representative models of atypical brain structural decline. Results In group-level analyses, the N 3 biomarker shows the largest effect sizes in the detection of Mild Cognitive Impairment, Alzheimer's Disease, and Frontotemporal Dementia. Similarly, the N 3 biomarker achieves the highest predictive performance in the classification of neurodegenerative diseases on a single subject level. Notably, the N 3 estimates remain stable across age and robust to compositional changes in the reference sample. Finally, correlation analyses indicate that it captures distinct and complementary aspects of brain structural variation compared to existing approaches. Conclusions Our findings underscore that rethinking normativity assessments to explicitly accommodate natural inter-individual variability can advance our collective efforts toward truly personalized patient care.

Background

Despite established consensus about the individuality of brain physiology and structural changes, current neuroimaging biomarker paradigms heavily rely on population averages. Here, we define normativity not as a single reference point but as a landscape of permissible configurations arising from diverse physiological manifestations.

Methods

We introduce the Nearest Neighbor Normativity (N3) framework, designed to parse the natural heterogeneity in brain structural measurements into a diversity-aware biomarker of brain structural decline. Through repeated comparisons within different demographic subgroups, N3 contextualizes an individual's measurements from several viewpoints along the aging continuum. Relying on local density estimation, it accommodates multiple, shared normative configurations within and across age groups. We use T1-weighted MRI data from 29,883 individuals for training and 7,013 individuals for validation, and benchmark our framework against Brain Age models and Normative Modeling. We evaluate each biomarker's ability to detect neurodegenerative diseases, using them as representative models of atypical brain structural decline.

Results

In group-level analyses, the N3 biomarker shows the largest effect sizes in the detection of Mild Cognitive Impairment, Alzheimer's Disease, and Frontotemporal Dementia. Similarly, the N3 biomarker achieves the highest predictive performance in the classification of neurodegenerative diseases on a single subject level. Notably, the N3 estimates remain stable across age and robust to compositional changes in the reference sample. Finally, correlation analyses indicate that it captures distinct and complementary aspects of brain structural variation compared to existing approaches.

Conclusions

Our findings underscore that rethinking normativity assessments to explicitly accommodate natural inter-individual variability can advance our collective efforts toward truly personalized patient care.

title: Recent progress in biomarker-responsive fluorescent probes for real-time monitoring of glioblastoma.
abstract: Glioblastoma (GBM) is highly infiltrative and heterogeneous, making accurate tumor delineation and real-time assessment of its dynamic microenvironment particularly challenging. Biomarker-responsive fluorescent probes offer a promising route to molecularly informed contrast beyond conventional fluorescence accumulation. This review summarizes recent advances, particularly since 2023, in probes responsive to biothiols and sulfur species, reactive oxygen and nitrogen species, formaldehyde, enzymes, protein-binding events, mitochondrial viscosity, and polarity. We organize these systems according to response mechanism and critically compare their delivery, optical transduction, and validation across cell-based, subcutaneous, orthotopic, and human-tissue settings. Recent developments have shifted the field from single-analyte turn-on probes toward multiplexed molecular profiling, reversible receptor-localized redox imaging, and multi-enzyme activation. However, probe delivery, target accessibility, and irreversible signal accumulation can complicate interpretation of fluorescence as a quantitative measure of biomarker dynamics. Future progress will require rigorous control of selectivity, pharmacokinetics, temporal response, and orthogonal biological validation, together with margin-level evaluation in clinically relevant GBM models. These advances may enable biomarker-responsive fluorescence imaging to evolve from tumor visualization toward biologically interpretable monitoring and more precise fluorescence-guided surgery.

title: Design and analytical validation of a graphene oxide-modified FTO immunosensor for NT-proBNP detection.
abstract: Heart failure (HF) remains a leading cause of global morbidity and mortality, with timely and accurate biomarker quantification being critical for diagnosis, risk stratification, and therapeutic monitoring. N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) is the most clinically reliable biomarker for HF; however, current detection platforms, ranging from chemiluminescent immunoassays to lateral flow devices, are limited by high infrastructure requirements, enzymatic labels, complex fabrication workflows, or insufficient sensitivity at physiologically critical concentrations. Here, we report a label-free, reagent minimised electrochemical immunosensor fabricated by depositing carboxyl functionalised graphene oxide (GO) on fluorine-doped tin oxide (FTO) glass electrodes, followed by covalent antibody immobilization via EDC-NHS-PEG chemistry. The platform is scalable, cost-effective, and compatible with portable electrochemical instrumentation, establishing a strong foundation for point-of-care integration. These findings provide a promising foundation for future optimisation of the GO-FTO immunosensor, including clinical sample validation, device integration, and translation towards point-of-care heart failure diagnostics.

title: Activatable hypoxia magnetic resonance imaging for early stratification of radiotherapy response.
abstract: Tumor hypoxia is a major cause of radioresistance and heterogeneous outcomes in radiotherapy (RT). Noninvasive strategies capable of quantifying tumor hypoxia prior to treatment are essential for precision radiotherapy and prognostic stratification. Here, we developed an activatable hypoxia magnetic resonance imaging (ahMRI) nanoprobe (HIG) that translates hypoxia-induced chemical cues into distance-dependent T 1 relaxation signals. In a 4T1 breast cancer model, ahMRI demonstrated strong correlations with canonical hypoxia biomarkers from pimonidazole staining. Importantly, pre-treatment ahMRI readouts enabled early discrimination between RT responders and non-responders. Moreover, the change in the signal-to-noise ratio (ΔSNR tumor ) value before RT was significantly associated with immune response, including cytotoxic T cell infiltration and M1/M2 macrophage ratios, as well as with tumor growth suppression. These findings highlight the pivotal role of tumor oxygenation in shaping RT efficacy and establish ahMRI as a noninvasive platform for early outcome prediction. This nanoplatform provides a promising avenue for precision-guided RT and individualized cancer treatment.

title: A chemometrically validated discriminative sensing strategy combining biomolecular specificity with data-driven classification of Aβ 1-40 fibrils.
abstract: Achieving selective and sensitive early detection of amyloid-β (Aβ 1-40 ) fibrils, the hallmark of neurodegenerative disease, in the presence of monomers and abundant serum proteins remains a long-standing major challenge for detecting the disease at its preclinical stage. Here, we report a rationally designed fluorescent probe that exhibits a pronounced 585 nm emission enhancement, enabling rapid and selective identification of Aβ 1-40 fibrils with minimal background interference, highlighting its potential for detecting Aβ 1-40 fibrils. The probe shows negligible response toward monomers and common proteins, including human serum albumin (HSA), bovine serum albumin (BSA), and lysozyme, demonstrating high selectivity to Aβ 1-40 fibrils. Mechanistic studies using NMR (Nuclear Magnetic Resonance), FTIR (Fourier-Transform Infrared), CD (Circular Dichroism), and UV-visible spectroscopy reveal that the sensing response arises from specific probe-fibril interactions, including site-dependent binding and π-π stacking with β-sheet structures. CD and FTIR analyses confirm fibril formation and structural integrity, while NMR provides molecular-level evidence of binding-induced perturbations. Chemometric analysis, including principal component analysis (PCA), hierarchical cluster analysis (HCA), k-nearest neighbours (kNN), and partial least squares discriminant analysis (PLS-DA), enables clear classification of fibrils, monomers, and protein interferents with an accuracy of 88.8% and 90%, using fluorescence and absorbance, respectively, validating the potential of the sensing platform. This work establishes a chemometrically validated sensing strategy that combines molecular specificity with data-driven classification via both absorbance and emission spectroscopy, offering a scalable approach for the selective detection of Aβ 1-40 fibrils relevant to Alzheimer's disease (AD) diagnostics.

title: A chromone-based Schiff base derivative for the Cd 2+ -promoted detection of l-proline: validated by DFT, test strip, cotton swab, fish tissue, cellular imaging, and real/herbal water recovery analysis.
abstract: l-proline is a vital stress marker in plants and an indicator of food quality and clinical diagnosis. In this work, we applied a simple chromone-based Schiff base derivative, ( E )-3-(((3-mercapto-5-phenyl-4 H -1,2,4-triazol-4-yl)imino)methyl)-4 H -chromen-4-one (CT), for the Cd 2+ -complex-promoted detection of l-proline in acetonitrile. Within 10 minutes of incubation, the CT-Cd 2+ complex exhibited a strong PL "Turn-On" response in the presence of l-proline among the amino acids, which remained stable between pH 3 and 8. The Job's plot and 1 H NMR (nuclear magnetic resonance)-based titration studies confirmed the 1 : 1 stoichiometry of CT + Cd 2+ to l-proline. Between 0.1 µM and 300 µM, the PL linear dynamic range of CT + Cd 2+ to l-proline was observed, with a limit of detection (LOD) of 141 nM and an association constant ( K a ) of 4.25 × 10 3 M -1 using the Benesi-Hildebrand plot. The mode of binding and the possible photoinduced electron transfer/fluorescence resonance energy transfer (PET/FRET) mechanism are defined by FTIR spectroscopy, 1 H NMR, HR mass spectrometry, and density functional theory (DFT) studies. l-proline sensing by the Cd 2+ complex-promoted technique is corroborated using a test strip, cotton swab, fish tissue, and A549/MCF-7 cellular imaging. l-proline recovery from tap water and herbal water extracts (including Astragalus root (AA), Hedysari root (NAAI), and Coastal Glehnia root (SGC)) ranged from 89.89% to 113.98%. This unique design drives future innovation for l-proline monitoring in biological and environmental samples.

title: π-Bridge engineering of NIR-II fluorophore nanoparticles for high-contrast bioimaging and image-guided surgery.
abstract: Early and accurate diagnosis is essential to timely clinical intervention. Compared with conventional imaging modalities such as magnetic resonance imaging and computed tomography, which remain subject to high cost, inadequate resolution, or ionizing radiation, near-infrared (NIR) fluorescence imaging provides high sensitivity, excellent spatial resolution, and minimal invasiveness. Nevertheless, the development of highly bright NIR fluorophores remains challenging because simultaneous optimization of the molar absorption coefficient ( ε ) and quantum yield ( Φ PL ) is difficult to achieve. Here, TPE-HEXOT-DPTQ is rationally designed through π-bridge engineering to balance molecular planarity and distortion. The concurrent optimization of ε and Φ PL endowed TPE-HEXOT-DPTQ nanoparticles with the highest fluorescence brightness, together with exceptional colloidal stability, photostability, and biocompatibility. In vivo NIR-II fluorescence imaging demonstrated remarkable tissue penetration, high spatial resolution, and superior signal-to-background ratios, enabling clear visualization of intricate vascular architectures, including cerebral and auricular vasculature. In subcutaneous breast cancer and orthotopic colorectal tumor models, TPE-HEXOT-DPTQ nanoparticles not only achieved high-contrast tumor imaging but also enabled precise surgical resection of malignant tissues. This work establishes a rational molecular design strategy for high-performance NIR-II fluorophores and highlights their considerable promise for bioimaging and imaging-guided surgery.

title: PFH-loaded hollow iron oxide nanoparticles suppress breast cancer progression through magnetothermal ferroptosis and inhibition of TGF-β1/Smad-driven EMT.
abstract: Breast cancer metastasis remains a major cause of mortality, and epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) is a key process driving tumor progression. Here, we developed perfluorohexane-loaded hollow iron oxide nanoparticles (PFH-HIONs) as a magnetothermal phase-transition platform for image-guided breast cancer therapy. PFH-HIONs were synthesized by vacuum-assisted loading of PFH into hollow iron oxide nanoparticles and characterized for morphology, size, zeta potential, magnetothermal performance, and ultrasound phase-transition behavior. Their antitumor effects were evaluated in MCF-7 cells and in a xenograft model. Ferroptosis-related changes, EMT-associated signaling, macrophage polarization, and immune-related responses were further assessed. PFH-HIONs showed a hollow nanostructure, AMF-responsive heating, and stimulus-triggered ultrasound contrast enhancement. PFH-HIONs combined with AMF reduced MCF-7 cell viability and increased apoptotic cell death. This treatment also induced ferroptosis-related changes, including GPX4 downregulation, 4-HNE and ACSL4 upregulation, and ROS accumulation. In TGF-β1-treated MCF-7 cells, PFH-HION plus AMF suppressed Smad2/3 phosphorylation, reversed EMT-associated protein and transcription factor expression, and these effects were partially attenuated by ferrostatin-1. In addition, PFH-HIONs plus AMF promoted a more pro-inflammatory macrophage phenotype, and conditioned medium from treated tumor cells induced a similar macrophage reprogramming. In vivo , PFH-HIONs plus AMF inhibited tumor growth, increased necrosis, reduced Ki67, and were associated with increased intratumoral infiltration of CD8-positive lymphocyte-like cells and elevated IFN-γ levels, with acceptable short-term biosafety. PFH-HIONs function as a magnetothermal phase-transition nanoplatform with antitumor activity associated with ferroptosis, EMT suppression, and immune-related tumor microenvironment changes, supporting further investigation for image-guided breast cancer therapy.

PFH-HIONs combined with AMF reduced MCF-7 cell viability and increased apoptotic cell death. This treatment also induced ferroptosis-related changes, including GPX4 downregulation, 4-HNE and ACSL4 upregulation, and ROS accumulation. In TGF-β1-treated MCF-7 cells, PFH-HION plus AMF suppressed Smad2/3 phosphorylation, reversed EMT-associated protein and transcription factor expression, and these effects were partially attenuated by ferrostatin-1. In addition, PFH-HIONs plus AMF promoted a more pro-inflammatory macrophage phenotype, and conditioned medium from treated tumor cells induced a similar macrophage reprogramming. In vivo, PFH-HIONs plus AMF inhibited tumor growth, increased necrosis, reduced Ki67, and were associated with increased intratumoral infiltration of CD8-positive lymphocyte-like cells and elevated IFN-γ levels, with acceptable short-term biosafety. PFH-HIONs function as a magnetothermal phase-transition nanoplatform with antitumor activity associated with ferroptosis, EMT suppression, and immune-related tumor microenvironment changes, supporting further investigation for image-guided breast cancer therapy.

title: Imageless Robot-assisted Lateral Unicompartmental Knee Arthroplasty.
abstract: Background Lateral unicompartmental knee arthroplasty (UKA) is a technically demanding procedure because of the unique anatomy, biomechanics, and frequent posterolateral wear of the lateral compartment. Robotic assistance may improve accuracy and reproducibility. Purpose To describe a step-by-step technique for imageless robotic-assisted lateral UKA. Surgical technique The procedure is performed through a lateral parapatellar approach using the imageless CORI platform. Key steps include confirmation of isolated lateral osteoarthritis, imageless registration, dynamic ligament assessment, implant planning to address posterolateral wear while preserving constitutional valgus alignment, robotic bone preparation, and final implantation with assessment of alignment and ligament balance. Discussion Imageless robotic systems avoid preoperative CT imaging and enable real-time planning based on intraoperative soft-tissue assessment. These features may be particularly advantageous in lateral UKA. Conclusion Imageless robotic-assisted lateral UKA using the CORI system is a reproducible technique for isolated lateral compartment osteoarthritis. Accurate registration, preservation of native alignment, and dynamic assessment of ligament function are key principles for successful reconstruction.

title: Comparative efficacy of ultrasound versus elbow arthrography in treating Monteggia fractures in young children.
abstract: Purpose This study aims to compare the effectiveness and clinical value of ultrasound-assisted and arthrography-assisted treatment for acute Monteggia fractures in young children. Methods We conducted a retrospective analysis of 40 cases of acute Monteggia fractures in children treated with Kirschner wire or elastic intramedullary nail fixation between April 2020 and April 2025. Among these cases, 19 were treated under arthrography assistance (Group A), and 21 were treated under ultrasound guidance (Group B). We recorded baseline data for both groups, including gender, age, fracture side and type, associated injuries, time from injury to surgery, internal fixation device, fluoroscopy time, surgical duration, follow-up duration, and internal fixation removal time. Postoperative X-ray examination was performed to assess the quality of fracture reduction. Results Fluoroscopy time and surgical duration in Group B were significantly lower than in Group A (P < 0.05). Based on the evaluation criteria for assessing reduction quality, 17 cases were graded excellent, and 2 were considered good in Group A, while in Group B, 20 cases were deemed excellent and 1 was considered good. At the final follow-up, there was no significant difference in the range of elbow flexion, extension, pronation, and supination between the affected limbs of Group A and Group B (P > 0.05). Conclusion Ultrasound not only saves surgical time and reduces intraoperative radiation exposure for the patients but also enables the exploration of peripheral nerves, vessels, and soft tissue compressions.

title: Surgical versus Conservative Treatment of Isolated Posterior Malleolar Fractures: Clinical, Radiological, and Pedobarographic Outcomes.
abstract: Background Optimal management of isolated posterior malleolar (PM) fractures remains controversial, particularly regarding the influence of fracture fragment size on treatment selection and outcomes. Purpose To compare clinical, radiological, and pedobarographic outcomes of surgically and conservatively treated isolated PM fractures and to assess the effect of fracture fragment size on outcomes. Study design Retrospective observational study. Methods Patients with isolated PM fractures were divided into surgical and conservative groups. Fracture classification and fragment size were assessed using plain radiographs and computed tomography (CT). Clinical evaluation included the American Orthopaedic Foot and Ankle Society (AOFAS) score, visual analog scale (VAS) for pain, ankle range of motion, and radiographic osteoarthritis graded by the Kellgren-Lawrence classification. Static and dynamic pedobarographic analyses were performed. Subgroup analyses were conducted according to CT-measured fragment size. Results Thirty patients were included. CT measurements revealed significantly larger fragment sizes than plain radiographs (p < 0.001). Surgical treatment was associated with higher AOFAS scores and lower VAS pain scores than conservative treatment in this non-randomized cohort. In the subgroup with fragments involving more than 25% of the articular surface, surgically treated patients had higher AOFAS scores and lower pain scores; this exploratory comparison included only 10 surgical and 4 conservatively treated patients. No consistent pedobarographic differences were detected, although these exploratory comparisons were likely underpowered. Contralateral hindfoot pressure differed in one comparison. Conclusion Surgical treatment was associated with higher functional scores and lower pain levels in this small, non-randomized cohort. The apparent difference in the > 25% subgroup is exploratory and requires confirmation in larger studies. CT-based assessment provided more detailed evaluation of fracture morphology and may assist treatment planning.

title: Agreement and Interobserver Reliability of Radiographic Measurements for Pes Planus Assessment in Young Adults.
abstract: Background Radiographic measurements of pes planus may differ in classification outcomes and interobserver reliability. Purpose To compare three radiographic angles in young adults regarding pes planus classification agreement and interobserver reliability, and to examine the influence of the observer on classification. Study design Retrospective radiographic measurement study. Methods This study included 300 participants (600 feet; mean age, 18.48 years). Bilateral weight-bearing lateral radiographs were evaluated using calcaneal pitch, talar declination, and Meary's angles. Pes planus was suggested by calcaneal pitch <20°, talar declination >24°, or plantar-convex Meary's angle >4°. Classification rates were compared using Cochran's Q and McNemar's tests, agreement using Cohen's kappa and prevalence-adjusted kappa and interobserver reliability using intraclass correlation coefficients (ICCs) among three observers who each measured the same 80 participants (160 feet) RESULTS: Classification rates differed significantly among measurements bilaterally (Cochran's Q, p < 0.001). Calcaneal pitch yielded the highest positive classification rate on the right (37.7%), whereas talar declination yielded the highest rate on the left (38.3%). Agreement between calcaneal pitch and talar declination was no better than chance (right κ = -0.031; left κ = -0.037). Between the two residents' patient series, classification rates for talar declination and Meary's angle differed (e.g., right Meary's angle, 42.7% vs 6.0%), whereas those for calcaneal pitch did not (34.7% vs 40.7%) On the same radiographs, Meary's angle classified 9.4% to 59.4% of feet as suggestive of pes planus, depending on the observer. Calcaneal pitch demonstrated good interobserver reliability (ICC = 0.860), whereas talar declination (ICC = 0.214) and Meary's angle (ICC = 0.219) showed poor reliability. Conclusions Pes planus classification varied across radiographic measurements, with generally low agreement. Classification also depended on the observer, most markedly for talar declination and Meary's angle Calcaneal pitch showed the highest interobserver reliability, emphasizing the importance of standardized measurement methods, observer training, and classification thresholds. Level of clinical evidence Level 4.

title: Preoperative Prediction of Lymphovascular Invasion in Breast Cancer Using MRI-Based Radiomics: a systematic review and diagnostic test accuracy (DTA) meta-analysis.
abstract: Rationale and objectives Lymphovascular invasion (LVI) is a major adverse prognostic factor in breast cancer, associated with increased risk of nodal and distant metastasis. It is typically confirmed on histopathological examination of surgical specimens, while reliable preoperative assessment remains limited due to the constraints of core needle biopsy. This meta-analysis evaluates the diagnostic value of MRI radiomics in detecting LVI in breast cancer patients. Materials and methods A comprehensive search of PubMed, Embase, Scopus, and Web of Science was conducted. Eligible studies were studies developing radiomics-based predictive models using machine learning techniques, and studies using clinical-only models were excluded. SROC model curves were implemented using Reitsma's bivariate model. The pooled effect size was analyzed using the inverse-variance method. Publication bias was assessed using Deeks' funnel plot. The methodological quality was assessed using the QUADAS-2 tool, the Radiomics Quality Score (RQS) and the METhodological RadiomICs Score (METRICS). This study was prospectively registered with PROSPERO (CRD420251186235). Results 23 studies published from 2019 to 2025 were included in the review. Seventeen studies (n=1,668) were included in the SROC analysis, yielding an AUC of 0.83 (95% CI 0.80-0.85), with pooled sensitivity of 0.73 and specificity of 0.80. The pooled AUC analysis including all 23 studies (n=1,902), was 0.78 (95% CI 0.75-0.81), with moderate heterogeneity (I²=33.6%). Externally validated models showed higher sensitivity than internally validated models (0.83 vs. 0.62, p=0.02), while performance did not differ significantly by feature extraction software, MRI field strength or segmentation region. Deeks' funnel plot showed no statistically significant evidence of publication bias (p=0.49). Conclusion MRI-based radiomics show promising diagnostic performance for preoperative prediction of LVI. This is relevant in the neoadjuvant era, where treatment response may obscure histopathologic evidence of LVI and mask an important adverse prognostic factor. Prospective studies with robust external validation are needed.

title: [The infected diabetic foot syndrome - diagnosis, treatment, and interdisciplinary care].
abstract: Abstract Diabetic foot syndrome (DFS) is one of the most severe long-term complications of diabetes mellitus and represents the leading cause of non-traumatic lower extremity amputations in industrialized nations. While the pathogenesis of foot ulcerations is primarily driven by a combination of diabetic polyneuropathy and peripheral arterial disease (PAD), secondary infections are frequently the main trigger for critical tissue loss. Consequently, these infections necessitate urgent inpatient admission and often result in major amputations as a last resort.The diagnosis of a diabetic foot infection is fundamentally based on clinical presentation. Key components for successful management include the early detection of underlying osteomyelitis, the identification of relevant perfusion deficits, and the immediate initiation of a structured, multimodal therapy regimen. This standard regimen comprises targeted surgical debridement, consistent pressure offloading, pathogen-specific antimicrobial therapy, and prompt vascular revascularization. Due to the highly complex underlying pathophysiology, patients with advanced disease stages benefit substantially from organized interdisciplinary care involving diabetologists, specialized podiatric surgeons, vascular surgeons, interventional radiologists, clinical infectious disease specialists, and orthopedic shoemakers. This comprehensive article provides a highly practice-oriented overview of the modern diagnosis and therapeutic management of the infected diabetic foot, strictly aligned with the current recommendations of the German Diabetes Society (DDG) and the International Working Group on the Diabetic Foot (IWGDF).

title: Prospective evaluation of deep-learning tools for the endoscopic detection of gastric precancerous conditions and eosinophilic esophagitis in a real-life cohort.
abstract: Background Neuronal-network-based methods have increasingly been applied to various tasks in gastrointestinal endoscopy, but prospective data are scarce. Recently, we published two Deep-Learning (DL) classifiers for the detection of gastric precancerous conditions (GPC) and eosinophilic esophagitis (EoE). Our aim was to investigate real-life performance of these tools in an unselected dataset of consecutive patients. Patients and methods In total, 650 patients undergoing esophagogastroduodenoscopy were recruited. Endoscopists selected up to six images in predefined scope positions (Loc 1-4 proximal stomach; Loc 5-6 esophagus) for evaluation. Finally, 1681 images of 583 patients were analyzed for GPC. title: [Cone beam CT-guided bronchoscopic navigation: step by step].
abstract: Abstract The assessment of peripheral lung lesions (PPH) is gaining increasing importance with the introduction of lung cancer screening using low-dose CT. Bronchoscopic navigation techniques, such as electromagnetic or virtual navigation bronchoscopy or robot-assisted bronchoscopy, are used for histological evaluation and have improved diagnostic accuracy. Navigation to the lesion using a preoperative chest CT scan can be inaccurate, particularly for small lesions or those in the lower lobe, due to CT-to-body divergence. Intraoperative 3D imaging using cone beam CT (CBCT) can significantly improve diagnostic accuracy. The combination of modern navigation techniques and CBCT is non-inferior to CT-guided transthoracic biopsy in terms of diagnostic accuracy and has a significantly more favorable risk profile. This article provides a detailed step-by-step description of how to perform CBCT-guided bronchoscopy.

title: 18F-Fluorodeoxyglucose Positron Emission Tomographic/Computed Tomographic Findings and Post-Therapeutic Radioiodine Avidity in Differentiated Thyroid Cancer Patients with Suspected Distant Metastases.
abstract: Aim The aim of this study was to investigate the role of 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography/computed tomography in detecting distant metastasis and its influence on treatment planning before radioactive iodine therapy in differentiated thyroid cancer patients. Methods This retrospective study included 106 postoperative differentiated thyroid cancer patients who underwent 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography/computed tomography due to suspected metastasis (elevated thyroglobulin or anti-thyroglobulin antibodies). 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomographic/computed tomographic findings were analyzed alongside post-therapy whole-body scintigraphy and clinical data. Results 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography/computed tomography identified distant metastases in 45 of 106 patients (42%). Pre-ablation baseline laboratory data revealed a median serum thyroglobulin level of 25.5 ng/mL (range: 0.01->500 ng/mL) and a median anti-thyroglobulin antibody level of 13 IU/mL (range: 2-4,000 IU/mL). The lung was the most common site (56%), followed by multi-organ involvement (22%). Among the 45 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography/computed tomography-positive patients, post-therapy whole-body scintigraphy demonstrated radioactive iodine uptake in 32 cases (71%), whereas 13 of 45 patients (29%) exhibited no uptake, representing radioactive iodine-non-avid disease. Conversely, among the 61 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography/computed tomography-negative patients, post-therapy whole-body scintigraphy identified a distant metastasis in only one patient (1.6%). Conclusion Pre-therapeutic 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography/computed tomography complements imaging for detecting distant metastases in differentiated thyroid cancer patients with unexplained thyroglobulin or anti-thyroglobulin elevation. Integration of fluorodeoxyglucose uptake and post-therapy radioactive iodine avidity enables individualized treatment planning, distinguishing radioactive iodine-responsive lesions from refractory disease and guiding radioiodine dose optimization and alternative therapies.

title: The Therapeutic Pipeline: Future Treatments and Precision Medicine.
abstract: Abstract Rare interstitial lung diseases (ILDs) represent a heterogeneous group of disorders characterized by various pathogenic mechanisms, clinical presentations, prognoses, and therapeutic challenges. Among these, acid sphingomyelinase deficiency (ASMD), pulmonary alveolar proteinosis (PAP), and pulmonary Langerhans cell histiocytosis (PLCH) exemplify rare pulmonary diseases driven by distinct biological mechanisms, including lysosomal dysfunction, impaired surfactant homeostasis, and activation of the mitogen-activated protein kinases (MAPK) pathways. Recent advancements in molecular biology, genomics, and translational research boosted the development of precision medicine strategies and disease-specific therapies for these conditions. This narrative review was conducted in accordance with the SANRA guidelines. A thorough literature search of the PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, and Scopus databases was performed from January 2000 to June 2026. Significant progress has been made in treating all three diseases. In ASMD, enzyme replacement therapy with olipudase alfa has greatly improved visceral and lung symptoms, while research in gene therapy, gene editing, and metabolic treatments is ongoing. For PAP, inhaled granulocyte-macrophage colony-stimulating factor (GM-CSF) is now the primary disease-specific treatment, now supported by phase III trial evidence for inhaled molgramostim, complemented by potential therapies such as immunomodulation, macrophage transplantation, and gene-based strategies. In PLCH, the discovery of recurrent MAPK pathway variants has supported the use of genotype-targeted treatments with B-Raf proto-oncogene, serine (BRAF)/threonine kinase and mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK)/extracellular signal-regulated kinase (ERK) kinase inhibitors. Under these conditions, advances in molecular diagnostics, circulating biomarkers, quantitative high-resolution computed tomography (HRCT), radiomics, and artificial intelligence (AI) are poised to enhance diagnosis, patient stratification, prognosis, and treatment decisions. ASMD, PAP, and PLCH are entering into an era of precision medicine, in which disease-specific molecular mechanisms play an increasing role in guiding diagnosis and treatment. Ongoing integration of genomics, biomarkers, advanced imaging, AI, and targeted therapies could revolutionize the management of conditions such as ASMD, PAP, and PLCH, leading to better long-term patient outcomes.

title: Technology-Enabled Skin Longevity Optimization.
abstract: Aims and Backgrounds: Facial aging is a multifactorial process involving cellular senescence, ultraviolet damage, and structural decline across the epidermis, dermis, subcutaneous fat, and superficial musculoaponeurotic system. Contemporary rejuvenation has evolved beyond surgical repositioning toward biologically targeted cutaneous optimization. Technology Energy-based technologies including laser photothermolysis, radiofrequency-mediated dermal thermomodulation, microfocused ultrasound, and emerging microwave and cryobiologic modalities induce controlled tissue injury that activates wound-healing pathways, fibroblast proliferation, and extracellular matrix remodeling. Techniques Regenerative strategies including microneedling-assisted mechanotransduction, platelet-derived biologics, autologous fat grafting, collagen biostimulators, and extracellular vesicle therapies provide biologically oriented tissue restoration through paracrine signaling and matrix synthesis. Current and Future Development: Artificial intelligence applications in facial phenotyping, treatment planning, and outcome assessment are emerging. Future directions include senescence-targeting therapies and precision-based multimodal protocols. Conclusions and clinical relevance Multimodal treatment sequencing addressing multiple anatomical layers represents the contemporary standard. Integration of device-based technologies with regenerative adjuncts enables biologically informed, individualized facial rejuvenation.

title: OVARIAN PRESERVATION IN PEDIATRIC OVARIAN TORSION: A SYSTEMATIC REVIEW SUPPORTING DETORSION REGARDLESS OF TIMING OR INTRAOPERATIVE APPEARANCE.
abstract: Introduction One in five children with ovarian torsion undergo oophorectomy and/or salpingectomy. We sought to evaluate the current evidence regarding the timing of operative intervention, intraoperative decision making and postoperative follow-up in the management of pediatric ovarian torsion. Our goal is to optimize adnexal conservation in this population. Methods A systematic review (PROSPERO CRD42024605394) was conducted following PRISMA guidelines. PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, ClinicalTrials.gov, and Mednar were searched for studies from 2010-2023 including pediatric patients (1-18 years) with benign ovarian torsion. Three clinical questions were addressed: (1) safe time window for operative detorsion based on symptom duration, (2) intraoperative findings guiding ovarian preservation, and (3) optimal timing of postoperative surveillance ultrasound. Results Of 1,035 screened studies, 19 met inclusion criteria (7 cohort studies, 12 case reports), with a total of 248 patients and 250 torsed ovaries. These studies were heterogenous in their reporting and overall have a level of evidence of 4. Ovarian conservation surgery was performed in 234/250 (94%) ovaries. Among those with documented follow-up (222/234, 95%), postoperative ultrasound demonstrated ovarian viability in 190/222 (86%). Delayed presentation and ischemic appearance did not reliably predict loss of function. Conclusion Ovarian conservation should be attempted in all cases of benign pediatric ovarian torsion, regardless of symptom duration or intraoperative appearance. Postoperative ultrasound within three months of detorsion is recommended to confirm ovarian viability and standardize follow-up care.

title: Knowledge, Compliance, and Associated Factors of Radiation Protection Adherence Among Dental Students, Interns, and Dentists: A Cross-Sectional Study.
abstract: Objectives Dental radiography is essential for diagnosis and treatment planning, but exposure to ionizing radiation requires strict adherence to radiation protection principles. This study evaluated radiation protection knowledge, self-reported compliance, and their associated factors among dental students, interns, and dentists. Materials and methods A cross-sectional study included 136 participants (86.1% response rate). A content-reviewed bilingual questionnaire assessed 7 knowledge items (6 scored in the composite knowledge score) and 12 self-reported compliance items. Pilot testing, translation, content validity (scale-level average content validity index [S-CVI/Ave] = 0.91), and internal consistency (α = 0.78; Kuder-Richardson Formula 20 [KR-20] = 0.70) were evaluated. Multivariable ordinary least squares regression examined factors associated with compliance using SPSS 27 and Python software. Results The composite knowledge score was 0.804; the pediatric radiation protection item had a correct-response rate of 54.4% (single-item assessment). Mean compliance was 3.09/4. Composite knowledge score was independently associated with self-reported compliance ( B = 1.092, 95% confidence interval: 0.817-1.366, p < 0.001). Compliance was significantly lower among Year 5 students and interns than among Year 3 students ( p = 0.037 and p = 0.005, respectively), whereas gender and the remaining training-level contrasts were not significant ( R 2 = 0.360). Knowledge showed a moderate-to-strong positive correlation with compliance ( rₛ = 0.528, p < 0.001). Exploratory analyses indicated a stronger knowledge-compliance association among more advanced trainees (Year 5, interns, and dentists/faculty) than among earlier-year students. The largest compliance gaps involved X-ray image repetition frequency, use of protective shielding devices, and motion-restraining tools. Conclusion Composite knowledge score was independently associated with self-reported compliance, and adjusted compliance was lower among Year 5 students and interns than among Year 3 students. However, the cross-sectional design and reliance on self-reported data preclude causal interpretation. Lower compliance was observed for X-ray image repetition frequency, protective shielding devices, and motion-restraining tools. These findings support competency-based training and curriculum review, but recommendations remain exploratory and require confirmation in larger multi-institutional prospective studies.

title: Radiographic manifestations of pneumatosis intestinalis and construction of an AI-assisted diagnostic system.
abstract: Pneumatosis intestinalis (PI) has a wide range of etiologies, and the imaging differentiation between benign and ischemic PI is difficult, leading to a high risk of missed diagnosis. This study systematically summarizes the CT (Computed Tomography) imaging manifestations of PI and constructs an AI (Artificial Intelligence)-assisted diagnostic model that integrates multidimensional features. This study retrospectively collected CT and x-ray data from 612 patients with PI (398 benign and 214 ischemic cases) from three tertiary hospitals, and included an external validation set of 106 cases. Imaging analysis established a five-level PI-CT severity scoring system based on gas morphology, distribution, portal venous gas (PVG), intestinal wall enhancement, mesenteric edema, and ascites. The AI system adopted a two-level architecture: The first level used EfficientNet-B3 for rapid screening on x-ray films; the second level used 3D nnU-Net (No-new-Net) to segment intestinal wall gas, and then fused the data through a three-branch network (gas morphology, accompanying signs, and clinical metadata) via cross-attention to output the probability of ischemic PI. In the internal test set, the model achieved an AUC (Area Under the Curve) of 0.947 for ischemic PI (sensitivity 91.3%, specificity 93.6%), significantly outperforming senior radiologists (AUC = 0.876); the AUC on the external validation set was 0.931. SHapley Additive exPlanations analysis showed that PVG and blood lactate were the most important predictors. This two-tiered AI system can significantly improve the early identification of the causes of critical PI, providing a reliable method for intelligent diagnosis of emergency imaging.

title: Foundation models in radiology: Development, applications, and future impact.
abstract: Foundation models represent a major evolution in artificial intelligence, enabling models pretrained on large, diverse datasets to be adapted to a wide range of downstream tasks with substantially less task-specific training data. In radiology, advances in transformer architectures, self-supervised learning, and vision-language models have created new opportunities to integrate image and text understanding within versatile artificial intelligence systems. Potential applications span the radiology workflow and include image interpretation, automated report drafting and summarization, clinical decision support, information retrieval, and development of specialized task-specific models. Among these, AI-assisted report generation represents a particularly promising near-term application, although current performance supports a role as a drafting assistant rather than an autonomous replacement for radiologists. Important barriers to clinical adoption remain, including limitations in model performance, regulatory requirements, and the risk of automation bias. In the near term, foundation models may have their greatest impact by augmenting radiologists and accelerating the development of specialized artificial intelligence applications rather than replacing existing systems or physician expertise. This review describes the technological advances underlying foundation models, highlights their current and emerging applications in radiology, examines key risks and implementation challenges, and considers their potential impact on the future practice of radiology.

title: The impact of artificial intelligence on peer review in radiology journals.
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is rapidly transforming radiology research and is progressively influencing the scholarly publication process itself. Large language models (LLMs) are being increasingly used for manuscript writing. At the other end of the spectrum, AI can assist with manuscript screening, statistical and methodological assessment, language editing, reference checking, reviewer selection, and the generation of peer-review comments. LLMs have the potential to improve the efficiency of journal review by reducing repetitive tasks and helping reviewers identify reporting deficiencies. However, their integration also introduces substantial concerns regarding confidentiality, hallucination, bias, reproducibility, authorship, accountability, and manipulation of the peer-review process. In this article, the authors examine the potential benefits and limitations of AI-assisted peer review in radiology journals and propose a framework in which AI serves as a controlled decision-support tool rather than an autonomous reviewer. Human reviewers and editors should retain responsibility for scientific judgment, confidentiality, and final editorial decisions. This approach harnesses AI's efficiency while maintaining accountability.

title: Radiology-led 3D printing in adult cardiothoracic care: a narrative review and implementation roadmap.
abstract: Patient-specific three-dimensional (3D) printing can help plan selected cardiothoracic procedures, but print accuracy alone does not make a model useful. This narrative review combines appropriateness criteria, a structured update of comparative studies published since November 2019, implementation and quality literature, and U.S. regulatory and coding sources into a radiology-led roadmap for adult acquired cardiac, thoracic aortic, and thoracic care. For left atrial appendage occlusion, meta-analyses of small comparative studies associate printed models with fewer device-size disagreements and peri-device leaks. For transcatheter valve procedures the evidence is mostly feasibility and accuracy work, and for septal myectomy, thoracic aortic repair, and lung segmentectomy it is largely single-center and retrospective; the only randomized trial that kept digital reconstruction in both arms found no difference. Digital planning, including virtual reality and computational simulation, is therefore the comparator against which printing should be judged. The 10-step pathway runs from the clinical question and a documented print-or-no-print decision through imaging and model prescription, segmentation, anatomic validation, design approval, manufacture, verification and release, delivery, and outcome tracking. We map published accuracy data to verification targets, follow an illustrative case through every step, and set out why radiology should own the image-dependent steps, what that costs, and which alternative service models exist. Controls are scaled to three operational categories that are not regulatory device classes. Prospective comparisons with contemporary digital planning, reporting failures and denominators, are still needed.

title: Should the carbon footprint of imaging be considered to ensure an effective, sustainable supplementary breast screening strategy for women with dense breasts?
abstract: Breast density is an independent risk factor for breast cancer and reduces the sensitivity of mammography, increasing the chance of a missed breast cancer. Notifying women of their breast density aims to increase their awareness about their breast cancer risk and support discussions about supplemental screening (e.g. ultrasound or magnetic resonance imaging) with their healthcare providers. Although supplemental screening may improve cancer detection, it also brings challenges, including lack of international consensus on how best to manage screening in women with dense breasts. The implementation of breast density notification and supplemental screening will significantly impact global screening programs, and provides an opportunity to re-evaluate screening pathways, not only in terms of benefits and harms, but also environmental sustainability. In this perspective, we discuss the benefits and harms of supplemental screening for women with dense breasts, including the carbon footprint of screening, and considerations for clinicians, consumers and policymakers.

title: Clinical and behavioral delineation of cochlear implant non-users: a 20-year retrospective descriptive analysis.
abstract: Background Although cochlear implants (CIs) effectively restore hearing, device abandonment ('non-use') remains a critical challenge limiting long-term auditory rehabilitation. Aims/objectives This study aimed to evaluate the prevalence, clinical and radiological characteristics, and patient-reported reasons for CI non-use, comparing pre-lingually and post-lingually deafened individuals to inform long-term retention strategies. Material and methods We retrospectively reviewed 545 CI recipients implanted between 2002 and 2023 (excluding 24 patients lost to follow-up or with incomplete data). Clinical features, temporal bone CT, internal auditory canal MRI, and speech-language therapy records of 36 non-users were analyzed. Results Overall non-use rate was 6.6% (36/545), comprising 8.7% (25/287) in pre-lingual and 4.3% (11/258) in post-lingual recipients. Inner ear anomalies were identified in 11 pre-lingual non-users, including two with isolated cochlear nerve deficiency. Primary non-use reasons were sound maladaptation (48.0% pre-lingual vs. 36.4% post-lingual) and lack of subjective listening effect (48.0% vs. 18.2%). Post-lingual non-users presented distinct adult-specific psychosocial barriers (27.3%), including depression and cognitive decline. Conclusions and significance CI non-use is driven by distinct physiological, psychological, and socioeconomic factors depending on deafness onset. Delineating these onset-specific profiles provides essential guidance for tailored preoperative counseling and age-appropriate post-implantation monitoring to minimize long-term device abandonment.

title: Environmental burden of endoscopy-based gastric cancer screening in a national population-based program.
abstract: Objective Population-based endoscopic screening reduces gastric cancer mortality in high-incidence countries; however, its environmental impact is not well defined. This study quantified the carbon footprint of the Korean National Gastric Cancer Screening Program. Methods National screening data from 2014 to 2023 were obtained from the Korean Statistical Information Service, including annual participation, gastric cancer detection rates, and age-stratified data. Carbon emissions attributable to gastroscopy were estimated using published life cycle assessment data and applied to national screening volumes. Trends in the number needed to screen (NNS), the proportion of non-high-risk (NHR) individuals, and age-stratified carbon emissions were analyzed. Results Endoscopic participation increased to 60.3%, resulting in ∼8.04 million annual screening examinations. NNS was substantially higher in younger individuals (1,798 in 40-49 years vs. 147 in ≥80 years in 2023). During the same period, declining Helicobacter pylori prevalence and expansion of the NHR group, particularly among younger individuals, resulted in an increased proportion of screening conducted in lower-risk populations. Despite lower screening efficiency, younger age groups generated the greatest absolute carbon emissions, reaching 742,239 kg carbon dioxide equivalents (CO 2e ) by individuals aged 40-49 years, compared to 48,754 kg CO 2e in those aged ≥80 years in 2023. Overall, carbon emissions increased across all age groups over time. Conclusion Nationwide endoscopic screening for gastric cancer is associated with an increasing carbon footprint, particularly among younger populations. Integrating environmental considerations into future screening strategies may be necessary to balance clinical benefits with long-term healthcare sustainability.

title: Association of second-trimester maternal serum AFP with umbilical venous blood flow and placental morphometry: a prospective study.
abstract: Background Maternal serum alpha-fetoprotein and umbilical venous Doppler measurements may reflect different aspects of fetoplacental function, but their relationship during the second trimester remains unclear. This study aimed to evaluate associations between maternal serum alpha-fetoprotein multiples of the median (AFP MoM) and umbilical venous Doppler parameters, foetal weight percentile, and placental morphometry. Methods This prospective observational study included 104 singleton pregnancies examined at 16-22 weeks. Maternal blood sampling and ultrasound/Doppler assessment were performed on the same day. Associations were evaluated using Spearman correlations and partial Spearman correlations adjusted for gestational age. Exploratory comparisons between pregnancies with AFP <2.0 MoM and AFP ≥2.0 MoM were also adjusted for gestational age. The Benjamini-Hochberg procedure controlled the false discovery rate. Results AFP MoM was available for 103 pregnancies and was not associated with foetal weight percentile or umbilical venous Doppler parameters. A weak inverse association with placental length was observed after gestational-age adjustment (partial r = -0.229; nominal p = 0.021), but it did not remain significant after false discovery rate correction ( p = 0.193). In the exploratory analysis, the AFP ≥2.0 MoM group had a lower adjusted placental length (difference, -11.63 mm; 95% confidence interval, -21.10 to -2.17; nominal p = 0.017), but this difference was not significant after correction ( p = 0.149). Conclusion Maternal serum AFP MoM was not associated with contemporaneous umbilical venous Doppler parameters or foetal weight percentile. Findings involving placental length were weak and should be considered exploratory.

title: CosMxScope: scalable reconstruction and digital pathology integration of imaging-based CosMx spatial transcriptomics data.
abstract: Spatial transcriptomics technologies have transformed the capacity to quantify gene expression from human tissues, simultaneously capturing both the cell functional state and spatial organization at cellular and subcellular resolution. The CosMx Spatial Molecular Imager (SMI) is one of the leading platforms at single-cell spatial multi-modal omics profiling, capable of measuring thousands of RNA or protein targets at single-cell and subcellular resolution across whole slide sections. Exported data include field-of-view (FOV) image tiles, subcellular transcript coordinates, and cell segmentation polygons, outputs that are rich in spatial information but not directly compatible with widely used digital pathology tools. Here we present CosMxScope, a lightweight open-source Python framework designed for data exported from the CosMx Spatial Molecular Imager through the AtoMx platform, bridging CosMx spatial outputs with histopathology visualization environments. CosMxScope provides functions for stitching FOV image tiles into reconstructed whole-slide images, converting cell segmentation polygons and transcript coordinates into GeoJSON objects for downstream visualization and assessment within QuPath, and generating spatial visualization plots of cell types, transcript locations, and gene expression patterns. The framework is designed for practical use in translational research settings, enabling interactive exploration of spatial transcriptomic data alongside cell morphology. CosMxScope has been applied in multiple ongoing research projects involving CosMx profiling of human and mouse tissues, supporting pathology-based spatial analysis workflows. This open-source software is available at https://github.com/AivaraX-AI/CosMxScope.

title: Exoscope-assisted resection of spinal tumors: volumetric efficacy, safety and learning curve analysis in 47 consecutive cases.
abstract: Objective To evaluate the clinical outcomes, volumetric extent of resection, safety profile, and skill acquisition dynamics of 3D-4K digital exoscope-assisted spinal tumor resection. Methods A retrospective analytical single-center study was conducted on 47 consecutive patients undergoing exoscope-assisted resection across intramedullary (IM, n = 7), intradural extramedullary (IDEM, n = 34), and extradural (ED, n = 6) compartments. Extent of resection was determined via blinded postoperative subtraction MRI. Surgical skill acquisition was modeled using sequential Cumulative Sum (CUSUM) analysis of intraoperative blood loss. Results Mean age was 49.1 ± 17.3 years (63.8% female). Overall Gross Total Resection (GTR > 95%) was achieved in 85.1% ( n = 40/47), reaching 100% in IM lesions ( n = 7/7) and 82.4% in IDEM tumors ( n = 28/34, p = 0.567). Postoperative CSF fistula occurred in 6.4% ( n = 3/47), restricted exclusively to IDEM Schwannomas. Median operative time was 3.27 hours (IQR: 2.68-5.05; n = 32/47). Median hospital stay was 3.0 days (IQR: 3.0-5.0). At 6-month follow-up, paired evaluations demonstrated significant functional and pain improvements (mMs and ODI/NDI, p < 0.001). Sequential CUSUM analysis identified a structural break at case 28, marking the transition to technical mastery without blood loss inflation during early cases ( p = 0.553). Conclusions Resection of spinal tumors using the 3D-4K exoscope is safe, effective, and yields high volumetric resection rates. Skill acquisition follows a patient-safe learning curve, achieving technical proficiency at case 28.

title: Hyper-acute orbital edema and vision loss following palliative radiotherapy of the lacrimal gland.
abstract: Breast carcinoma is the most common primary malignancy to metastasize to the orbit. While mild delayed orbital edema is a recognized complication of orbital radiotherapy, hyper-acute severe edema resulting in transient vision loss is rare. A 48-year-old woman with metastatic invasive lobular breast carcinoma and left orbital involvement received a first-dose palliative radiation fraction of 8 Gy to the left orbit. Within 5 hours, she developed severe proptosis, chemosis, elevated intraocular pressure, and monocular vision loss. Computed tomography demonstrated proptosis of the left globe and optic nerve stretching. She received 8 mg of intravenous dexamethasone, and her vision rapidly recovered to baseline with the resolution of her acute compressive symptoms without any change in tumor-directed therapy. This case highlights the rare risk of hyper-acute post-radiation orbital edema within hours of radiotherapy and demonstrates that early, prompt medical management can successfully rescue compressive optic neuropathy.

title: High-grade malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumor of the ocular surface in a long-standing blind eye.
abstract: Malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumor (MPNST) is a rare and aggressive soft tissue sarcoma, exceptionally uncommon in the ocular region. We report the case of an 88-year-old man presenting with a rapidly growing exophytic mass on the ocular surface of a long-standing amaurotic eye. Imaging demonstrated a lesion confined to the ocular surface without intraorbital extension. Histopathology revealed a high-grade spindle cell neoplasm with complete loss of H3K27me3 expression and CDKN2A deletion, consistent with MPNST. Systemic staging showed no metastatic disease. The patient underwent enucleation, with histopathological examination confirming a tumor confined to the ocular surface without intraocular extension. Following multidisciplinary assessment, postoperative surveillance without adjuvant radiotherapy was selected. This case highlights an unusual ocular surface presentation of MPNST and underscores the importance of integrated histopathological and molecular assessment and individualized management.

title: A multicenter large-sample survey on adverse events of focused ultrasound ablation surgery for benign uterine diseases in clinical training and teaching hospitals.
abstract: Objective To evaluate the adverse events and complications associated with focused ultrasound ablation surgery(FUAS)for benign uterine diseases in teaching and training centers. Materials and methods From October 2010 to December 2023, 26,844 patients with benign uterine diseases were treated with FUAS and more than 2000 doctors had been trained in three teaching and training centers. Among the treated patients, 16,619 had uterine fibroids, 8732 had adenomyosis, 1154 had cesarean scar pregnancy, and 379 had placental accreta spectrum. According to the classification system of the Society of Interventional Radiology (SIR), these adverse events were classified as mild adverse event (no therapy or nominal therapy), moderate adverse event (moderate escalation of care, requiring substantial treatment), severe adverse event (marked escalation of care), Life-threatening or disabling event, and patient death or unexpected pregnancy abortion. Results Mild adverse effects occurred in 2,352 (8.75%) patients, moderate adverse events were seen in 147 (0.55%) patients, severe adverse events encountered in 50 (0.18%) patients. No life-threatening or disabling event, and patient death or unexpected pregnancy abortion occurred. The overall incidence rate of severe adverse events was 0.18% ( n = 50). From 2010 to 2023, the annual incidence rates of severe adverse events were 0%, 0.42%, 0%, 0%, 0.28%, 0.23%, 0.09%, 0.08%, 0.20%, 0.28%, 0.44%, 0.16%, 0.16%, and 0.10%, respectively. Conclusion Based on the results, we concluded that FUAS is a safe treatment for benign uterine diseases. The training course for trainee did not increase the risk of severe adverse events.

title: Long-term outcomes of LINAC single-dose versus fractionated stereotactic radiation for vestibular schwannoma.
abstract: Introduction Vestibular schwannomas (VS) are increasingly being managed with LINAC-based stereotactic radiosurgery (SRS) or fractionated stereotactic radiotherapy (fSRT). There is a paucity of long-term outcomes especially in relation to post-treatment volumetric tumour and pseudoprogression data. Methods 197 patients treated with LINAC-SRS ( n = 92) and LINAC-fSRT ( n = 105) between November 2003 and September 2019 were analysed. Tumour control was assessed volumetrically using MRI. The primary outcome was radiological VS control at last follow-up. The secondary outcomes were freedom from further intervention, serviceable hearing at last follow-up and incidence of new or worsened facial nerve palsy. Results Patients undergoing fSRT had larger pre-treatment tumour size (2.1 cm 3 vs 1.0, p = 0.008). At a median follow-up of 10.9 years, radiological control rates were 94% for SRS and 91% for fSRT (p = 0.41). Rates of freedom from further surgical or radiation intervention were 98% and 97%, respectively. SRS showed a larger median pseudoprogression (≈75%). Facial nerve palsy and sensation changes were low and comparable between the groups. Hydrocephalus occurred more frequently after fSRT (9.8% vs. 1.1%, p = 0.021). Conclusion LINAC-fSRT and LINAC-SRS are both associated with excellent long-term tumour control rates. Hydrocephalus was more common in patients after fSRT with the caveat these patients had a larger pre-treatment tumour volume.

title: Association of HIV infection with short-term major adverse cardiovascular events among Chinese patients with carotid atherosclerosis: a single-center retrospective cohort study.
abstract: Background People living with HIV (PLWH) suffer accelerated atherosclerotic injury, but real-world Chinese cohort data excluding patients with pre-existing cardiovascular and cerebrovascular diseases remain scarce regarding HIV-related incident major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE). This study aimed to explore the independent associations between HIV infection and 2-year incident MACE among Chinese patients with carotid atherosclerosis free of prior cardiovascular events, and identify correlated metabolic and renal factors. Methods A retrospective single-center cohort design was adopted. We enrolled patients with ultrasound-confirmed carotid atherosclerosis from January 2020 to June 2023, excluded individuals with prior coronary heart disease, ischemic stroke or transient ischemic attack, and conducted standardized 2-year follow-up for all eligible participants. Univariate statistical tests screened variables correlated with MACE; variables with univariate p < 0.05 plus core clinical confounders (age, sex, hypertension, diabetes) were incorporated into multivariate binary logistic regression to identify independent correlates of new-onset MACE. Results Patients with HIV infection showed significantly younger age compared with HIV-negative counterparts (63.55 ± 10.81 years vs 70.61 ± 9.75 years, p < 0.001). The cumulative 2-year occurrence rate of MACE was markedly higher in the HIV-positive group (40.4% versus 22.9%, p = 0.023). Multivariate regression analysis verified four independent risk markers for incident MACE: HIV seropositivity (OR = 2.24, 95%CI 1.19-4.22, p = 0.012), baseline active smoking (OR = 1.98, 95%CI 1.07-3.66, p = 0.028), reduced estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) (OR = 2.15, 95%CI 1.15-4.02, p = 0.017) and hyperuricemia (OR = 1.89, 95%CI 1.02-3.51, p = 0.043). Conclusion Chinese people living with HIV (PLWH) combined with carotid atherosclerosis develop atherosclerotic lesions at an earlier age and carry elevated short-term MACE risk. Integrated intervention strategies covering HIV viral control, smoking cessation, renal function protection and serum uric acid management can effectively improve cardiovascular long-term prognosis for this special population.

title: An MRI-based diagnostic model for identifying amyloid- and tau-positive status in patients with dementia.
abstract: Background The diagnosis and assessment of disease severity in Alzheimer's disease (AD) mainly rely on biomarkers derived from cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) analysis and positron emission tomography (PET) imaging. Limited accessibility of samples and high costs restrict their widespread application. In this study, dementia patients were classified into amyloid- and tau-positive (A + T+) and non-A + T + groups based on CSF biomarkers, with the aim of identifying differences in magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)-based brain structural and topological metrics between the groups and developing a diagnostic model. Methods A total of 31 patients in the A + T + group and 49 in the non-A + T + group were recruited. All participants exhibited clinical manifestations consistent with AD. All patients underwent clinical scale assessments, CSF testing, and brain MRI examinations. Results Compared to non-A + T + patients, A + T + patients had smaller caudate nucleus volumes and lower whole-brain network topological parameter λ values. There were no differences in cortical thickness, hippocampal volume, or amygdala volume between the two groups. The diagnostic model developed to differentiate A + T + from non-A + T + dementia patients, based on age, gender, disease duration, caudate/estimated total intracranial volume (eTIV), and λ, achieved an AUC of 0.817. Conclusions Combining clinical manifestations with MRI-based structural and topological parameters helps improve the diagnostic ability for A + T + dementia patients. Caudate/eTIV and λ may represent promising noninvasive candidate biomarkers for monitoring AD progression, although their utility requires validation in future longitudinal studies.

title: Association between pancreatic ectopic fat deposition and QCT-assessed bone mass status in patients with chronic kidney disease: a cross-sectional study.
abstract: Background Patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD) are at increased risk of bone abnormalities. Beyond disturbances in mineral metabolism, ectopic fat deposition may also be associated with skeletal abnormalities in CKD. However, the relationship between pancreatic fat and bone mass status remains unclear. This study aimed to evaluate the association between mean pancreatic fat fraction and quantitative computed tomography (QCT)-assessed bone mass status in patients with CKD. Methods This retrospective cross-sectional study included 327 patients with CKD. Vertebral volumetric bone mineral density was measured using QCT to classify bone mass status as normal bone mass, osteopenia, or osteoporosis. Mean pancreatic fat fraction was quantified from CT images. Ordinal logistic regression, restricted cubic spline (RCS), subgroup analyses, and sensitivity analyses were performed to evaluate its association with bone mass status. Results Mean pancreatic fat fraction was highest in patients with osteoporosis ( p < 0.001). In the fully adjusted model, each 5-percentage-point increase in mean pancreatic fat fraction was associated with higher odds of a more severe bone mass category (OR = 1.481, 95% CI: 1.152-1.905, p = 0.002). RCS analysis showed a significant overall association ( p = 0.009), with no evidence of nonlinearity ( p = 0.290). No statistically significant interactions were detected for sex, age, diabetes status, or CKD stage. Conclusion A higher mean pancreatic fat fraction was associated with more severe bone mass categories in patients with CKD after adjustment for the measured covariates. QCT-based pancreatic fat assessment may provide additional information on metabolic features associated with bone mass abnormalities in CKD.

RCS analysis showed a significant overall association (p = 0.009), with no evidence of nonlinearity (p = 0.290). No statistically significant interactions were detected for sex, age, diabetes status, or CKD stage.

Conclusion

A higher mean pancreatic fat fraction was associated with more severe bone mass categories in patients with CKD after adjustment for the measured covariates. QCT-based pancreatic fat assessment may provide additional information on metabolic features associated with bone mass abnormalities in CKD.

title: Diffusion MRI and Inflammation-Nutrition-Based Nomogram for Early Tumor Response to HAIC-Based Triple Therapy in Hepatocellular Carcinoma with Portal Vein Tumor Thrombus.
abstract: Purpose To develop and evaluate a pretreatment nomogram predicting early objective response to HAIC-based triple therapy in unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma with portal vein tumor thrombus. Methods This retrospective three-center study included 170 patients (training, 82; pooled external validation, 88). The nomogram incorporated ln(SII), prognostic nutritional index, and normalized diffusion-weighted imaging-to-apparent diffusion coefficient ratio. Evaluation included discrimination, calibration, decision curves, 500-bootstrap internal validation, SHAP interpretation, and survival stratification. Results Objective response occurred in 27/82 (32.9%) training patients and 30/88 (34.1%) external patients. The areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUCs) were 0.934 (95% CI, 0.879-0.989) and 0.924 (95% CI, 0.869-0.978); the optimism-corrected AUC was 0.917. At the training-derived probability cutoff of 0.1933, sensitivity was 92.6% (95% CI, 76.6-97.9%) and 90.0% (95% CI, 74.4-96.5%), respectively. External calibration showed a Brier score of 0.112 and a slope of 1.456. The model had higher AUCs than Child-Pugh class, ALBI grade, and the six-and-twelve category. Higher predicted response probability was associated with longer overall and progression-free survival in both cohorts (all log-rank p < 0.001). Conclusion The nomogram showed promising discrimination for early objective response in selected patients with HCC and PVTT receiving HAIC-based triple therapy.

title: Effect of Pupillary Dilation on Image Gradeability and Diagnostic Performance in AI-Based Diabetic Retinopathy Detection Among Older Adults - A Clinical Evaluation.
abstract: Purpose Artificial intelligence (AI) has demonstrated significant potential in detecting diabetic retinopathy (DR) from retinal images. However, image acquisition in older adults is often affected by constricted pupils and media opacity. This study evaluated the effect of pupillary dilation on retinal image gradeability and diagnostic yield in AI-assisted DR detection among older adults. Methods In this prospective study, adults aged ≥65 years were recruited from a tertiary eye hospital in India. Retinal images were captured using a clinically validated AI-integrated fundus camera (Optain Resolve OPTFC01, Optain Health, Melbourne, Australia) before and after pupillary dilation. The proportion of ungradable images, need for repeated imaging, and diagnostic yield of AI-based DR detection were compared between the two conditions. Results A total of 197 retinal images from 100 participants (mean (SD) age: 70 (4.78) years) were analysed. Ungradable images significantly decreased from 33% without dilation to 10% after dilation ( p < 0.0001). The proportion requiring repeated imaging reduced from 70.6% to 33.5% ( p < 0.0001). Before dilation, AI-based DR detection showed a sensitivity of 87.0% (95% CI: 73.7-95.1), a specificity of 88.7% (95% CI: 77.0-95.7), and an AUC of 0.878 (95% CI: 0.813-0.944). Corresponding values after dilation were 86.7%, 86.1%, and 0.864, respectively ( p = 0.729). Conclusion Our findings indicate that pupillary dilation significantly improved retinal image gradeability and reduced repeated imaging in older adults. Although diagnostic accuracy metrics remained stable, the higher proportion of gradable images enabled more patients to benefit from AI-assisted DR detection. Selective dilation may therefore be useful when non-mydriatic imaging yields ungradable results, particularly in elderly populations.
